【3】**Incidence.Rare.**

【4】**Ultrasound diagnosis. On the three-vessel and trachea view： right aortic arch： aortic arch on the right of the trachea； double aortic arch：“N” shape with bifurcation of the aortic arch in front of the trachea； vascular ring： abnormal retrotracheal vessel.**

【5】**Risk of chromosomal anomalies.Relatively high for the right aortic arch with aberrant subclavian artery and for the double aortic arch (22q11 microdeletion).**

【6】**Risk of nonchromosomal syndromes. Relatively low.**

【7】**Outcome. Excellent in the case of isolated anomalies； if associated with major CHDs， final outcome will depend on the severity of these.**

【8】Definition Aortic arch anomalies comprise a variety of congenital abnormalities of the position， branching pattern， or both of the aortic arch. They result from aberrant development of one or more components of the embryonic pharyngeal arch system. These anoma-lies can be divided into those that cause a vascular ring around the trachea and esophagus， usually determining compression of both structures， and those that do not.

【9】Anatomy. The left or right position of the aortic arch is defined in relation to the mainstem bronchus， which is crossed by the descending thoracic aorta， and does not refer to the side of the midline on which the aorta descends. In the left aortic arch， the descending tho-racic aorta crosses over the left mainstem bronchus and descends left to the midline along the spine. Three vessels arise from the aortic arch： first the innominate artery branching into the right carotid and right subcla-vian arteries； second， the left carotid artery； and， third， the left subclavian artery. Usually， the first aortic arch vessel gives rise to the carotid artery， which is oppo-site to the side of the aortic arch (i.e.， the right carotid artery in the left aortic arch and the left carotid artery in the right aortic arch (RAA)). The ductus arteriosus joints the aorta distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. Normally， the ductus arteriosus can left-sided， bilateral， or right-sided. A RAA occurs in about 1 in1000 of the general population.

【10】The most common types of RAA branching are as follows：

【11】·1Mirror-image branching (left innominate artery， right carotid artery， and right subclavian artery)；

【12】Retroesophageal left (aberrant) subclavian artery with a normal caliber：

【13】Retroesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell.

【14】In the first case (mirror branching)， the RAA is asso-ciated with major CHD (especially TOF) nearly 90%of the time. Usually， in this case the ductus arteriosus courses to the right of the trachea， and， therefore， there is no vascular ring. In fact， the presence or absence of a vascular ring in the setting of a RAA depends on the branching of the brachiocephalic vessels and the loca-tion of the ductus arteriosus： if these are located on the left of the trachea， this will create the retrotracheal sling； and， vice versa， if the ductus arteriosus courses to the right of the trachea， together with the right-sided aortic arch， then there is no vascular ring.

In the other two cases (i.e.， with a retroesophageal W left \[aberrant\] subclavian artery with or without a ret-roesophageal diverticulum of Kommerell)， the RAA is associated with a left-sided ductus arteriosus. In this condition， the trachea is positioned between the transverse aortic arch and the ductus arteriosus， which|删除0换行|represent the vascular ring (or retrotracheal sling). Commonly， this condition is associated with an aber-rant course of the left subclavian artery， commonly from a retroesophageal diverticulum situated at the iunction of the ductus arteriosus with the descending aorta， called a Kommerel diverticulum. This branching pattern is not usually associated with a major cardiac malformation. The tighter vascular ring is represented by the double aortic arch. In this case， both right and left aortic arches are present： the ascending aorta splits into two limbs， which encircle the trachea and esoph-agus to join at the level of the descending aorta. As to the size of the two aortic arches， the most common arrangement is with hypoplasia of the left arch， but cases with hypoplasia of the right arch or normal size of both have also been described. This anomaly is commonly associated with a patent ductus arteriosus.

【16】Ultrasound diagnosis. As described here， the aortic arch _can be examinated on the three-vessel and trachea view_  通用删除6(英):<u>\[50\]</u>. A RAA is diagnosed when the trans-verse aortic arch is located to the right of the trachea on this axial view of the mediastinum. If the ductus arteriosus is left-sided， the RAA and the left ductal arch form a U-shaped configuration with the trachea located between them 通用删除6(英):<u>\[47-49\]</u>. In addition， any branch coursing behind the trachea (e.g.， a right aberrant subclavian artery) should be considered as an abnormal aberrant branch . Color Doppler is extremely useful to trace the course of the abnormal vessels in the upper mediastinum . Spectral Doppler may be used to differentiate the innom-inate vein from arterial vessels (e.g.， aberrant subclavian arteries) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[50\]</u> . Four-dimensional echocardiography permits an easier diagnosis of all aor-tic arch anomalies. B-flow and， to a lesser extent， inver-sion mode are the renderings of choice.

【17】_Association with other malformations. RAA with_ mirror-image branching is often associated with other complex cardiac anomalies (TOF and CATs). VSD is the cardiac anomaly most commonly associated with a vascular ring.

【18】Risk of chromosomal anomalies. This is relatively high. Vascular ring and isolated RAA can be associated with the 22q11 microdeletion 通用删除6(英):<u>\[50\]</u>.

【19】**Risk of nonchromosomal syndromes. This is low in cases of vascular ring.**

【20】Obstetric management. For isolated RAA， the option of fetal karyotyping with a FISH analysis for the 22q11microdeletion should be discussed with the patient.

【21】通用删除16(英):<u>**Figure 5.52Aortic arch anomalies： three-vessel and trachea view. (a) In the normal spatial relationships， the trachea (arrow) is located on the right of the aortic arch. (b) In a right aortic arch， the trachea (a ITICrrow) is located between the aortic and ductal arches. Sometimes， as in this case， a retrotracheal vessel (sling) can be identified. (c) In a double aortic arch， the arches feature an upside-down “N，" with the oblique bar of the “N" (2； 1 represents the first arch) representing the second arch. The trachea (arrow) in this case is located between the two aortic arches， although several spatial arrangements are possible. (d) In some cases， the aortic arch is normally positioned on the left of the trachea (arrow)， but the neck vessels can have an abnormal origin and course. In this case， there was an aberrant retrotracheal right subclavian artery (arrowhead). See this chapter’s text for details. Ao： aortic arch； Pa： pulmonary artery and ductus arteriosus.**</u>

Prognosis， survival， and quality of life. Vascular rings encircle the trachea and the esophagus， which candetermine symptomatic compression of both CC structures， especially in cases of double aortic arch. Compression of the trachea causesupper airway obstruction that impairs inspiratory and， to a lesser degree， expiratory airflo . The extent of respiratory impairment depends upon the severity of compression，|删除0换行|which can vary considerably. In addition to the air-way symptoms， patients may experience swallowing problems related to the esophageal compression. The prognosis of patients with vascular rings depends on several factors， including the severity of tracheal and esophageal compression and the association with other cardiac and extracardiac anomalies.

【23】**TETr ALo Gy o F FALLoT**

【24】**Definition TOF is a cardiac malformation character-ized by the following：**

【25】Subaortic VSD caused by malalignment between the infundibular and the trabecular septum；

【26】An aorta overriding the VSD；

【27】Obstruction of varying severity of the right outflow tract：

【28】Consequent hypertrophy of the right ventricle (after birth).

【29】Its incidence reaches 9%-11% after birth， but due to the prevalence of complex cardiac anomalies， its inci-dence in utero is reduced to about 3%.

Anatomy. The extent of the anatomic obstruction to the right outflow tract is determined by the degree of devia-tion of the infundibular septum， the hypertrophy of the septum and anterior wall of the right ventricle， and the association of pulmonary valvular stenosis. In the fetus， because of the frequent absence of pulmonary stenosis|删除0换行|and the presence of physiologic shunts， the tetralogy often becomes a di-or trilogy， with the right ventricular hypertrophy being absent and the pulmonary stenosis present only in the more important cases and/or devel-oping late in gestation. Although the TOF spectrum comprises numerous variants and subtypes， TOF with an absent pulmonary valve， which is characterized by severe dilation of the pulmonary trunk and branches due to severe stenosis and the insufficiency of the func-tionally absent pulmonary valve， certainly represents a well-known entity with an unfavorable prognosis， which needs to be addressed separately .

【31】Ultrasound diagnosis. As for most conotruncal anom-alies， the four-chamber view is unremarkable， unless anomalies of the atrioventricular plane are associated. Only in TOF with absent pulmonary valve can the four-chamber view be abnormal due to the presence of cardiomegaly 通用删除6(英):<u>\[51\]</u>. Classic TOF is diagnosed on the _long-axis views. On the long axis of the left ventricle，_ a malalignment VSD with an overriding aorta can be seen . Sweeping further cephalad from this view， on the right outflow tract view， the smaller pulmonary artery can be detected . The pulmonary artery may have a diameter within the nor-mal range， but the aorta-pulmonary artery diameter ratio will be abnormal. As mentioned here， the hyper-trophy of the right ventricle is absent， whereas the infun-dibular stenosis is not a constant finding in the second trimester. Color Doppler can be used to demonstrate flow through the VSD toward the aorta  from both left and right ventricles and flo through the smaller pulmonary outflow tract and arterial duciCtt. IInn utero， it is unusual to detect pronounced acceler- ation of blood across the right outflow tract， even in the presence of an obvious reduction of the vessel size， due to the presence of the usually large shunt represented by the malalignment VSD. Moreover， stenosis is frequently absent at the time of diagnosis in the second trimester but it becomes evident later on in gestation； in a few cases， a narrow pulmonary outflow may progress to atresia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[52\]</u>. This is why serial US monitoring is important in order to demonstrate antegrade flow through the pulmonary artery late in gestation to exclude the potential need for prostaglandin therapy after birth. Spectral Doppler is of limited value， as is 4D echocardiography， even though there is recent evidence that a high peak systolic velocity pe：of the pulmonary trunk may predict the need for early intervention 通用删除6(英):<u>\[53\]</u>. The latter may be of help if anomalies of the aortic arch are associated.

**_Differential diagnosis_ s _._ . AsSalready mentioned，111utero TOF cannot be differentiated from an isolated|删除0换行|malalignment VSD if evident pulmonary stenosis is absent. Therefore， in the absence of pulmonary outflow obstruction， it is always necessary to consider the possi-ble evolution from malalignment VSD in TOF. Another important concept is that the degree of aortic overrid-ing is variable and cannot be fully appreciated in utero. Therefore， when the aorta emerges about 50% from the right ventricle， differentiation of TOF from a Fallot-like DORV can be difficult the two being distinguished only by the degree of aortic overriding. Hence， if aortic overriding is found， the right outflow tract should be evaluated： if a small pulmonary artery is connected to the right ventri-cle， the diagnosis is TOF； if this is atretic， it is PAVSD； and if the pulmonary artery originates from the single emerging vessel， it is CAT .

Postnatal treatment. The treatment of this defect is sur-gical in all cases. However， the type of approach will depend on different anatomic features that may be ascertained only after birth. These include the degree of pulmonary trunk and branch stenosis， the presence of multiple VSDs， and the presence of coronary anomalies. All of these features have an impact on the type of treat-ment. In most cases， definitive surgical correction will be performed at three-six months of age， depending on the orientation of the reference cardiosurgical center， with a surgical mortality rate of less than 2.5%. The surgical approach includes removal of the outflow obstruction(infundibulectomy)， together with closure of the VSD with a patch and， if necessary， pulmonary valvulotomy. However， if pulmonary outflow obstruction is signifi-cant， an early intervention is needed in order to ensure an adequate blood flow to the lungs and， consequently，|删除0换行|an acceptable oxygen saturation. This is obtained with a palliative aortopulmonary shunting procedure， the modified Blalock-Taussig operation. This consists of the interposition of a Gore-Tex conduct between the left subclavian artery and the left pulmonary artery.

【42】Prognosis， treatment， and quality of life. The overall prognosis will depend on several factors， including karyotype， associated extracardiac malformations， and cardiac anatomy. With regard to survival， case series of patients with isolated TOF report long-term survival rates as high as 80%-90%.The variant with an absent pulmonary valve has significantly lower survival rates and will be discussed in the “Absent Pulmonary Valve Syndrome” section. In conclusion， if no unfavor-able prognostic factors are found in utero and， above all， after birth， TOF is an easily correctable heart defect with excellent survival and good quality of life.

【77】开头批量删除-1:<u>Chapters of the book are divided into global presentations that should be familiar to neurologists and other healthcare providers. There are two chapters that concentrate on sensory impairment and pain， and an initial chapter devoted to the interpretation of diagnos-tic testing.</u>

【89】开头批量删除-1:<u>The field of neuromuscular medicine has grown considerably even since l graduated from fellowship just a few years ago， with signifi-cant advances in diagnostic testing and treatment having emerged. Laboratories around the world are working diligently to determine the causes of and treatments for these and many other neurologic disorders. In this context， it is now more important than ever to make firm and accurate diagnoses in our patients.</u>

【95】开头批量删除-1:<u>The evaluation of patients with neuromuscular diseases usually requires a comprehensive approach that utilizes laboratory， elec-trodiagnostic， and sometimes histopathologic testing. However， the process starts with a detailed history and physical examination that guides localization， differential diagnosis， and test selection. 【96】开头批量删除-1:<u>Hallmark but nonspecific clinical features include symmetric proximal weakness in myopathy with associated difficulty perform-ing tasks such as combing hair， rising from a chair， and climbing stairs. Myalgias and muscle cramps can be present. In some myop-athies， there are accompanying bulbar and ocular symptoms such as ptosis， dysphagia， and dysarthria. Patients with neuromuscular transmission disorders， such as myasthenia gravis (MG)， may com-plain of fatigable weakness， ptosis， diplopia， dysarthria， dysphagia， and shortness of breath. Sensorimotor neuropathies usually present with sensory symptoms such as numbness and paresthesias， along with distal weakness and reflex loss. Hereditary neuropathies are not typically associated with pain and have a slowly progressive course. Patients with motor neuronopathies such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) present with asymmetric weakness， bulbar symptoms， and fasciculations. There is considerable overlap of many of these signs and symptoms among disorders of the motor unit.</u>

【99】**Serum Creatine Kinase**

【100】Neurologists are frequently consulted to evaluate elevated creatine kinase (CK) levels， regardless of whether there are accompanying symptoms of weakness.

【101】The MM isozyme of serum CK is predominantly produced by skele-tal muscle， and serum CK levels reflect muscle membraneintegrity.

【102】CK is located in myofibrils and is also present in mitochondria. It plays a role in energy metabolism by catalyzing creatine and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) to phosphocreatine and adenosine diphosphate(ADP). CK levels become elevated if there is a muscle membrane leak or muscle necrosis.

【103】__ The normal range depends on the individual's muscle mass， race， sex， and activity levels.

【104】Vigorous exercise is associated with elevated CK levels， and it is important for the patient to stop exercising 5-7 days before CK levels are checked.

【105】CK measurement is one of the most useful tests in neuromuscular disease， especially when myopathy is in the differential diagnosis. However， CK elevation is not specific to myopathy. Some neurogenic disorders， exercise， and trauma are among the conditions that ele-vate CK. A list of such processes is found in Table 1.1， along with the usual range of CK values. Additional descriptions of metabolic myop-athies are found in the next subsection. Also， keep in mind that the CK level may be elevated in cardiac disease， but the MB fraction is most dramatically affected. Electrodiagnostic testing， muscle biopsy， and genetic testing may be considered for further evaluations follow-ing identification of an elevated CK (discussed later in the chapter).

【106】Aldolase，which is found in the liver as well as muscle， is elevated in most conditions in which the CK is elevated. An abnormally high level of aldolase may be seen in some inflammatory disor-ders affecting fascia in which the CK level is normal.

【107】With regard to myopathy， other potentially useful laboratory testing is listed in Table 1.2.

The diagnosis of CEL requires the exclusion of secondary eosinophilia in a number of neoplastic disorders， such as peripheral T-cell disorders， Hodgkin lymphoma (HL)， systemic mastocytosis(SM)， acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)， other chronic MPNs \[chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML)， polycythe-mia vera (PV)， essential thrombocythemia (ET)， primary myelofibrosis (PMF】.

【7】**MYELOID AND LYMPHOID NEOPLASMS WITH EOSINOPHILIA AND ABNORMALITIES _OF PDGFRA， PDGFRB， OR FGFR1_**

【8】**Myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and abnor-malities of PDGFRA， PDGFRB， or FGFRI constitute three specific disease groups， which can present as a chronic MPN or less often as a lymphoid neoplasm. The PDGFRA-related disorders present usually as CEL with prominent involve-ment of the mast cell lineage and sometimes of the neutro-philic lineage， less often as acute myeloid leukemia (AML) or T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (in both instances with accompa-nying eosinophilia). In the case of PDGFRB-related disease， the features of the MPN are more variable but are often those of CMML with eosinophilia with or without mast cell prolif-eration. In the case of FGFRI-related disease， a lymphoma-tous presentation is common， particularly T-lymphoblastic lymphoma with accompanying eosinophilia. Other patients have CEL， precursor B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma or AML. The disorders with either PDGFRA or PDGFRB are responsive to imatinib.**

【9】**MYELOID AND LYMPHOID NEOPLASMS WITH PDGFRA REARRANGEMENT (SYNONYMS： MYELOPROLIFERATIVE VARIANT OF THE HYPEREOSINOPHILIC SYNDROME； _CEL WITH FIP1L1-PDGFRA_**

【10】The most common MPNassociated with PDGFRA rearrange-ment is that associated with FIPILI-PDGFRA formed as a result of a cryptic deletion at 4q12 . Presentation is generally as CEL but can be as AML， T-lymphoblastic lymphoma， or both. Acute transformation can follow pre-sentation as CEL. The eosinophil count is almost always1.5×10/L or above. There is no Philadelphia chromosome or BCR-ABL fusion. The blood and BM are always involved. Tissue infiltration by eosinophils leads to tissue damage(most often the heart， lung， central nervous system， skin， and

通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 31.5 FISH analysis showing PDGFRA rearrangement. Green represents SCFD2； orange represents LNX； aqua represents _PDGFRA._**</u>|删除换行|gastrointestinal tract). The spleen is enlarged in a majority of cases. Serum tryptase is often increased and serum vitamin B， level is markedly elevated. FIPILI-PDGFRA-associated CEL is imatinib responsive.

【12】**Morphology**

【13】Blood smear shows marked eosinophilia with predominance of mature forms and occasional eosinophil myelocytes or promyelocytes. Only rare patients have blasts in the blood. The BM is hypercellular with markedly increased eosino-phils and precursors. Mast cells are often increased (usually CD2-/CD25\*) and may be indistinguishable from SM based on the morphology alone.

【14】**Cytogenetics/FISH and Molecular Studies**

【15】Usually， cytogenetic analysis is normal， with FIPILI-PDGFRA fusion gene resulting from cryptic del(4)(q12). Occasionally， there is a chromosomal rearrangement with a 4q12 breakpoint such as t(1；4) or t(4；10). In other patients， unrelated cytogenetic abnormality， such as trisomy 8， may be seen. The fusion gene can be detected by reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) or fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) studies using a probe for CHIC2 gene， which is uniformly deleted， or using a break-apart probe that encompasses FIPIL I _and PDGFRA._

【16】**MYELOID NEOPLASMS WITH PDGFRB REARRANGEMENT \[SYNONYM： CMML WITH EOSINOPHILIA ASSOCIATED WITH T(5；12)\]**

【17】参考段删除-1:<u>There is a distinctive group of myeloid neoplasms associated with rearrangement of PDGFRB at 5q31. Most often there is t(5；12)(q31-33； p12) with formation of an ETV6-PDGFRB fusion gene， but some rare variants may occur. The hemato-logical neoplasms include CMML with eosinophilia， CEL，</u>

【18】MPN with eosinophilia， or chronic basophilic leukemia. Cytogenetic analysis usually shows t(5；12). Variant translo-cations include t(1；3；5)， t(1；5)， t(3；5)， t(5；7)， t(5；10)， t(5；14)， t(5；15)， t(5；16)， and t(5；17).

【19】**8P11 MYELOPROLIFERATIVE SYNDROME**

【20】Several recurrent translocations that involve chromosome band 8pl1 have been described in myeloid malignancies. These translocations target FGFRI gene at 8pl1 with dif-ferent gene partners (e.g.， ZNF198， CEPIIO， FOP， TIFI， and BCR) resulting in constitutive activation of the tyrosine kinase activity contained within FGFRI. The 8p11 myelo-proliferative syndrome (EMS) also known as the stem cell leukemia/lymphoma syndrome or “myeloid and lymphoid neoplasms with FGFRI abnormalities”(WHO classification) is characterized by (1) an MPN associated with eosinophilia；(2) lymphadenopathy， usually involved by T-lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia； (3) frequent progression into AML； and (4) reciprocal translocations involving chromosome 8p1 1通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，6-14\]</u>. EMS shows a male predominance， with young to adult patients being the most often affected， although EMS can occur at any age (3-84 years； median 44 years). The symptoms include fatigue (35%)， night sweats (28%)， weight loss (18%)， or fever (13%) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>.

【21】Onset of the EMS is acute without a prior history of cyto-toxic therapy. The majority of patients have leukocytosis(median 46 ×10°/L； range 3.8-400) with a leukemoid reac-tion， circulating blasts (55% of cases)， eosinophilia (79%)， and/or monocytosis (37%) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>. The BM is usually hyper-cellular with myeloid hyperplasia and eosinophilia (71% of cases) and its morphologic features overlapping between MPN (with eosinophilia and/or mastocytosis)， myelodys-plastic syndrome (MDS)， and acute leukemia. In a series reported by Jackson et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>， 66% of cases had blast counts in the normal range， 18% had between 6% and 19%， and 16% had ≥20% blasts (usually myeloid or mixed pheno-type lineage). In the lymph node， the majority of cases show T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (79%) and the remaining cases show myeloid sarcoma (21%) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15-17\]</u>.

【22】**The most commonly observed translocation of EMS is t(8；13)通用删除11(英):<u>(p11；q12)</u>， which results in the expression of a chi-meric ZNF198-FGFRI tyrosine kinase 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，11，18\]</u>. FGFRI on chromosome 8p11 has two or three immunoglobulin-like domains， a transmembrane domain， and an intracellular domain with tyrosine kinase activity. The immunoglobulin-like domains are lost in the translocation t(8；13). ZNF198on chromosome13q12 haIsSfive zinc finger (ZNF) domains， a proline-rich domain， and a nuclear localiza-tion domain. Other translocations include t(8；22)通用删除11(英):<u>(p11；q11)</u>(BCR-FGFRI)， t(8；9)通用删除11(英):<u>(p11；q33)</u>， t(6；8)(q27；p11)， and t(8；16)通用删除11(英):<u>(p11；p13)</u>通用删除6(英):<u>\[9-11，19\]</u>.**

【23】EMS may occur as t(8；13)-positive biphenotypic malignancy involving the lymph nodes or extranodal sites， which is char-acterized by eosinophils， prominent high endothelial venules， and sheets of T lymphoblasts surrounded by larger cells with myeloid phenotype (which may also express CD3) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[20\]</u>.

【24】EMS is an aggressive disease with a high rate of progres-sion into AML (0 days to 24 months； mean 4.2 months) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13\]</u>. Disease progression is often associated with chromosome21 abnormalities (+21)， numerous marker chromosomes， and trisomy of chromosome 8， 9， 12， or 19， deletions of chromosome 9， and complex karyotype (more than three abnormalities). Currently， only allogeneic stem cell trans-plantation appears to be effective in eradicating or suppress-ing the malignant clone.

【25】**Differential Diagnosis**

【26】**The differential diagnosis includes AML， MDS， MPN (CML， other)， CMML， SM， and CEL.**

【27】**CHRONIC BASOPHILIC LEUKEMIA**

【28】Chronic basophilic leukemia is very rare and poorly understood MPN that is characterized by prominent chronic basophilia in the absence of the Philadelphia chromosome 通用删除6(英):<u>\[21\]</u>. BM exami-nation shows trilineage hyperplasia with basophilia and eosin-ophilia， megakaryocytic hyperplasia with atypia， but without megakaryocyte clustering. Atypical mast cells can be present in the subset of patients. It may be aggressive with the potential to transform into acute leukemia. The differential diagnosis includes CML in accelerated or blast phase with basophilia.

【29】**MASTOCYTOSIS**

【30】Mastocytosis is a heterogeneous group of BM-derived dis-orders characterized by proliferation of the clonally trans-formed mast cells， often associated with somatic activating point mutations within KIT， and a broad spectrum of clini-cal and morphologic features ranging from a self-limiting benign disorder (i.e.， juvenile cutaneous mastocytosis or urticaria pigmentosa) to highly aggressive neoplasms such as mast cell leukemia 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，22-33\]</u>. The symptoms observed in mastocytosis are related to the spontaneous or triggered release of mast cell mediators or due to consequences of pathological accumulation of mast S i1n tissues. Basically， mastocytosis can be divided into two main sub-types： cutaneous mastocytosis and SM mainly involving the BM. The WHO has specified criteria for classification of mastocytosis (SM) into seven major subtypes ： cutaneous mastocytosis， indolent SM， SM with an associated clonal hematological nonmast cell disorder， aggressive SM， mast cell leukemia， mast cell sarcoma， and extracutaneous mastocytoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，24，29，30，34\]</u>. Cutaneous mastocytosis can be divided into four different clinical variants： urticaria pigmentosa， solitary mastocytoma， dif-fuse cutaneous mastocytosis， and telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans 通用删除6(英):<u>\[35\]</u>.

【31】Skin findings are often accompanied by symptoms sec-ondary to mast cell release of mediators. These symptoms can be both localized to the skin lesion and systemic because of the release of mediators into the bloodstream. The major-ity of pediatric cases of cutaneous mastocytosis show a good

Findings in patients with SM include anemia， leukocytosis， eosinophilia， thrombocytopenia， and sple-nomegaly. SM variants can be further subclassified by the presence of clinicopathological criteria referred to as“B”findings (>30% mast cells in the BM and/or serum tryptase levels >200 ng/mL； increased marrow cellularity/dysplasia without meeting the criteria for another myeloid neoplasm； or enlargement of the liver， spleen， or lymph nodes with-out evidence of organ damage) and“C"criteria (evidence of organ damage such as abnormal liver function and/or ascites， hypersplenism， cytopenias， large osteolytic lesions/fractures， and malabsorption with weight loss) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，34，36，37\]</u>. Mast cell leukemia is an extremely rare subtype of mas-tocytosis with a leukemic spread of mast cells and a rapid progression of disease. The criteria for SM are presented in Table 31.3.**

【41】Myeloid neoplasms associated with SM include MDS， MPNs， CMML， eosinophilic disorders， and AML. Lymphoid neoplasms are much less common. In a series of SMs asso-ciated with clonal h1ematological nonmast cell disorder(n= 138 cases) reported by Pardanani et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[38\]</u>， 123 (89%) had an associated myeloid neoplasm and the remaining patients had lymphoma (n=7)， myeloma (n =5)， chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL； n = 2)， and primary amyloi-dosis (n = 1). Myeloid neoplasms included MPN \[55 cases， including 30 MPN， unclassifiable (MPN-U)， 2 PV， 15 CEL，6 ET， and 2 PMF\]， CMML (36 cases)， MDS (28 cases)， and AML (2 cases).

【42】**MORPHOLOGY**

【43】**Mastocytosis is a morphologic diagnosis and should not be diagnosed on the basis of clinical findings alone. Majority of patients with mastocytosis have evidence of skin involve-ment. The BM is involved in SM. Other sites include the spleen， lymph nodes， liver， and gastrointestinal tract. Normal mast cells are typically round and mononuclear with prominent metachromatic granules in the cytoplasm. Mast cel1l1progenitors(ungranulated，Ltryptase-positive blasts， metachromatic， blasts， and promastocytes)are rarely seen. In the mastocytosis， mast cells may be round to polygonal with prominent cytoplasmic granules， but atypical forms， including spindle cells， multilobed cells，**

【45】**Criteria for SM**

【50】**1\. In biopsy sections of the BM or other extracutaneous organs，>25%of the mast cells in the infiltrate are spindle shaped or have atypical mnorphology or， of all mast cells in BM aspirate smears，>25% are ininature or atypical.**

【55】and metachromatically granulated blast-like cells， may be present . Systemic and more aggressive vari-ants of mast cell disease more often display atypical cyto-morphologic features. A BM core biopsy shows multiple， well-demarcated foci of mast cells within a fibrohistiocytic matrix， with a tendency to perivascular and/or paratrabec-ular locations . Mast cells are accompanied by lymphocytes， histiocytes， eosinophils， and fibroblasts. In the lymph node involved by SM ， mast cells may form inconspicuous clusters or a prominent infiltrate replacing normal elements. Scattered mast cells are often seen in the lymph node involved by other malignancies， for example， classical HL， or the BM involved by lympho-plasmacytic lymphoma (LPL). SM may be associated with other hematopoietic neoplasms， such as acute leukemia， MDS ， malignant lymphoma， or other MPNs.

【56】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【57】Use of antibodies against tryptase， CD117， and CD25 is rec-ommended in every suspected case. Because most cases of SM show a very low degree of infiltration of the BM， mast cell tryptase and anti-CD117 are of major importance for screening and quantification of mast cells， in particular to detect even small compact infiltrates as the only major diag-nostic criterion for mastocytosis. Expression of CD25 on mast cells is defined as a minor diagnostic criterion and is usually seen only in mastocytosis  and not in reactive states of mast cell hyperplasia. Immunophenotypic studies of neoplastic mast cells reveal expression of CD2， CD25， CD43， CD45， CD68， CD117， and mast cell tryptase. Normal (benign) mast cells lack the expression of CD2 and

【60】CD25.CD30 expression by mast cells is usually associated with aggressive SM or mast cell leukemia， but rarely may be seen in indolent conditions 通用删除6(英):<u>\[33，39\]</u>. On flow cytometric analysis， mast cells appear as brightly CD117+ cells with increased side scatter .

【61】**CYTOGENETICS AND MOLECULAR FINDINGS**

【62】With conventional cytogenetics， ~35%-40% of the patients have chromosomally abnormal clones in BM cells including which are similar to those observed in other hematological neoplasms 通用删除6(英):<u>\[40，41\]</u>. The following chromosomal abnormalities

Detection of codon 816 KIT mutation is a minor diagnostic criterion of SM 通用删除6(英):<u>\[34\]</u>. Demonstration of one minor criterion(KIT D816V mutation) in the presence of major criterion(presence of multifocal mast cell clusters of ≥15 cells in the BM biopsy) is required for the diagnosis of SM. Mast cell leukemia  is an unusual form of aggressive SM accounting for <1% of all mastocytoses通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，32，45-47\]</u>. It may appear de novo or secondary to previous mastocytosis. Diagnosis is based on the presence of ≥20%atypical mast cells in the marrow or ≥10% in the blood； however， an aleukemic variant is frequently encountered in which the number of circulating mast cells is <10% 通用删除6(英):<u>\[45\]</u>. Mast cells are usually poorly differentiated with nucleoli，|删除0换行|fine chromatin， and bilobed nuclei， and morphologically resemble other immature mononuclear cells. They are posi-tive for CD45 and usually CD117， although the expression of CD117 may be dimmer than in SM. Some cases may also express CD30. 【1】Atherosclerosis. Atherosclerosis is the disease process often called arteriosclerosis or hardening of the arteries. It is a progressive process that may begin in childhood. It can occur in any artery in the body， but it is most common in medium-sized arteries such as those of the heart， brain， kidneys， and legs. Starting in childhood， the arteries begin to fill with a fatty substance， or lipids such as triglycerides and cholesterol， which then calcify or harden .

【2】This filler， called plaque， is made up of fats， calcium， and fibrous scar tissue and lines the usually supple arterial walls， progressively narrowing the arteries. These arteries carry blood rich in oxygen to the myocardium (middle layer of the heart consisting of the heart muscle)， but the atheroscle-rotic process leads to ischemia and to necrosis of the heart muscle. Necrotic tissue gradually forms a scar， but before scar formation， the weakened area is susceptible to aneurysm development.

【3】When fully developed， plaque can cause bleeding， clot for-mation， and distortion or rupture of a blood vessel . Heart attacks and strokes are the most sudden and often fatal signs of the disease.

【4】Thrombus. When plaque builds up on the artery walls， the blood flow is slowed and a clot (thrombus) may form on the plaque. When a vessel becomes blocked by a clot， it is

Atherosclerosis begins with an injury to the endothelial lining of the artery (intimal layer) that makes the vessel permeable to circulating lipoproteins. Penetration of lipo-proteins into the smooth muscle cells of the intima produces “fat-ty streaks.” A fibrous plaque large enough to decrease blood flow through the artery develops. Calcification with rupture or hemor-rhage of the fibrous plaque is the final advanced stage. Thrombosis(stationary blood clot) may occur， further occluding the lumen of the blood vessel.</u>|删除换行|called thrombosis. Coronary thrombosis refers to the forma-tion of a clot in one of the coronary arteries， usually causing a heart attack.

【6】Spasm. Sudden constriction of a coronary artery isc1S C1alled a spasm； blood flow to that part of the heart is cut off or decreased. A brief spasm may cause mild symptoms that never return. A prolonged spasm may cause heart damage such as an infarct. This process can occur in healthy persons who have no cardiac history， as well as in those who have known atherosclerosis. Chemicals like nicotine and cocaine may lead to coronary artery spasm； other possible factors include anxiety and cold air.

The tradition-al model held that an atherosclerotic plaque in the blood vessel， particularly a coronary blood vessel， kept growing inward and ob-structing flow until it closed off and caused a heart attack. This is not entirely correct. It is more accurate to say that in the normal vessel (A)， penetration of lipoproteins into the smooth muscle cells of the intima produces fatty streaks (B) and the start of a coronary lesion forms. C and D， The coronary lesion grows outward first in a compensatory manner to maintain the open lumen. This is called positive remodeling， as the blood vessel tries to maintain an open lumen until it can do so no more. E， Only then does the plaque(atheroma) begin to build up， gradually pressing inward into the lu-men with obstruction of blood flow and possible rupture and throm-bosis， potentially leading to myocardial infarction (Ml) or stroke.F， Vascular disease today is considered a disease of the wall. 【8】Risk Factors. In 1948 the United States government decided to investigate the etiology， incidence， and pathology of CAD by studying the residents of Framingham， Massa-chusetts， a typical small town in the United States. Over the next multiple decades， various aspects of lifestyle， health， and disease were studied. The research revealed important modi-fiable and nonmodifiable risk factors associated with death caused by CAD. Since that time， an additional category， con-tributing factors， has been added . The AHA has also developed a validated health-risk appraisal instrument to assess individual risk of heart attack， stroke， and diabetes.

【9】More recent research has identified other possible risk fac-tors for， and predictors of， cardiac events， especially for those persons who have already had a heart attack. These additional risk factors include：

Therefore whenever screening chest pain， keep in mind the demo-graphics： older men and women， menopausal women， and African-American women are at greatest risk.

【24】Diabetes alone poses a greater risk than any other factor in predicting cardiovascular problems in women. Women with diabetes are seven times more likely to have cardiovascular complications and about half of them will die of CAD.36

【31】Clinical Signs and Symptoms. Atherosclerosis， by itself， does not necessarily produce symptoms. For mani-festations to develop， there must be a critical deficit in blood supply to the heart in proportion to the demands of the myocardium for oxygen and nutrients (supply and demand imbalance). When atherosclerosis develops slowly， collateral circulation develops to meet the heart’s demands. Often， symptoms of CAD do not appear until the lumen of the coronary artery narrows by 75% .

【32】Although the arteries are rarely completely blocked， the deposits of plaque are often extensive enough to restrict blood flow to the heart， especially during exercise in a clinical practice when there is a need to deliver more oxygen-carry-ing blood to the heart. Like other muscles， the heart， when deprived of oxygen， may ache， causing chest pain or discom-fort referred to as angina.

【33】CAD is a progressive disorder， especially if left untreated. If the blood flow is entirely disrupted， usually by a clot that has formed in the obstructed region， some of the tissue that is supplied by the vessel can die， and a heart attack or even sudden cardiac death results.

【34】When tissue loss is extensive enough to disrupt the elec-trical impulses that stimulate the heart’s contractions， heart failure， chronic arrhythmias， and conduction disturbances may develop.

【35】Acute pain in the chest， called angina pectoris， results from the imbalance between cardiac workload and oxygen supply to myocardial tissue. Angina is a symptom of obstructed or decreased blood supply to the heart muscle primarily from atherosclerosis.

【36】Atherosclerosis is now recognized as an inflammatory condition affecting the coronary arteries and the peripheral vessels. It is often accompanied by hypertension and signs of PVD. Although the primary cause of angina is CAD， angina can occur in individuals with normal coronary arteries and with other conditions affecting the supply/demand balance.

【37】As vessels become lined with atherosclerotic plaque， symp-toms of inadequate blood supply develop in the tissues sup-plied by these vessels. A growing mass of plaque in the vessel collects platelets， fibrin， and cellular debris. Platelet aggrega-tions are known to release prostaglandins capable of causing vessel spasm. This in turn promotes platelet aggregation， and a vicious spasm/pain cycle begins. CyC

The present theory of heart pain suggests that pain occurs as a result of an accumulation of metabolites within an|删除0换行|ischemic segment of the myocardium. The transient ischemia of angina or the prolonged， necrotic ischemia of an MI sets off pain impulses secondary to rapid accumulation of these metabolites in the heart muscle.

【39】The imbalance between cardiac workload and oxygen sup-ply can develop as a result of disorders of the coronary ves-sels， disorders of circulation， increased demands on output of the heart， or damaged myocardium unable to utilize oxygen properly.

【40】Types of Anginal Pain. There are a number of types of anginal pain， including chronic stable angina (also referred to as walk-through angina)， resting angina (angina decubi-tus)， unstable angina， nocturnal angina， atypical angina，new-onset angina， and Prinzmetal’s or“variant"angina.

【41】Chronic stable angina occurs at a predictable level of physi-cal or emotional stress and responds promptly to rest or to nitroglycerin. No pain occurs at rest， and the location， dura-tion， intensity， and frequency of chest pain are consistent over time.

【42】_Resting angina， or angina decubitus， is chest pain that_ occurs at rest in the supine position and frequently at the same time every day. The pain is neither brought on by exer-cise nor relieved by rest.

【43】Unstable angina， also known as crescendo angina， prein-farction angina， or progressive angina， is an abrupt change in the intensity and frequency of symptoms or decreased thresh-old of stimulus， such as the onset of chest pain while at rest. The most common trigger of unstable angina is the burst-ing of a cholesterol-filled plaque in the lining of a coronary artery. A blood clot forms at that site， partially blocking blood flow. The duration of these attacks is longer than the usual 1to 5 minutes； they may last for up to 20 to 30 minutes and can progress into a full-blown heart attack. Pain or discomfort unrelieved by rest or nitroglycerin signals a higher risk for MI. Such changes in the pattern of angina require immediate medical follow-up by the client’s physician.

【44】Nocturnal angina may awaken a person from sleep with the same sensation experienced during exertion. During sleep this exertion is usually caused by dreams. This type of angina may be associated with underlying CHF.

【45】Atypical angina refers to unusual symptoms (e.g.， tooth-ache or earache) related to physical or emotional exertion. These symptoms subside with rest or nitroglycerin. New-onset angina describes angina that has developed for the first time within the last 60 days.

【46】_Prinzmetal's (vasospastic or variant) angina produces_ symptoms similar to those of typical angina but is caused by abnormal or involuntary coronary artery spasm rather than directly by a build-up of plaque from atherosclerosis. These spasms periodically squeeze arteries shut and keep the blood from reaching the heart. About two thirds of people with Prinzmetal's have severe coronary atherosclerosis in at least one major vessel. The spasm usually occurs very close to the blockage.

This form of angina typically occurs at rest， especially in the early hours of the morning， and can be difficult to induce by exercise. It is cyclic and frequently occurs at the same time|删除0换行|each day. In postmenopausal women who are not undergo-ing hormone replacement therapy， the reduction in estrogen may cause coronary arteries to spasm， resulting in vasospastic(Prinzmetal’s) angina.

【48】Recognizing heart pain in women is more difficult because the symptoms are less reliable and often do not follow the classic pattern described earlier. Many women describe the pain in ways consistent with unstable angina， suggesting that they first become aware of their chest discomfort or have it diagnosed only after it reaches more advanced stages.

This overflow increases the chance that final common pain pathways between the chest and the abdomen may occur.

【1】Atherosclerosis. Atherosclerosis is the disease process often called arteriosclerosis or hardening of the arteries. It is a progressive process that may begin in childhood. It can occur in any artery in the body， but it is most common in medium-sized arteries such as those of the heart， brain， kidneys， and legs. Starting in childhood， the arteries begin to fill with a fatty substance， or lipids such as triglycerides and cholesterol， which then calcify or harden .

【2】This filler， called plaque， is made up of fats， calcium， and fibrous scar tissue and lines the usually supple arterial walls， progressively narrowing the arteries. These arteries carry blood rich in oxygen to the myocardium (middle layer of the heart consisting of the heart muscle)， but the atheroscle-rotic process leads to ischemia and to necrosis of the heart muscle. Necrotic tissue gradually forms a scar， but before scar formation， the weakened area is susceptible to aneurysm development.

【3】When fully developed， plaque can cause bleeding， clot for-mation， and distortion or rupture of a blood vessel . Heart attacks and strokes are the most sudden and often fatal signs of the disease.

【4】Thrombus. When plaque builds up on the artery walls， the blood flow is slowed and a clot (thrombus) may form on the plaque. When a vessel becomes blocked by a clot， it is

通用删除16(英):<u>Fig. 6.2Hardening of the arteries. Atherosclerosis begins with an injury to the endothelial lining of the artery (intimal layer) that makes the vessel permeable to circulating lipoproteins. Penetration of lipo-proteins into the smooth muscle cells of the intima produces “fat-ty streaks.” A fibrous plaque large enough to decrease blood flow through the artery develops. Calcification with rupture or hemor-rhage of the fibrous plaque is the final advanced stage. Thrombosis(stationary blood clot) may occur， further occluding the lumen of the blood vessel.</u>|删除换行|called thrombosis. Coronary thrombosis refers to the forma-tion of a clot in one of the coronary arteries， usually causing a heart attack.

【6】Spasm. Sudden constriction of a coronary artery isc1S C1alled a spasm； blood flow to that part of the heart is cut off or decreased. A brief spasm may cause mild symptoms that never return. A prolonged spasm may cause heart damage such as an infarct. This process can occur in healthy persons who have no cardiac history， as well as in those who have known atherosclerosis. Chemicals like nicotine and cocaine may lead to coronary artery spasm； other possible factors include anxiety and cold air.

【7】通用删除16(英):<u>Fig. 6.3Updated model of atherosclerosis. New technology using intravascular ultrasound shows the whole atherosclerotic V We VI plaque and has changed the way we view things. The tradition-al model held that an atherosclerotic plaque in the blood vessel， particularly a coronary blood vessel， kept growing inward and ob-structing flow until it closed off and caused a heart attack. This is not entirely correct. It is more accurate to say that in the normal vessel (A)， penetration of lipoproteins into the smooth muscle cells of the intima produces fatty streaks (B) and the start of a coronary lesion forms. C and D， The coronary lesion grows outward first in a compensatory manner to maintain the open lumen. This is called positive remodeling， as the blood vessel tries to maintain an open lumen until it can do so no more. E， Only then does the plaque(atheroma) begin to build up， gradually pressing inward into the lu-men with obstruction of blood flow and possible rupture and throm-bosis， potentially leading to myocardial infarction (Ml) or stroke.F， Vascular disease today is considered a disease of the wall. Some researchers like to say the disease is in the donut， not the hole of a donut， and that is a new concept.101</u>

【8】Risk Factors. In 1948 the United States government decided to investigate the etiology， incidence， and pathology of CAD by studying the residents of Framingham， Massa-chusetts， a typical small town in the United States. Over the next multiple decades， various aspects of lifestyle， health， and disease were studied. The research revealed important modi-fiable and nonmodifiable risk factors associated with death caused by CAD. Since that time， an additional category， con-tributing factors， has been added . The AHA has also developed a validated health-risk appraisal instrument to assess individual risk of heart attack， stroke， and diabetes.

【9】More recent research has identified other possible risk fac-tors for， and predictors of， cardiac events， especially for those persons who have already had a heart attack. These additional risk factors include：

【13】4\. High levels of fibrinogen， a protein that binds together platelet cells in blood clots24

【1】Atherosclerosis. Atherosclerosis is the disease process often called arteriosclerosis or hardening of the arteries. It is a progressive process that may begin in childhood. It can occur in any artery in the body， but it is most common in medium-sized arteries such as those of the heart， brain， kidneys， and legs. Starting in childhood， the arteries begin to fill with a fatty substance， or lipids such as triglycerides and cholesterol， which then calcify or harden .

【2】This filler， called plaque， is made up of fats， calcium， and fibrous scar tissue and lines the usually supple arterial walls， progressively narrowing the arteries. These arteries carry blood rich in oxygen to the myocardium (middle layer of the heart consisting of the heart muscle)， but the atheroscle-rotic process leads to ischemia and to necrosis of the heart muscle. Necrotic tissue gradually forms a scar， but before scar formation， the weakened area is susceptible to aneurysm development.

【3】When fully developed， plaque can cause bleeding， clot for-mation， and distortion or rupture of a blood vessel . Heart attacks and strokes are the most sudden and often fatal signs of the disease.

【4】Thrombus. When plaque builds up on the artery walls， the blood flow is slowed and a clot (thrombus) may form on the plaque. When a vessel becomes blocked by a clot， it is

Penetration of lipo-proteins into the smooth muscle cells of the intima produces “fat-ty streaks.” A fibrous plaque large enough to decrease blood flow through the artery develops. Calcification with rupture or hemor-rhage of the fibrous plaque is the final advanced stage. Thrombosis(stationary blood clot) may occur， further occluding the lumen of the blood vessel.</u>|删除换行|called thrombosis. Coronary thrombosis refers to the forma-tion of a clot in one of the coronary arteries， usually causing a heart attack.

【6】Spasm. Sudden constriction of a coronary artery isc1S C1alled a spasm； blood flow to that part of the heart is cut off or decreased. A brief spasm may cause mild symptoms that never return. A prolonged spasm may cause heart damage such as an infarct. This process can occur in healthy persons who have no cardiac history， as well as in those who have known atherosclerosis. Chemicals like nicotine and cocaine may lead to coronary artery spasm； other possible factors include anxiety and cold air.

【7】通用删除16(英):<u>Fig. 6.3Updated model of atherosclerosis. New technology using intravascular ultrasound shows the whole atherosclerotic V We VI plaque and has changed the way we view things. The tradition-al model held that an atherosclerotic plaque in the blood vessel， particularly a coronary blood vessel， kept growing inward and ob-structing flow until it closed off and caused a heart attack. This is not entirely correct. It is more accurate to say that in the normal vessel (A)， penetration of lipoproteins into the smooth muscle cells of the intima produces fatty streaks (B) and the start of a coronary lesion forms. C and D， The coronary lesion grows outward first in a compensatory manner to maintain the open lumen. This is called positive remodeling， as the blood vessel tries to maintain an open lumen until it can do so no more. E， Only then does the plaque(atheroma) begin to build up， gradually pressing inward into the lu-men with obstruction of blood flow and possible rupture and throm-bosis， potentially leading to myocardial infarction (Ml) or stroke.F， Vascular disease today is considered a disease of the wall. Some researchers like to say the disease is in the donut， not the hole of a donut， and that is a new concept.101</u>

【8】Risk Factors. In 1948 the United States government decided to investigate the etiology， incidence， and pathology of CAD by studying the residents of Framingham， Massa-chusetts， a typical small town in the United States. Over the next multiple decades， various aspects of lifestyle， health， and disease were studied. The research revealed important modi-fiable and nonmodifiable risk factors associated with death caused by CAD. Since that time， an additional category， con-tributing factors， has been added . The AHA has also developed a validated health-risk appraisal instrument to assess individual risk of heart attack， stroke， and diabetes.

【9】More recent research has identified other possible risk fac-tors for， and predictors of， cardiac events， especially for those persons who have already had a heart attack. These additional risk factors include：

【10】1\. Exposure to bacteria such as Chlamydia pneumoniae， Por- _phyromonas gingivalis， and Cytomegalovirus21-23_

【11】2\. Excess levels of homocysteine， an amino acid by-product of food rich in proteins

【12】3\. High levels of alpha-lipoprotein， a close cousin of LDL that transports fat throughout the body

【13】4\. High levels of fibrinogen， a protein that binds together platelet cells in blood clots24

【17】8.Past history of cancer treatment (cardiotoxic chemothera-peutic agents， trunk radiation)3

【22】Women do not seem to do as well as men after tak-ing medications to dissolve blood clots or after undergoing heart-related medical procedures. Of the women who survive a heart attack， 46% will be disabled by heart failure within 6years.删除14:<u>35</u>

【23】In general， the rate of CAD is rising among women and falling among men. Men develop CAD at a younger age than women， but women make up for it after menopause. The prevalence of CAD among African-American women is 48%， whereas it is 36% for Caucasian women. Therefore whenever screening chest pain， keep in mind the demo-graphics： older men and women， menopausal women， and African-American women are at greatest risk.

【24】Diabetes alone poses a greater risk than any other factor in predicting cardiovascular problems in women. Women with diabetes are seven times more likely to have cardiovascular complications and about half of them will die of CAD.36

【25】Studies have shown that women and men actually differ when it comes to symptoms of CAD and in the manner in which acute MI can present. Women experience symptoms of CAD， which are more subtle and“atypical"compared with the traditional symptoms such as angina and chest pain.

【26】One of the most important primary signs of CAD in women is unexplained， severe episodic fatigue and weak-ness associated with a decreased ability to carry out normal activities of daily living (ADLs). Because fatigue， weakness， and trouble sleeping are general types of symptoms， they are not as easily associated with cardiovascular events and are many times missed by health care providers when screening for heart disease.删除14:<u>37</u>

【27】Symptoms of weakness， fatigue and sleeping difficulty， and nausea have been reported as a common occurrence as much as a month before the development of acute MI in women . 【30】Risk reduction in women focuses on lifestyle changes such as smoking cessation； low fat， low cholesterol diet； increased intake of omega-3 fatty acids； increased fruit， vegetable， whole grain intake； salt and alcohol limitation； and increased exer-cise and weight loss. If the woman has diabetes， strict glucose control is extremely important.删除14:<u>38</u>

【31】Clinical Signs and Symptoms. Atherosclerosis， by itself， does not necessarily produce symptoms. For mani-festations to develop， there must be a critical deficit in blood supply to the heart in proportion to the demands of the myocardium for oxygen and nutrients (supply and demand imbalance). When atherosclerosis develops slowly， collateral circulation develops to meet the heart’s demands. Often， symptoms of CAD do not appear until the lumen of the coronary artery narrows by 75% .

【32】Although the arteries are rarely completely blocked， the deposits of plaque are often extensive enough to restrict blood flow to the heart， especially during exercise in a clinical practice when there is a need to deliver more oxygen-carry-ing blood to the heart. Like other muscles， the heart， when deprived of oxygen， may ache， causing chest pain or discom-fort referred to as angina.

【33】CAD is a progressive disorder， especially if left untreated. If the blood flow is entirely disrupted， usually by a clot that has formed in the obstructed region， some of the tissue that is supplied by the vessel can die， and a heart attack or even sudden cardiac death results.

【34】When tissue loss is extensive enough to disrupt the elec-trical impulses that stimulate the heart’s contractions， heart failure， chronic arrhythmias， and conduction disturbances may develop.

【35】Acute pain in the chest， called angina pectoris， results from the imbalance between cardiac workload and oxygen supply to myocardial tissue. Angina is a symptom of obstructed or decreased blood supply to the heart muscle primarily from atherosclerosis.

【36】Atherosclerosis is now recognized as an inflammatory condition affecting the coronary arteries and the peripheral vessels. It is often accompanied by hypertension and signs of PVD. Although the primary cause of angina is CAD， angina can occur in individuals with normal coronary arteries and with other conditions affecting the supply/demand balance.

【37】As vessels become lined with atherosclerotic plaque， symp-toms of inadequate blood supply develop in the tissues sup-plied by these vessels. A growing mass of plaque in the vessel collects platelets， fibrin， and cellular debris. Platelet aggrega-tions are known to release prostaglandins capable of causing vessel spasm. This in turn promotes platelet aggregation， and a vicious spasm/pain cycle begins. CyC

The present theory of heart pain suggests that pain occurs as a result of an accumulation of metabolites within an|删除0换行|ischemic segment of the myocardium. The transient ischemia of angina or the prolonged， necrotic ischemia of an MI sets off pain impulses secondary to rapid accumulation of these metabolites in the heart muscle.

【39】The imbalance between cardiac workload and oxygen sup-ply can develop as a result of disorders of the coronary ves-sels， disorders of circulation， increased demands on output of the heart， or damaged myocardium unable to utilize oxygen properly.

【40】Types of Anginal Pain. There are a number of types of anginal pain， including chronic stable angina (also referred to as walk-through angina)， resting angina (angina decubi-tus)， unstable angina， nocturnal angina， atypical angina，new-onset angina， and Prinzmetal’s or“variant"angina.

【41】Chronic stable angina occurs at a predictable level of physi-cal or emotional stress and responds promptly to rest or to nitroglycerin. No pain occurs at rest， and the location， dura-tion， intensity， and frequency of chest pain are consistent over time.

【42】_Resting angina， or angina decubitus， is chest pain that_ occurs at rest in the supine position and frequently at the same time every day. The pain is neither brought on by exer-cise nor relieved by rest.

【43】Unstable angina， also known as crescendo angina， prein-farction angina， or progressive angina， is an abrupt change in the intensity and frequency of symptoms or decreased thresh-old of stimulus， such as the onset of chest pain while at rest. The most common trigger of unstable angina is the burst-ing of a cholesterol-filled plaque in the lining of a coronary artery. A blood clot forms at that site， partially blocking blood flow. The duration of these attacks is longer than the usual 1to 5 minutes； they may last for up to 20 to 30 minutes and can progress into a full-blown heart attack. Pain or discomfort unrelieved by rest or nitroglycerin signals a higher risk for MI. Such changes in the pattern of angina require immediate medical follow-up by the client’s physician.

【44】Nocturnal angina may awaken a person from sleep with the same sensation experienced during exertion. During sleep this exertion is usually caused by dreams. This type of angina may be associated with underlying CHF.

【45】Atypical angina refers to unusual symptoms (e.g.， tooth-ache or earache) related to physical or emotional exertion. These symptoms subside with rest or nitroglycerin. New-onset angina describes angina that has developed for the first time within the last 60 days.

【46】_Prinzmetal's (vasospastic or variant) angina produces_ symptoms similar to those of typical angina but is caused by abnormal or involuntary coronary artery spasm rather than directly by a build-up of plaque from atherosclerosis. These spasms periodically squeeze arteries shut and keep the blood from reaching the heart. About two thirds of people with Prinzmetal's have severe coronary atherosclerosis in at least one major vessel. The spasm usually occurs very close to the blockage.

This form of angina typically occurs at rest， especially in the early hours of the morning， and can be difficult to induce by exercise. It is cyclic and frequently occurs at the same time|删除0换行|each day. In postmenopausal women who are not undergo-ing hormone replacement therapy， the reduction in estrogen may cause coronary arteries to spasm， resulting in vasospastic(Prinzmetal’s) angina.

【48】Recognizing heart pain in women is more difficult because the symptoms are less reliable and often do not follow the classic pattern described earlier. Many women describe the pain in ways consistent with unstable angina， suggesting that they first become aware of their chest discomfort or have it diagnosed only after it reaches more advanced stages.

【49】Some experience a sensation similar to inhaling cold air， rather than the more typical shortness of breath. Other women complain only of weakness and lethargy， and some have noted isolated pain in the midthoracic spine or throb-bing and aching in the right biceps muscle .

【50】Pain associated with the angina and MI occurring along the inner aspect of the arm and corresponding to the ulnar nerve distribution results from common connections between the cardiac and brachial plexuses.

【51】Cardiac pain referred to the jaw occurs through internun-cial (neurons connecting other neurons) fibers from cervical spinal cord posterior horns to the spinal nucleus of the tri-geminal nerve. Abdominal pain produced by referred cardiac pain is more difficult to explain and may be caused by the overflow of segmental levels to which visceral afferent nerve pathways flow . This overflow increases the chance that final common pain pathways between the chest and the abdomen may occur.

【52】The sensation of angina is described as squeezing， burn-ing， pressing， choking， aching， or bursting. Chest pain can be brought on by a wide variety of noncardiac causes .

【53】In particular， angina is often confused with heartburn or indigestion， hiatal hernia， esophageal spasm， or gallbladder disease， but the pain of these other conditions is not described as sharp or knife-like.

【54】The client often says the pain feels like “gas"or"heartburn”or “indigestion.” Referred pain from a trigger point in the external oblique abdominal muscle can cause a sensation of heartburn in the anterior chest wall . A physi-cian must make the differentiation between angina and heart-burn， hiatal hernia， and gallbladder disease. The therapist can assess for trigger points； relief of symptoms with elimination of trigger points is an important diagnostic finding.

【57】Severity is usually mild or moderate. Rarely is the pain described as severe. The five-grade angina scale ranks angina as：

【58】**Grade 0No anginaGrade 1Light， barely noticeableGrade 2Moderately bothersomeGrade 3Severe， very uncomfortable**

【59】**Grade 4 Most pain ever experienced**

【60】As to location， 80% to 90% ofclients experience the pain as retrosternal or slightly to the left ofthe sternum. The duration of angina as a direct result of myocardial ischemia is typically l to 3 minutes and no longer than 3 to 5 minutes. However， attacks precipitated by a heavy meal or extreme anger may last 15 to 20 minutes. Angina is relieved by rest or nitroglyc-erin (a coronary artery vasodilator).

【61】People who have had coronary artery stents placed can experience angina if an occlusion occurs above， below， or within the stent. Anyone with a stent who has chest pain should be immediately sent for referral to a physician.

【62】Severity of pain is not a good prognostic indicator； some persons with severe discomfort live for many years， whereas others with mild symptoms may die suddenly. If the pain is not relieved by rest or with up to three nitroglycerin tablets(taken one at a time at 5-minute intervals) in 10 to 15 min-utes， the physician should be notified and the client taken to a cardiac care unit.

Like other muscles， the heart， when deprived of oxygen， may ache， causing chest pain or discom-fort referred to as angina.

【33】CAD is a progressive disorder， especially if left untreated. If the blood flow is entirely disrupted， usually by a clot that has formed in the obstructed region， some of the tissue that is supplied by the vessel can die， and a heart attack or even sudden cardiac death results.

【34】When tissue loss is extensive enough to disrupt the elec-trical impulses that stimulate the heart’s contractions， heart failure， chronic arrhythmias， and conduction disturbances may develop.

【35】Acute pain in the chest， called angina pectoris， results from the imbalance between cardiac workload and oxygen supply to myocardial tissue. Angina is a symptom of obstructed or decreased blood supply to the heart muscle primarily from atherosclerosis.

【36】Atherosclerosis is now recognized as an inflammatory condition affecting the coronary arteries and the peripheral vessels. It is often accompanied by hypertension and signs of PVD. Although the primary cause of angina is CAD， angina can occur in individuals with normal coronary arteries and with other conditions affecting the supply/demand balance.

【37】As vessels become lined with atherosclerotic plaque， symp-toms of inadequate blood supply develop in the tissues sup-plied by these vessels. A growing mass of plaque in the vessel collects platelets， fibrin， and cellular debris. Platelet aggrega-tions are known to release prostaglandins capable of causing vessel spasm. This in turn promotes platelet aggregation， and a vicious spasm/pain cycle begins. CyC

The present theory of heart pain suggests that pain occurs as a result of an accumulation of metabolites within an|删除0换行|ischemic segment of the myocardium. The transient ischemia of angina or the prolonged， necrotic ischemia of an MI sets off pain impulses secondary to rapid accumulation of these metabolites in the heart muscle.

【39】The imbalance between cardiac workload and oxygen sup-ply can develop as a result of disorders of the coronary ves-sels， disorders of circulation， increased demands on output of the heart， or damaged myocardium unable to utilize oxygen properly.

【40】Types of Anginal Pain. There are a number of types of anginal pain， including chronic stable angina (also referred to as walk-through angina)， resting angina (angina decubi-tus)， unstable angina， nocturnal angina， atypical angina，new-onset angina， and Prinzmetal’s or“variant"angina.

【41】Chronic stable angina occurs at a predictable level of physi-cal or emotional stress and responds promptly to rest or to nitroglycerin. No pain occurs at rest， and the location， dura-tion， intensity， and frequency of chest pain are consistent over time.

【42】_Resting angina， or angina decubitus， is chest pain that_ occurs at rest in the supine position and frequently at the same time every day. The pain is neither brought on by exer-cise nor relieved by rest.

【43】Unstable angina， also known as crescendo angina， prein-farction angina， or progressive angina， is an abrupt change in the intensity and frequency of symptoms or decreased thresh-old of stimulus， such as the onset of chest pain while at rest. The most common trigger of unstable angina is the burst-ing of a cholesterol-filled plaque in the lining of a coronary artery. A blood clot forms at that site， partially blocking blood flow. The duration of these attacks is longer than the usual 1to 5 minutes； they may last for up to 20 to 30 minutes and can progress into a full-blown heart attack. Pain or discomfort unrelieved by rest or nitroglycerin signals a higher risk for MI. Such changes in the pattern of angina require immediate medical follow-up by the client’s physician.

【44】Nocturnal angina may awaken a person from sleep with the same sensation experienced during exertion. During sleep this exertion is usually caused by dreams. This type of angina may be associated with underlying CHF.

【45】Atypical angina refers to unusual symptoms (e.g.， tooth-ache or earache) related to physical or emotional exertion. These symptoms subside with rest or nitroglycerin. New-onset angina describes angina that has developed for the first time within the last 60 days.

【46】_Prinzmetal's (vasospastic or variant) angina produces_ symptoms similar to those of typical angina but is caused by abnormal or involuntary coronary artery spasm rather than directly by a build-up of plaque from atherosclerosis. These spasms periodically squeeze arteries shut and keep the blood from reaching the heart. About two thirds of people with Prinzmetal's have severe coronary atherosclerosis in at least one major vessel. The spasm usually occurs very close to the blockage.

This form of angina typically occurs at rest， especially in the early hours of the morning， and can be difficult to induce by exercise. It is cyclic and frequently occurs at the same time|删除0换行|each day. In postmenopausal women who are not undergo-ing hormone replacement therapy， the reduction in estrogen may cause coronary arteries to spasm， resulting in vasospastic(Prinzmetal’s) angina.

【48】Recognizing heart pain in women is more difficult because the symptoms are less reliable and often do not follow the classic pattern described earlier. Many women describe the pain in ways consistent with unstable angina， suggesting that they first become aware of their chest discomfort or have it diagnosed only after it reaches more advanced stages.

【49】Some experience a sensation similar to inhaling cold air， rather than the more typical shortness of breath. Other women complain only of weakness and lethargy， and some have noted isolated pain in the midthoracic spine or throb-bing and aching in the right biceps muscle .

【50】Pain associated with the angina and MI occurring along the inner aspect of the arm and corresponding to the ulnar nerve distribution results from common connections between the cardiac and brachial plexuses.

【51】Cardiac pain referred to the jaw occurs through internun-cial (neurons connecting other neurons) fibers from cervical spinal cord posterior horns to the spinal nucleus of the tri-geminal nerve. Abdominal pain produced by referred cardiac pain is more difficult to explain and may be caused by the overflow of segmental levels to which visceral afferent nerve pathways flow . This overflow increases the chance that final common pain pathways between the chest and the abdomen may occur.

【52】The sensation of angina is described as squeezing， burn-ing， pressing， choking， aching， or bursting. Chest pain can be brought on by a wide variety of noncardiac causes .

【53】In particular， angina is often confused with heartburn or indigestion， hiatal hernia， esophageal spasm， or gallbladder disease， but the pain of these other conditions is not described as sharp or knife-like.

【54】The client often says the pain feels like “gas"or"heartburn”or “indigestion.” Referred pain from a trigger point in the external oblique abdominal muscle can cause a sensation of heartburn in the anterior chest wall . A physi-cian must make the differentiation between angina and heart-burn， hiatal hernia， and gallbladder disease. The therapist can assess for trigger points； relief of symptoms with elimination of trigger points is an important diagnostic finding.

【57】Severity is usually mild or moderate. Rarely is the pain described as severe. The five-grade angina scale ranks angina as：

【58】**Grade 0No anginaGrade 1Light， barely noticeableGrade 2Moderately bothersomeGrade 3Severe， very uncomfortable**

【59】**Grade 4 Most pain ever experienced**

【60】As to location， 80% to 90% ofclients experience the pain as retrosternal or slightly to the left ofthe sternum. The duration of angina as a direct result of myocardial ischemia is typically l to 3 minutes and no longer than 3 to 5 minutes. However， attacks precipitated by a heavy meal or extreme anger may last 15 to 20 minutes. Angina is relieved by rest or nitroglyc-erin (a coronary artery vasodilator).

【61】People who have had coronary artery stents placed can experience angina if an occlusion occurs above， below， or within the stent. Anyone with a stent who has chest pain should be immediately sent for referral to a physician.

【62】Severity of pain is not a good prognostic indicator； some persons with severe discomfort live for many years， whereas others with mild symptoms may die suddenly. If the pain is not relieved by rest or with up to three nitroglycerin tablets(taken one at a time at 5-minute intervals) in 10 to 15 min-utes， the physician should be notified and the client taken to a cardiac care unit.

【54】The most common symptoms include sweatiness， palpitations， weakness， hunger， drowsiness， restlessness， tremor， seizures and coma. Occasionally personality changes may be a presenting symptom. There may be a history of pituitary dysfunction. Causes of pituitary failure include tumour， trauma， pituitary surgery and infection. The symptoms of Addison's disease include weakness， weight loss， dizziness and pigmentation of the buccal mucosa and palmar creases. 【318】Important aspects of the history are to enquire about symptoms suggestive of the diagnosis of anaemia， and to establish any underlying cause.

【319】**Symptoms of anaemia**

【320】The symptoms of anaemia are dependent on the degree of anaemia， speed of onset， age and the presence of co-existing disease. Mild to moderate chronic anaemia may be asymptomatic in young， fit individuals. Symptoms of anaemia include tiredness， lethargy and dyspnoea. Anaemia can precipitate or worsen angina and lower limb claudication.

【321】Blood loss is a common cause of iron deficiency anaemia and frank bleeding can easily be established from the history. Occult bleeding from the gastrointestinal tract is an important cause of chronic blood loss. Patients may have melaena and may also experience upper abdominal pains from peptic ulceration， gastritis， gastro-oesophageal reflux or gastric carcinoma . The causes of lower gastrointestinal bleeding are detailed on p. 399. The amount and frequency of blood loss with menstruation should be documented and the presence of haemoptysis and haematuria should be ascertained. Malabsorption can cause a deficiency of substrate or coenzyme requirements for the synthesis of haemoglobin. Gastrectomy or atrophic gastritis with pernicious anaemia may impair both iron and vitamin B.，absorption due to alterations in pH and effects on intrinsic factor， respectively. Impairment of vitamin B.， absorption may also result from extensive disease or resection involving the terminal ileum and predisposes to megaloblastic anaemia. A history of travel to areas where malaria and hookworm infections are endemic should be sought.

【322】It is important to take a dietary history， as folate deficiency results from poor dietary intake. This is in contrast to iron， as dietary deficiency of iron alone rarely results in anaemia unless accompanied by increased utilisation or blood loss. Owing to intrinsic stores of vitamin B， dietary deficiencies may take up to two years before becoming clinically apparent. The amount of alcohol intake should also be noted because alcohol excess may result in a macrocytic anaemia.

【323】**Past medical and drug history**

A number of chronic diseases can result in anaemia but it is important to exclude other concomitant causes before attributing anaemia to the effects of the primary illness. Diseases predisposing to macrocytic anaemia have been listed above. Aplasia of the marrow may occur|删除0换行|as a complication of viral hepatitis or exposure to radiation and result in aplastic anaemia. Drugs such as chemotherapeutic agents， chloramphenicol and sulphonamides may also precipitate bone marrow failure. Respiratory tract infections with mycoplasma， infectious mononucleosis， lymphomas and connective tissue disease are associated with autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.

【325】Haemoglobinopathies such as thalassaemia and sickle cell disease may be inherited. Alternatively， hereditary enzyme defects (G6PD) or red cell membrane defects (hereditary spherocytosis) may also result in intravascular haemolysis.

【326】**EXAMINATION**

【327】Classically， patients with anaemia have pallor of the palmar skin creases and conjunctivae； however， diagnosis based solely on these findings is unreliable. With iron deficiency， spoon-shaped nails(koilonychia) may be noted； these findings may be accompanied by angular cheilitis and glossitis. Jaundice can be a complication of haemolytic anaemia or can result from chronic liver disease.

【328】Subacute combined degeneration of the cord is a complication of severe vitamin B。 deficiency. Neurological examination reveals symmetrical loss of light touch， vibration and proprioception of the feet due to dorsal column involvement. In addition， Romberg's sign may be elicited. Less common features are peripheral neuropathy， optic atrophy and dementia.

【329】With anaemia， examination of the cardiovascular system may reveal evidence of a hyperdynamic circulation with tachycardia， bounding pulse and a systolic flow murmur.
