【16】During puberty， HMB can occur as a result of hypofunction of the anterior pituitary body， with consequent failure of ovulation and there-fore no corpus luteum is formed. The ovaries contain unruptured Graafian follicles； there is increased oestrogen production and a lack of the luteal hormone progesterone. Once the pituitary gradually assumes its normal cyclic activity， then the cycles often occur spontaneously. These are anovulatory cycles and are usually painless.

【17】Perimenopausal women may experience heavy menstrual bleeding secondary to cessation of reg-ular ovulatory cycles. When there is a complete absence of progesterone in the second half of the menstrual cycle， the cycle is referred to as anovular， drawing attention to failure of ovulation and for-mation ofa corpus luteum. The endometrium may undergo polypoidal thickening with a characteris-tic microscopic appearance known as ‘Swiss cheese’endometrium or complex hyperplasia. Episodes of amenorrhoea of some weeks may be followed by prolonged irregular and heavy bleeding.

【18】Heavy menstrual bleeding can be associated with fibroids((benign leiomyomas)， adeno-myosis， pelvic infection， endometrial polyps， endometriosis and the presence of an intrauterine contraceptive device. Of all the causes of pure HMB， leiomyoma (fibroids) of the uterus stands out as the only important growth associated with this symptom and a simple bimanual examina-tion， as a rule， suffices to show that such a tumour exists. The size and shape of the uterus is depend-ent on the number and size of the fibroids， as there may be more than one tumour in the uterus， whose shape may be exceedingly irregular. The uterus feels firm and， in most cases， is mobile.

【19】The only difficulty in diagnosis， as a rule， lies in distinguishing a fibroid of the uterus from an ovarian cyst. This is sometimes difficult， for it is not always possible to say that a given tumour is actually the enlarged uterus. Ultrasound scan-ning is helpful in the diagnosis of fibroids by establishing whether a pelvic swelling is both uterine and solid. Fibroids may be submucous， intramural、 subserosal Or pedunculated. Distortion of the uterine cavity with an increase in the surface area from which menstruation occurs will lead to menorrhagia .

【20】Chronic pelvic infection (in the form of a pyosalpinx， a hydrosalpinx， a tubo-ovariian abscess or chronic interstitial salpingitis) and ovarian endometriosis both give rise to HMB

In either case， a firm tender swelling in the pouch of Douglas is felt on bimanual palpation. Intermenstrual or irregular bleeding is also common in these cases.

【22】Adenomyosis is a condition that can present with HMB and pain at the time of menstruation； on examination the uterus may be tender. The diagnosis can only be confirmed histologically， as endometrial tissue is found invading the myometrium . The condition is more common in parous women and， in essence， there has been bleeding in the myometrium that gives rise to the pain and tenderness.

【24】There is almost always some increase of the menstrual blood loss with the use ofintrauterine contraceptive devices (IUCDs； copper devices) and， in some cases， the loss amounts to HMB. This results from the inflammatory reaction the coil sets up in the myometrium to prevent implantation of the fertilised egg. Changing the IUCD to a progestogen-releasing IUCD usually improves the situation.

【25】There arecertain1haemorrhagic disorders that can cause excessive menstrual loss. These include thrombocytopenic _purpura，_ VOI Willebrand's disease and Christmas disease. These women may suffer excessive menstrual loss and may require surgical intervention. In thrombocytopenia， the blood loss relates to the platelet level and， in some cases， splenec-tomy for the underlying cause has improved the menstrual symptoms.

【26】Anticoagulation in women who are on long-term anticoagulants for prosthetic heart valves， previous pulmonary embolism or， in some cases， antiphospholipid syndrome may develop significant period problems depending on the international normalised ratio level.

【27】Thrombocytopenia can sometimes compli-cated by HMB. As soon as the platelet level is back to normal， the blood loss usually becomes normal.

【28】**Medical disorders**

【29】The function of the thyroid and adrenal glands can influence the menstrual loss， although the mechanism is unknown. HMB tends to be more common in hypothyroidism than thyrotoxicosis， and is not uncommon with Cushing’s disease.

【30】**Intermenstrual uterine bleeding**

Intermenstrual uterine bleeding means loss of blood vaginally between the menstrual periods， and the term should be applied strictly only to irregular haemorrhages during the reproductive age range， i.e. from puberty to the menopause. It may be used for losses of actual blood or for blood-stained discharges in which mucus is mixed with blood. For the purposes of discus-sion， irregular vaginal bleeding will be con-sidered here under three headings：|删除换行|irregular bleeding during menstrual life；

【32】irregular bleeding before puberty and after the menopause；

【33】irregular bleeding during pregnancy.

【34】It is important to emphasise that， if a woman has had regular periods and then starts to get irregu-lar bleeding for no apparent reason， one must exclude pregnancy and where that pregnancy is located，i.e. an ectopic pregnancy， as this is still a major cause of maternal death in the UK.

【35】**Irregular bleeding during menstrual life**

【36】The causes of irregular bleeding during men-strual life are given in Box 2.

【37】Malignancy

【38】_Carcinoma of the cervix_

Cervical cancer is an uncommon disease with an incidence that is reducing as a result of the cervi-cal screening programme. It is estimated that a general practitioner in the UK will see one case of cervical cancer every 7-9 years. The cervix is replaced with a friable mass， which causes irreg-ular bleeding as well as postcoital bleeding. The lesion can bee(diagnosedmacroscopically，|删除0换行|although many of these women will be seen in the colposcopy clinic so that a directed biopsy can be undertaken .

【40】**_Carcinoma of the uterine body_**

【41】Endometrial carcinoma does occur during the reproductive age group but it is much more common in postmenopausal women. It is the second most common genital tract tumour and presents with irregular bleeding. Risk factors include obesity (raised BMI)， nulliparity and his-tory of polycystic ovarian disease. It is unusual to diagnose this condition before the age of 40years， hence the Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists recommendations suggest-ing that women with menstrual irregularities before the age of 40 years should receive treat-ment for 3 months. If the irregularity persists， then a hysteroscopy and endometrial sampling should be undertaken. If the woman is over the age of 40 years， then this would be a first-line investigation .

【42】**_Sarcoma of the uterus_**

【43】This is a very uncommon tumour and occurs in fibroids. It may present with irregular bleeding， but many of these women will be post-menopausal and present with a rapidly expand-ing pelvic mass. The risk of a fibroid becoming malignant is estimated at about 1 in 1000. This tumour may occur in an existing fibroid or appear de novo. The difficulty with this condi-tion is the highly aggressive nature of the disease， which does not respond well to radiotherapy or chemotherapy as a rule .

【44】_Chorionic carcinoma_

This condition is fortunately very rare， and fol-lows hydatidiform mole in about 5 per cent of recorded cases， and it always follows pregnancy， never having been seen in the uterus where preg-nancy could be excluded， although the preg-nancy may have occurred some years earlier. It is associated with profuse bleeding and the rapid development of a fetid discharge due to decom-position of blood and necrosing tissues in utero. Secondary deposits of chorionic _：carcinoma_|删除换行|appear as small plum-coloured ulcerating nod-ules in the vagina and secondaries in the lungs cause haemoptysis. The patient rapidly becomes ill with pyrexia and profound anaemia. A raised level of chorionic gonadotrophin is found in the urine. The diagnosis depends upon the finding of masses of trophoblastic cells in uterine curettings without any evidence of villous formation .

【46】_Other malignancies_

【47】Carcinoma of the Fallopian tube is a rare tumour and tends to present in the postmenopausal woman， but may present with irregular bleeding. Ovarian cancer is unlikely to cause bleeding unless it has invaded the uterus. Clear-cell carcinoma of the vagina is also rare and has been reported in teenage girls exposed to stilboestrol in utero.

【48】Benign lesions that may cause irregular bleeding

【49】_Fibroids_

【50】Leiomyomas may cause a mixture of HMB and intermenstrual spotting. The irregular bleeding tends to occur when they are submucous. They may be in the process of extrusion when they may become infected and sloughing occurs. The reason for this is that， in these conditions， the tumours are partly strangulated by uterine con-traction1sS _a_ andd consequently congested with venous blood. This results in bleeding， which is unpredictable in timing and amount.

【51】_Polyps_

Cervical polyps are usually identi-fied at the time of taking a routine cervical smear test but， if the tip becomes inflamed， then it can give rise to vaginal bleeding or postcoital bleeding. Polyps within the endometrial cavity， whether fibroid or mucous， are common causes of inter-menstrual bleeding， and are usually quite defini-tivegrowths.Themicouspolypis soft、strawberry-red in colour， pedunculated and con-tains cystic spaces filled with glairy mucus. These growths are liable to infection and slough-ing， and are then apt to be mistaken for carcinoma or sarcoma macroscopically.

【53】**_Endometriosis_**

【54】This condition is defined as the finding of tissue outside the uterus that is histologically similar to that of endometrium， and is not strictly an inflammatory lesion. However， it is one of the commonest benign gynaecological conditions and may present with a myriad of symptoms， including painful bleeding and dyspareunia.

【55】_Ectropion of the cervix_

【56】This is a physiological condition in which there is eversion of the columnar epithelium from the endocervical canal towards the vagina. The colum-nar epithelium appears reddened because it is one-cell thick and consequently translucent， allowing the blood supply below to be seen. The term ero-sion should be avoided. as it suggests something pathological. The epithelium can become inflamed and gives rise to discharge， which sometimes results in contact bleeding， although intermen-strual bleeding is unusual. The columnar epithe-liummay undergo metaplastic changeetto squamous epithelium owing to pH changes within the vagina. This area is known as the transforma-tion zone. It is in this area that pre-cancerous changes may occur. Pre-cancerous changes within the cervix are asymptomatic and usually only diag-nosed by cytology and at time of colposcopy.

【57】**_Tuberculosis_**

【58】Tuberculosis (TB) may affect the genital tract and give rise to irregular bleeding and infertility. It is an uncommon problem within the UK but is much more common in the developing world. Histology of the endometrial curettings may give the diagnosis， although a strong suspi-cion of TB suggests the need to involve a physi-cian in the care of the woman.

【59】Heavy menstrual bleeding without obvious pathology

【60】Heavy menstrual bleeding without obvious pathology is also sometimes known as dysfunc-tional bleeding. It may occur at any age between puberty and the menopause， but 50 per cent occurs between the ages of 40 and 50 years， about 10 per cent at puberty， and the remainder between these ages. When it occurs in associa-tion with longer menstrual cycles， it is most likely the results of anovulation and for this rea-son is more likely seen in adolescents， at the time of the perimenopause and in women with polycystic ovarian syndrome. When the bleed-ing is usually preceded by amenorrhoea for some weeks then the length of bleeding may be prolonged.

【61】The histology of any curettings may prove to be essentially normal， although in women with a increased body mass index， polycystic ovarian syndrome or a perimenopausal woman， then endometrial hyperplasiamay be present. Endometrial hyperplasia  can occur as a

These conditions are histo-logical diagnoses and how the woman is treated will depend on her age and fertility status. Women with complex hyperplasia with atypia are at risk of developing endometrial cancer and hysterectomy is usually recommended.

【63】Contraception and heavy menstrual bleeding

【64】There are three main areas that can give rise to HMB as listed below.

【65】The copper-containing IUCDs can give rise to HMB and， in some cases， the low-grade inflammatory response of the endometrium to the coil can result in irregular shedding. The treatment would be to remove the coil in the first instance.

【66】Progesterone contraception， whether as the proges-terone only-pill， the Mirena lUCD or Depo-Provera， will usually result in the woman being amenor-rhoeic. There are a number of women who develop irregular bleeding， which may be completely unpre-dictable， although it is usually not particularly heavy.

【68】Bleeding associated with ovulation

【69】It is not uncommon for women to bleed very slightly about midway between the periods at the time of ovulation. When this is accompan-ied by lower abdominal pain (Mittelschmerz)， the diagnosis is straightforward.

【70】Bleeding due to granulosa-cell tumour

When irregular bleeding occurs in the presence of an ovarian swelling， the possibility of a granulosa-cell tumour arises. Removal of the|删除0换行|tumour and histology reveal its nature. The presence of an intrauterine lesion and a non-secreting ovarian tumour must not be over-looked.

【42】**_Elizabeth W. Twamley and Mark W. Bondi_**

【43】**Demnentia refers to a syndrome of acquired cognitive impairment that is caused by cerebral dysfuriction and interferes with social or occupational functioning . The DSM-IV fur-ther defines dementia as a disorder characterized by disturbances of memory and at least one additional cognitive function (e.g.， language， praxis， gnosis， or executive function). Dementias are distinguished from pure amnestic disorders by the presence of these additional impair-ments. The cognitive deficits present in dementia must represent a significant decline from premorbid functioning and must resuIt in sig-nificant declines in activities of daily living (ADLs). Further， the deficits must occur in the absence of delirium. Multiple types of dementia are delineated in the DSM-IV， including Dementia of the Alzheimer's Type， Vascular Dementia， Dementias Due to HIV Disease， Head Traumna， Parkin-son’s Disease， Huntington’s Disease， Pick’s Disease， and Substance-induced Persisting Dementia. This chapter focuses on Alzheimer's Disease， Vascular Dementia， Parkinson’s Disease， Huntington’s Disease， Lewy Body Disease， Frontotemporal dementias (e.g.， Pick’s Disease) and Substance-Related dementias. These forms of dementia are those that most commonly require differential diagnosis.**

**Because dementia， by definition， includes memory impairment， we begin this chapter with a discussion of the discrete types of memory functions that are differentially affected by various dementing disor-ders. We then discuss the differential diagnosis of dementia from non-dementing conditions such as delirium， normal aging， mild cognitive|删除0换行|impairment， and depression， The aforementioned categories of deinen-tia are examined in detail. Finally， we conclude with recommendations regarding the process of differential diagnosis of dementia.**

【45】**DEMENTIA AND MEMORY**

【46】**Because memoryimpairment is a pivotal requirement for the diagnosis of any dementing disorder， an understanding of the many forms of memnory dysfuniction is helpful in differentiating the various types of dementias. A1a basic level， memory systems may be classified as declarative and non-declarative . Declarative memory also known as explicit memory， refers to knowledge of facts or events that can be consciously recalled and stated or declared. Declarative memory can be autobiographical and context-based (in which case it is labeled ebisodic) or fact-based . An exan-ple of episodic memory is the ability to recall events， such as where one attended high school and where one recently parked the car. Semantic memory includes memory for overlearned knowledge， such as word meanings or historical events； examples include knowledge that a dog is a four-legged animal and that President Keunedy was assassinated in 1963. Episodic and semantic memory may be differentially impaired in demen-tia， due to their neurobiologically distinct substrates . In contrast to the “knowing that" of declarative memory， n0n-declarative memory (also known as implicit memory) has been character~ized as an unconscious knowing how." Examples of non-declarative memory include knowing how to tie shoelaces and driving.**

【47】**It has been well estahlished that damage to the medial temporal lobe(i.e.， hippocampus and related structures) or midline diencephalic structures (i.e.， dorsal medial nucleus of the thalamus) produces deficits in declarative memory， but not in nor-declarative memory. The dissociation between declarative and non-declarative memory systems suggests that medial ternporal and diencephalic structures mediate declarative memory， whereas other brain regions are important for non-declarative memory. Further， the medial temporal lobe and midline diencephalic structures appear 1o subserve the ability to encode new episodic memories， but patients with damage to these regions display preserved semantic memory .**

A temporal gradi-ent may exist in retrograde amnesia， where older memories are relative-ly more preserved than more recent ones. 【51】**“CORTICAL”AND“SUBCORTICAL”PATTERNS OF PERFORMANCE**

【52】**Various dementias are associated with a wide range of neuropathologi-cal features， and it is generally acknowledged that patients with differ-ent types of dementias present with varied cognitive， behavioral， and affective disturbances . Further， most dement-ed patients do not consistently exhibit global cognitive impairments， but instead have areas of relative preservation. Patterns of cognitive strengths and weaknesses， along with affective and behavioral features， are important considerations in the differential diagnosis of dementia.**

【53】**One of the main distinctions drawn in the classification of dementing disorders has heen captured by the categories of“cortical"and “subcor-tical" dementia. Subcortical dementias (e.g.， Huntington’s disease， Parkinson’s disease， and subcortical vascular disease) are characterized by (1) moderate memory retrieval deficits (i.e.， recognition better than free recall abilities)， (2) slowed cognitive processing， (3) impairment in attention and working memory， (4) problem-soiving or executive deficits， and (5) personality or mood changes. Deficits in motor func-tions may also be present. These impairments have been contrasted with those seen in patients with cortical dementing processes (e.g.， Alzheimer’s disease)， which are characterized by (1) prominent memo-ry dysfunction， with poor recognition and recall， or rapid forgetting；(2) aphasic， apraxic， and/or agnostic disturbances； and (3) the relative absence of sensory and motor deficits . Although the cortical-subcortical distinction appears valid and useful， it has been crit-icized as being overly simplistic . Furthermore， it is well known that primarily subcortical diseases can affect cortical regions， and vice versa. Thus， recent research has attempied to relate specific cognitive impairments with specific dementing disorders. Below， we discuss the neuropsychological profiles associated with different types of dementia， along with associated emo-tional and behavioral features. With this background， we then describe the differentiation of dementia from non-dementing conditions.**

【54】**The prevalence of dementia increases with age： among those aged65-74，5-8% meet criteria for dementia. Among 75-84-year-olds， the rate increases to 15-20%； and among those over 85， 25-50% have dementia. We begin the discussion of various dementing disorders with a review of Alzheimer's disease， not only because it is the most con~mon cause of dementia， but also because it provides an exemplar of a dementing disorder to which other dementias can be compared. As we describe each type of dementia， we discuss the prevaience，etiology， and neuropathology of the disease. We then discuss the typical course of the disease process. Cognitive， emotional， and behavioral features associat-ed with the disease are then discussed in detail， with an emphasis on neuropsychological test profiles.**

【55】**ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE**

**Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia in the elderly， probably accounting for more than half of dementia cases|删除0换行|. The prevalence of the dis-ease is highly correlated with age， with prevalence at about 1% at age 65and doubling with every 4.4 years of age thereafter . Controversy exists， however， regarding the presence of a plateau in prevalence among the oldest old. According to DSM-IV criteria， when the onset of AD occurs before age 65， it is referred to as “early-onset" whereas onset after age 65 is considered “late onset." Life expectancy averages about 8-12 years fol-lowing diagnosis.**

【57】**Risk factors for AD include older age， family history of deinentia， female gender， history of head injury and presence of the apolipopro-tein E-E4 allele (ApoE-e4). Biological markers of AD involve neuronal atrophy， synaptic loss， and neuritic plaques and neurofibrillary tangles within multiple cortical regions ； the diagnosis of AD can only be made following histopathologic confir-mation of these markers. The hippocampus and entorhinal cortex appear to be involved early in the course of the diseasc， with frontal， temporal， and parietal association regions increasingly affected with its progression . Primary motor and sensory cortices and subcortical structures are typically spared， but degeneration does occur in the basal forebrain (e.g.， the nucleus basalis of Meynert)， which leads to deficient levels of the neuro-transmitter acetylcholine . AD is characterized by a slow， insidious onset and gradual cognitive decline. Earlier-onset AD (i.e.， before age 60) is associated with genetic causes such as the ainyloid precursor protein (APP) mutation on chromosome 21 and the presenilin gene mutations on chromosomes l and 14 . Table 8.1 presents the NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for definite， probable， and possible AD.**

【58】**The cognitive deficits assuciated with AD are related to hippocampal and cortical damage and include impairments in the following areas：(1) memory function (e.g.， amnesia characterized by rapid forgetting)，(2) language functioning and loss of semantic knowledge (e.g.，anomia and aphasia)， (3) visuospatial functiuning (e.g.， constructional apraxia)， and (4) executive functioning (i.e. divided attention， sustained atten-tion， processing speed， initiation， sequencing， set-shifting， cognitive flexi-bility， planning) and abstract reasoning . Because memory dys function is the hallmark feature of AD， we will begin by describing the memory deficits that accompany the disease.**

【20】### Pathologic Features

【21】#### Macroscopic Pathology

【22】There are no specific gross alterations. Cysts may be observed if there is accompanying cystic change of ducts and ductules. Grittiness related to calcifications can be present when the tissue is sliced.

【23】#### Microscopic Pathology

【24】Histologically, columnar cell change features mild dilatation of terminal ducts and ductules surrounded by a loose stroma, which may appear slightly cellular. Lining epithelial cells disclose columnar shapes with vertical axes exceeding their widths, set perpendicularly to the underlying basement membranes. Nuclei are ovoid or elongated and are also oriented along the vertical plane. Apical snouts, luminal secretions, and calcifications are often present. Columnar cell hyperplasia shows multiple layers of columnar epithelial cells, leading to an irregular, ruffled luminal contour, often with a micropapillary or mound-like appearance.

【25】In flat epithelial atypia, epithelial cells become more cuboidal in shape, with slightly enlarged, rounded, vesicular nuclei that have discernible but usually small nucleoli. Because of cellular uniformity and monotony, the luminal surface appears relatively flat and rigid at low magnification. Additionally, there is a darker appearance that is due to increased nuclear–cytoplasmic ratios. As in columnar cell change, luminal secretions and calcifications are frequently present. By definition, if architectural atypia is observed in such a lesion, it should be classified as ADH. 【44】Atypical Ductal Hyperplasia
---------------------------

【45】### Definition

【46】Atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) is a clonal proliferation of monomorphic epithelial cells involving the terminal ductal lobular unit, with architectural atypia constituted by cribriform, micropapillary, papillary, and solid morphologies. Patients with ADH harbour a risk of subsequent breast cancer development that is three to five times greater than in the general population.

【47】### Clinical and Epidemiological Features

【48】As ADH is a microscopic lesion, it is almost always asymptomatic, but it can be associated with calcifications or accompany other lesions such as cystic changes, so the presentation may be through mammographic detection of, or symptoms from, associated lesions.

【49】### Imaging Features

【50】Clustered microcalcifications that are often indistinct and amorphous in morphology can be seen on mammography. The microcalcifications may also appear pleomorphic and indistinguishable from those observed in DCIS. ADH does not have any characteristic features on sonography, but it may occasionally involve underlying conditions like intraductal papillomas or fibroadenomas. ADH is often an incidental finding from biopsy for other lesions. There is no specific MRI morphology for ADH. It can be found as enhancing masses or non-mass enhancing lesions (likely related to accompanying lesions) that are focal, linear, or regional in distribution, with no reliable MR imaging features to predict upgrade.

【51】### Pathologic Features

【52】#### Macroscopic Pathology

【53】No specific macroscopic changes are present, apart from accompanying cystic changes and grittiness due to associated calcifications.

【54】#### Microscopic Pathology

【55】ADH resembles low nuclear grade DCIS, but it is a more limited lesion, which measures 2 mm or less, or only partially involves ducts. A useful histological guide is that ADH is diagnosed only when low nuclear grade DCIS is being seriously considered. Cytologically, ADH shows monomorphic, low-grade nuclei in atypical architectural formations. Calcifications may be observed .

【62】### Differential Diagnosis

【63】#### UDH Versus ADH

【64】Florid UDH should not be classified as ADH. In florid UDH, a heterogeneous population of epithelial cells fills and effaces the ductal lumen. Nuclear overlapping and variability, streaming, and slit-like spaces are present in florid UDH. In contrast, ADH shows a homogeneous epithelial population with rigid architectural patterns.

【65】#### ADH Versus Low Nuclear Grade DCIS

【66】Quantitative criteria are used to distinguish ADH from low nuclear grade DCIS, as the epithelial cells of these two lesions are qualitatively similar. ADH is a small, usually focal lesion, either partially involving ducts or completely involving ducts but measuring only up to 2 mm in maximal extent. A similar lesion measuring more than 2 mm may be diagnosed as low nuclear grade DCIS. Although the size criterion appears objective and is widely used, it is acknowledged that this cutoff is arbitrary, intended to avoid overtreatment of small, focal, low-grade lesions. The WHO working group also accepts the approach of using two or more membrane-bound spaces involved by a monotonous neoplastic population to define low-grade DCIS, with lesions below this threshold regarded as ADH 通用删除6(英):<u>\[ 8 \]</u>. As both ADH and low nuclear grade DCIS are composed of a similar clonal cell population, immunohistochemical panels are unable to distinguish these lesions.

【67】#### ADH Versus Collagenous Spherulosis

【68】ADH with a cribriform pattern may mimic collagenous spherulosis . In collagenous spherulosis, however, the cribriform spaces are pseudolumens rimmed by myoepithelial cells, whereas the true lumens of ADH are surrounded by neoplastic epithelial cells. Also, ADH shows a uniform population of ER-positive epithelial cells, whereas collagenous spherulosis features a mixed population of both luminal and myoepithelial cells.

【71】### Prognosis and Therapy Considerations

【72】With ADH, the risk of subsequent breast cancer is three to five times higher than the risk for the general population, and the risk applies to both breasts. Women with ADH are subjected to high-risk screening and in some cases risk reduction with anti-oestrogen therapy. If ADH is discovered on core biopsy, an excision is usually performed to exclude a larger lesion that would warrant a diagnosis of DCIS.

【73】Ductal Carcinoma In Situ

【74】### Definition

【75】Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) is a non-invasive malignant epithelial cell proliferation that is confined within the basement membranes, arising in the terminal ductal lobular unit, with cytological atypia that ranges from mild to marked in severity. DCIS is a non-obligate precursor to most invasive breast carcinomas.

【76】### Clinical and Epidemiological Features

【77】With the advent of mammographic screening, the incidence of DCIS has increased tremendously in recent decades, as many cases are associated with calcifications that are radiologically detected. Currently, DCIS accounts for 25–30 % of all newly detected breast cancers. Occasionally, DCIS may present symptomatically as a mass, nipple discharge, or nipple erosion (Paget disease) .

【0】toms emerge once a critical amount of iron has accumulated in the target organs.

【1】McLeod syndrome  is an X-linked disorder which characteristically presents in middle-aged men ， although it may be detected at a younger age if blood typing is performed or serological tests demonstrate elevated levels of creatine kinase or liver enzymes. Occasionally， carrier females have been symptomatic， presumably due to X-chromosome inactivation .

【2】**Late Adult Onset**

【3】Elderly patients who develop chorea should be thoroughly evaluated for a neoplas-tic syndrome or for an autoimmune disorder， especially if female . In the absence of these， HD should be considered a possible diagnosis. Late onset is often associated with CAG repeats in the borderline range， where penetrance is reduced； but instability and expansion with vertical transmission are likely， raising genetic counseling issues. If HD has been excluded， other genetic etiologies may be consid-ered， including HDL2， which can present at later ages with lower pathological repeat sizes . The entity of“senile chorea"is obsolete as these cases are now recognized as most probably being due to late onset of genetic disorders.

【4】**Disease Progression**

【5】**Acute Onset**

【6】As with all neurological disorders， details of disease progression are strongly suggestive of the nature of the diagnosis. Sudden onset of chorea which does not progress indicates a vascular event， either ischemic or hemorrhagic .

【7】Sudden onset of chorea related to medical illness suggests a causal relationship such as a metabolic ， postinfectious， or autoimmune 

删除5:<u>**I. INTRODUCTION**</u>|删除换行|etiology. However， the pediatric inherited metabolic disorders may be unmasked by stresses such as fever， illness， and trauma ， confounding the diagnosis.

【9】A common type of sudden-onset chorea in childhood is Sydenham chorea， seen following a streptococcal throat infection . Cases usually resolve after a few weeks， but symptoms may be debilitating.

【10】**Subacute Onset**

【11】Development of chorea over days to weeks may suggest a metabolic process， such as nonketotic hyperglycemia in a non-insulin-dependent dia-betic patient， although these patients can present quite acutely. Other metabolic disorders which present with this time frame include a range of electrolyte distur-bances such as hyper-  and hyponatremia ， hyper- and hypocalcemia ， or hypomagnesemia.

【12】Endocrine abnormalities related to thyroid or parathyroid disease may cause chorea ， specifically hyperthyroidism . Hypo- and hyperparathyroidism have also been associated with chorea， which may be paroxysmal，likely due to distur-bances of calcium .

【13】A subacute presentation may be seen with prion diseases， specifically new vari-ant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease， related to bovine spongiform encephalopathy ， or with slowly grow-ing mass lesions .

【14】A similar time course can be seen with paraneoplastic syndromes   and has been reported with a variety of tumors， including renal， small cell lung， breast， and Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lym-phoma. The causative autoantibodies include anti-CRMP-5/CV2 ， anti-Hu ， anti-Yo ， anti-NMDA receptor， and others.

【15】**Chronic Progressive Course**

【16】A slow disease course， progressing over a number of years， particularly when accompanied by cognitive or psychiatric findings， is likely to indicate a neurode-generative process， for example， due to HD ， the AD inherited ataxias， a neuroacanthocytosis syndrome (Chapters 6，7)， or a neurodegen-eration with iron accumulation syndrome (Chapters 8-10).

【17】**Chronic Stable Chorea**

Choreiform movements which develop gradually but do not progress can some-times be attributed to use of a medication. either as a direct side effect or as a tardive syndrome . Benign hereditary chorea  should also|删除0换行|be considered， particularly if there is childhood onset and an AD family history. This condition is due to mutations of thyroid transcription factor 1 (TITF-1)， also known as NKX2.1， although it may be genetically heterogeneous. The chorea may respond to L-dopa .

【19】A similar， relatively stable， temporal presentation may also be due to auto-immune processes， as in lupus ， Sjogren syndrome ， and antiphospholipid antibody syn-drome .

【20】**Episodic Chorea**

【21】The paroxysmal hyperkinetic disorders are more typically dystonic in nature， and thus， they have been classified with the genetic dystonias， although chorea can be a component . The diagnosis of these disorders was previously based upon their phenomenology and precipitating factors， but this is being replaced by molecular identification. Many appear to be due to mutations of ion channels and to respond to anticonvulsants. More rarely， episodic chorea may be psychogenic in etiology .

【22】Paroxysmal nonkinesigenic dyskinesia (paroxysmal dystonic choreoathetosis， DYT8) is due to a mutation of the myofibrillogenesis regulator gene located at2q33 ， which may be involved in detoxifying alcohol and caffeine . Episodes of dystonia and/or chorea typically occur at rest and may be precipitated by alcohol， caffeine， stress， extremes of temperature， fatigue， or fasting. Episodes are much less frequent than those of paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia， and only a few may occur in a month； but they tend to be more long-lasting and severe.

【23】Paroxysmal choreoathetosis with spasticity (DYT9) has been localized to1p.21-p13.3 . Episodes in these patients were precipitated by exercise， stress， alcohol consumption， and sleep deprivation and consisted of dystonia， choreoatherosis， and dysarthria. Spasticity also occurs and can persist between attacks.

【24】Paroxysmal kinesigenic dyskinesia (PKD； paroxysmal kinesigenic dystonia， DYT10) of childhood onset may be familial or sporadic and is characterized by very frequent， brief episodes of limb dystonia following movement. Episodes often resolve with age. Treatment with anticonvulsants is usually beneficial， sug-gesting a channelopathy. Other cases are associated with features such as seizures and have been termed“benign infantile convulsions and paroxysmal choreoathetosis”.

【25】Paroxysmal exertional dyskinesia (DYT18) is an intermediate form with invol-untary movements developing following more prolonged exertion than PKD， which can last from minutes to hours. This syndrome is one of several neurological

删除5:<u>**I. INTRODUCTION**</u>|删除换行|conditions， including seizures， due to mutations of the glucose transporter GLUT1.

【27】Patients with episodic ataxia 1 may sometimes manifest choreoathetosis during ataxic episodes . More typical features are dysarthria and persistent myokymia . Treatment with acetazolamide can be helpful.

【28】**Medical History**

【29】The medical history may be informative in the patient with chorea. In pediatric cases nonneurological features can be very helpful in indicating a specific inher-ited metabolic disorder .

【30】Patients with endocrine disorders， especially diabetic patients with nonketotic hyperglycemia ， and autoimmune disorders  may develop chorea， in some cases as the presenting symptom. Patients with aceruloplasmin-emia typically have diabetes mellitus due to deposition of iron in the pancreas. One-third of patients with Friedreich ataxia also develop diabetes， which is thought to be due to mitochondrial dysfunction .

【31】Women of childbearing age should be evaluated for pregnancy (chorea gravi-darum) or may develop chorea related to estrogen-/progesterone-containing med-ications . Hormone replacement therapy may similarly be responsible， possibly due to sensitization of dopamine receptors by estrogens. However， contradictorily， suppression of estrogen with luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone may also result in chorea .

【32】The gene identified as causing benign hereditary chorea has been reported as part of a multisystem disorder due to a mutation of the gene TITF-I ， which causes congenital hypothyroidism， hypotonia， and pulmonary problems. Correction of the hypothyroidism did not prevent development of the other features， including the chorea， suggesting that these were primary effects of the mutation rather than secondary to the hypothyroidism. Differences in the mutations in these two disorders may account for the varying severity.

【33】Polycythemia vera may be a cause of chorea ， although it is unclear whether this is due to the presence of autoantibodies or to hyperviscosity resulting in basal ganglia ischemia.

【34】Celiac disease has been associated with a number of neurological complica-tions， most likely due to an autoimmune mechanism. Chorea may occasionally respond to a gluten-free diet .

Patients with hepatic disease and chorea should be evaluated for the only treat-able genetic movement disorder， Wilson disease. Chorea may occasionally be seen|删除0换行| but is not commonly reported as a presenting symptom. More typically， there is an asymmetric， coarse flapping tremor present at rest， with posture holding or with action. Dystonia， parkinsonism， and ataxia can be seen. A thorough evaluation is required， including ophthalmological slit-lamp examina-tion. It is unusual for patients to present with neurological disease in the absence of hepatic findings. Ceruloplasmin levels are typically decreased but may be deceptively raised as it is an acute-phase reactant. Twenty-four-hour copper excretion is elevated. Rarely， Kayser-Fleischer rings may be absent in late-onset disease . If ceruloplasmin and 24-hour copper excretion are normal， hepatosplenomegaly in a patient with chorea suggests a neuroacantho-cytosis syndrome， either ChAc  or McLeod syndrome  . Liver dis-ease due to a variety of etiologies may also cause acquired hepatocerebral degeneration， likely due to manganese deposition in the basal ganglia， which may be seen in brain MRI.

【36】A condition of poorly-defined etiology known as “post-pump chorea”may occur in children after undergoing open-heart surgery or cardiopulmonary bypass. This may be due to microemboli or a hyperviscosity syndrome and appears to reduce in incidence with improvements in technology and experience  .

【37】Cardiac disease， specifically cardiomyopathy， is frequently found in Friedreich ataxia . Similar findings， along with arrhythmias， are seen in McLeod syndrome .

【38】In children with acute onset of chorea， evaluation for a recent upper respiratory tract infection by streptococcus group A， in consideration of Sydenham chorea， is essential. However， much more rarely， striatal necrosis may occur as a complication of measles encephalitis  or following undefined febrile illness . A similar picture can be seen after Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection ， with a mixture of chorea and dystonia， hyperreflexia， and encephalopathy. Chorea has also been reported in the setting of encephalopathy due to parvoviral infection  and following herpes simplex encephalitis .

【39】Abnormal susceptibility to infection and a predilection to develop cancers is seen in AT . The gene for chronic granulomatous disease is adjacent to the gene for McLeod syndrome on the X chromosome. With improved thera-pies for the chronic， recurrent infections to which these boys are susceptible， it is likely that some of them with large X-chromosome deletions could later develop McLeod syndrome.

【40】A variety of movement disorders including chorea have been associated with human immunodeficiency viral (HIV) infection . Sometimes these are due to a mass lesion， such as lymphoma or abscess ， whereas

删除5:<u>**I. INTRODUCTION**</u>|删除换行|in other cases they may be a direct result of HIV encephalopathy .

【42】Chorea has been reported following correction of hyponatremia causing central pontine myelinolysis .

【43】Medical findings suggestive of cancer， such as weight loss， lymphadenopathy， chronic cough， and change in bowel habit， may be indicative of a paraneoplastic syndrome ， although the absence of these does not rule out this diag-nosis as tumor growth may be suppressed by the autoantibodies which are respon-sible for the paraneoplastic syndromes.

【44】**Medication and Drug Use**

【45】A number of medications may cause chorea ， either as a direct， and often predictable， function of their action， as seen following L-dopa in Parkinson disease， or as a side effect.

【46】The effects of specific medications may suggest a relationship to the patho-physiology of chorea in other conditions， as information from animal models of L-dopa-induced dyskinesias may be used to further our understanding of mecha-nisms in other hyperkinetic disorders. The etiology of L-dopa-induced dyskine-sias in Parkinson disease， namely， an increase in dopaminergic stimulation within the putamen， can be inferred from the relationship to dosing with dopaminergic medications. However， to date， alterations have been observed in a large number of parameters related to different neurotransmitters involved in striatal function-ing， and agents with a variety of mechanisms of actions have been reported to reduce dyskinesias in animal models .

【47】Tardive dyskinesia (TD) is more accurately described as “chorea”and appears after an interval of 3 months following the initiation of a dopamine-blocking med-ication . In addition to the classic neuroleptics， TD has been reported with the atypical antipsychotics， including risperidone  and olanzapine . The newer agents quetiapine， clozapine， aripiprazole， and ziprasidone may occasionally cause TD. Other dopaminergic antagonists， such as compazine and metoclopramide， may also be responsible.

【48】The timing of the emergence of the symptoms and the fact that TD often does not resolve (and may even worsen) with discontinuation of the medication make it hard to confirm or refute the association of other medications with this disorder， but selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)， lithium， and anticonvulsant medications have also been implicated.

【49】Chorea may be seen as a direct side effect of other medications， including gabapentin ， lamotrigine ， and lithium .

【50】Stimulants in particular， including those used therapeutically  as well as those used recreationally， such as amphetamine， cocaine， and specifi-cally “crack”cocaine， may result in chorea (“crack-dancing"). The mechanism of action of these agents， namely the release of dopamine， is probably the explana-tion for the appearance of the movement disorder. Usually the timing and the resolution of the movements with discontinuation of the offending agent make the diagnosis and treatment straightforward.

【51】**ASSOCIATED NEUROLOGICAL FEATURES**

【52】**Distribution of Chorea**

【53】Chorea typically looks identical regardless of the etiology. The exceptions to this are when the facial and lingual muscles are markedly involved or when there is asymmetric involvement of the limbs.

【54】Facial muscles alone are most commonly affected in neuroleptic-induced TD. Prominent orofacial and lingual involvement can be seen in ChAc and PKAN. In ChAc the tongue movements are dystonic and specifically induced by eating.

【55】Structural lesions are a common cause of unilateral chorea in adults， often due to a focal lesion involving the basal ganglia . Another cause may be non-ketotic hyperglycemia， which is typically unilateral， for unknown reasons.

【56】**Peripheral Neuropathy**

【57】Hyporeflexia and peripheral sensory changes suggestive of a peripheral neuro-pathic process are characteristic of the two core neuroacanthocytosis syndromes， ChAc  and McLeod syndrome. The other disorders in which peripheral neuropathy may be present in addition to chorea are some of the inherited ataxias， both AR  and AD  .

【58】**Hyperreflexia**

【59】Hyperreflexia is seen in neurodegenerative disorders in which the cortex is also affected， for example， HD， HDL2， and the SCAs. Reflex asymmetry may serve to localize a focal lesion.

【60】删除5:<u>**I. INTRODUCTION**</u>

【61】**Ataxia**

【62】Ataxia and abnormal eye movements also suggest the inherited ataxias， which may be both AD and AR in inheritance . Ataxia and hyperreflexia suggest SCA17  and DRPLA. However， the phenotype may be remark-ably variable， both within and between families， and ataxia may be absent.

【63】**Cognitive and Psychiatric Symptoms**

【64】Neurodegenerative causes of chorea are frequently associated with personality changes， subcortical dementia， and frank psychiatric disease . This may be due to degenerative processes affecting the frontal cortex but also to involvement of the caudate nucleus in cortical-subcortical loops. These findings are being increasingly recognized as harbingers of frank neurological disease and can often be detected even when subtle by detailed neuropsychological testing.

【65】The use of neuroleptics for psychiatric symptoms preceding the appearance of a movement disorder may mask the diagnosis as neurological signs and symptoms may be erroneously attributed to the medication. Psychiatrists should be attuned to any atypical features of either psychiatric or neurological presentations.

【66】**Ophthalmological Findings**

【67】Abnormal eye movements are found in chorea of a variety of etiologies，including HD and ChAc， with intrusions of square-wave jerks. Impaired smooth pursuit and saccadic gaze， or ophthalmoplegia， may suggest a cerebellar disorder .

【68】Pigmentary retinopathy is indicative of PKAN and is an invariable feature of typical (young-onset) disease . The characteristic telangiectactic blood vessels seen in the conjunctivae of the eye may be helpful in making the diagnosis of AT but may be absent in atypical， late-onset disease .

【69】Other localophthalmologicalfindings mayindicate autoimmune disease.

【70】**Seizures**

【71】Seizures are seen in approximately 50% of patients with a neuroacanthocytosis syndrome (Chapters 6， 7). These can predate the appearance of the movement disorder by several years. Seizures can also be present in young-onset HD， although these patients tend to have an akinetic-rigid phenotype rather than chorea. Younger-onset patients with DRPLA tend to present with seizures， although in these cases chorea is less prominent than ataxia . Older-onset patients with chorea may develop seizures later in the disease course.

【72】**Myoclonus**

【73】Myoclonus is a frequent finding in prion diseases  and in DRPLA affecting younger patients.

【74】**DIAGNOSTIC TESTS**

【75】**Neuroimaging**

【76】Patients with chorea should always undergo neuroimaging， ideally brain MRI， preferably with contrast to exclude the presence of a space-occupying lesion. Vascular etiologies may include stroke， vasculitides， moya-moya disease， cavernous angioma， and arteriovenouss malformation . Rarely， movement disorders， including chorea， may be seen in multiple sclerosis.

【77】Atrophy of the head of the caudate nucleus is seen in the basal ganglia neuro-degenerative disorders and is usually interpreted as being consistent with a diag-nosis of HD， although this finding is not specific to this genetic cause.

【78】The basal ganglia， and particularly the globus pallidus， are vulnerable to min-eral deposition， probably due to high metabolic demands. The neuroradiological finding of calcium deposition in the brain， known as Fahr disease， may cause a variety of movement disorders， including chorea， dystonia， and parkinsonism， in addition to ataxia， cognitive impairment， and behavioral changes. The movement disorder may be due to the structural lesion caused by calcium deposition in the putamen  but could also be attributable to metabolic effects upon neurotransmission . The term “Fahr disease”is nonspecific and describes a number of different disorders， including those of calcium and mito-chondrial metabolism. In one family， with idiopathic basal ganglia calcification(IBGC)， linkage was demonstrated to 14q (IBGC1) ， although the gene has not yet been identified. In several other families with AD inheritance， linkage to this locus was excluded . In other families the pattern of inheritance and additional clinical features suggest mitochondrial inheritance .

【3】##### Discussion

【4】This patient had subacute/chronic, fluctuating symmetric proximal weakness with areflexia and normal sensory examination. The diagnoses suspected by the referring physician may fit with this pattern; for instance, non-amyotrophic lateral sclerosis motor neuron diseases, such as Kennedy's or adult-onset spinal muscular atrophies. Immune motor neuropathies usually present with distal, asymmetric rather than symmetric proximal weakness. Symmetric proximal weakness is the classic pattern in several myopathies, but reflexes are usually lost in proportion to the degree of weakness, and one would not expect loss of ankle reflexes with strong gastrocnemius muscles. Clues to the correct diagnosis include several details in the history (dry mouth, erectile dysfunction indicating autonomic involvement, weight loss and smoking history indicating possible malignancy, fluctuating nature of the weakness indicating possible disease of the neuromuscular junction) and the physical examination (facilitation of reflexes after brief exercise), all pointing to Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS). Electrodiagnosis is critical for the confirmation of the suspected diagnosis. The characteristic finding is small CMAP amplitudes that increase in size (facilitate) with 30 Hz repetitive nerve stimulation (RNS) or after sustained muscle contraction for 10 seconds. In our patient, CMAP increment of > 200% was noted after brief isometric exercise. Repetitive nerve stimulation at 2 Hz produced a significant (> 10%) decrement, another characteristic finding. Voltage-gated calcium channel antibodies were positive from serum. Computerized tomography (CT) of the chest and positron emission tomography (PET) scan were negative for malignancy, but because of the high index of clinical suspicion, they should be repeated at 6–12 month intervals. Note that about 60% of LEMS are paraneoplastic, with small-cell lung cancer being the most common malignancy. The remaining 40% are likely immune mediated and usually occur in younger patients without underlying malignancy; they may be associated with other autoimmune diseases .

【16】#### Introduction

【17】The cavernous sinus syndrome is defined by the presence of multiple cranial neuropathies as the result of involvement/compression of cranial nerves within the cavernous sinus (CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI).

【18】#### Cavernous sinus anatomy

【19】The cavernous sinus is the collection of venous plexi within the two layers of skullbase dura and is bordered by temporal bone inferiorly, the sella turcica medially, and the sphenoid wind anteriorly. The carotid arteries on each side pass through the cavernous sinus on each side forming the carotid siphon. Five cranial nerves are located lateral to the carotid artery within the cavernous sinus. Those include, superior to inferior: cranial nerves III, IV, and VI (innervate the eye muscles, and parasympathetics for CN III). Additionally autonomic sympathetic fibers surround the carotid artery on the way to the orbit as well as CN V branches (V1 and V2).

【20】#### Case vignette (pituitary apoplexy)

【21】A 64-year-old male presented with 24 hours of acute onset subtle confusion, headache, nausea, and inability to see out of the right eye. The vital signs were significant for hypotension (ultimately deemed to be secondary to hypocortisolemia) and low-grade fever. On neurologic examination, the patient was verbalizing but disoriented to place. On cranial nerve exam, the right eye was deviated laterally and down with ptosis (eyelid drooping) and he could not move it medially (CN III and IV palsies). On visual exam, he had some light perception but was unable to count fingers out of the right eye and had a temporal visual field loss out of the left eye. He also had a right afferent pupillary defect (decreased pupillary response to light).

【22】Computerized tomography (CT) of the head showed a lesion suggestive of a pituitary macroadenoma with evidence of hemorrhage. The patient was started on stress-dose hydrocortisone. Pituitary protocol magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was consistent with hemorrhagic pituitary macroadenoma with cavernous sinus invasion on the right and suprasellar extension with right optic nerve and chiasmal compression. Endocrine work-up revealed panhypopituitarism. The patient was taken for urgent surgical decompression. An endoscopic trans-sphenoidal adenomectomy was performed. Some visual improvement was noticed on postoperative day two. At 3-month follow-up, the vision has further improved, with near complete ophthalmoplegia resolution. The patient continued hormonal replacement.

【35】#### Introduction

【36】The seventh cranial nerve or facial nerve originates in the pons. The major function of the facial nerve is control of the muscles of facial expression. It also innervates the stapedius muscle in the middle ear. Dysfunction of the stapedius muscle results in hyperacusis. The facial nerve also provides parasympathetic innervation to the salivary glands and taste sensation to the anterior two thirds of the tongue.

【37】Facial nerve palsy can be the result of supranuclear, nuclear, or infranuclear dysfunction. Supranuclear lesions of the facial nerve affect motor function of the lower two thirds of the face sparing the frontalis (which is bilaterally innervated). Hyperacusis and impaired lacrimation and taste which occur in nuclear and infranuclear lesions are lacking in supranuclear lesions. With brainstem processes, there can be accompanying long tract signs and gaze palsies. Nuclear lesions of the facial nerve are the result of disease processes occurring in the brainstem (pons and medulla). Infranuclear lesions are usually due to injury in the subarachnoid space, skull base, and distally. In cases of nuclear and infranuclear dysfunction, other usually proximally located cranial nerves can be involved.

【38】The differential diagnosis in Table 88.1 focuses on nuclear and infranuclear etiologies.

【10】Decrease of social contacts， emotional impoverishment， early decrease of criti-cism， and lack of insight can be defined as cardinal symptoms of the behav-ioral variant of FTD. On a behavioral level， conspicuousSbehavior. disinhibition in social interaction， loss of interest (e.g.， in self-care)， and risky decision making characterize the disease. bvFTD is caused by different neuro-pathological pathways but may be related to focused loss of two specific cells types of the brain： the von Economo and the fork cells (discussed later).

【11】**Neuropsychological testing of patients with bvFTD should encompass prefrontal lobe functions sensitive tests (e.g.， working memory and flexibility of the TAP)， the RMET， Picture arrangement of the WIE， and the NPI answered by close friends or relatives. Tests for affective empathy and the object alternation task are especially sensitive in the early stages of bvFTD. Patients with bvFTD exhibit declined performance on tests assessing cogni-tive empathy and executive functions but not so much in the very early phase of their disease process. Standardneuropsychological tests such as the CERAD-NAB and the DemTect are not effective for a differential diagnosis of bvFTD.**

【12】Apart from the core set of tests， the neuropsychological differential diag-nosis of bvFTD should include at least two social perception or understand-ing tasks and the“RMET” has proven to be sensitive and of prognostic value. Patients with bvFTD suffer from emotion recognition deficits and these concern negative emotions more than positive emotions. On a cognitive level the object alternation (termed flexibility) task of the TAP should be used for the assessment. If there is any indication for bvFTD， the NPI should be answered by a relative of the patient. Changes in eating behavior and in irritability， disinhibition， and distraction are of major interest. Moreover the clinical observation should look for signs of prehension behavior and the anamnesis and increasing tension in the relationship not only related to increase irritability but also to a loss of affective empathy.

【13】**The neuroradiological assessment of the patients might show atrophy in the insular and the anterior cingulate and ventromedial prefrontal cortex； however， the diagnosis cannot be based on MRI scanning. There may be an increase level of total tau and phosphor-tau in bvFTD patients. Unfortunately this is not always the case. Therefore the diagnosis primarily depends on the clinical assessment.**

**Up to now there is no specific treatment for bvFTD neither on a func-tional nor on a pharmacological level. Serotonergic modulation might have the potential for symptom modulation (reducing disinhibition in the patients)， but there is no large-scale RCT to show that on a high level of evidence. In any case relatives of bvFTD should be offered professional education on how to deal with their affected family|删除0换行|members， because their behavior leads to severe losses of quality of live and often poses the question how to respond correctly. 【57】The mnemonic PINT will help to recall the causes of nightmares.

【58】**P-Psychiatric causes include anxiety， neurosis， and the various psychoses.**

【59】**I-Inflammation prompts the recall of nightmares associ-ated with systemic infections， and intoxication brings to mind the nightmares due to alcohol and drugs such as the benzodiazepines.**

【62】**Approach to the Diagnosis**

【63】If an infectious disease is suspected， a CBC， sedimentation rate， and chemistry panel should be done. Alcohol- or drug-induced nightmares may be diagnosed by the history and a drug screen. The history should also be useful in cases of head injury， especially when questioning the family or closely associated persons. If epilepsy is suspected， a wake-and-sleep electroencephalogram should be ordered； a trial of anticonvulsants may be necessary to rule out epilepsy. It may be useful to order a psychiatric consult early in the evaluation.

【64】**NOCTURIA**

【65】The differential diagnosis of nocturia is similar to that of polyuria. A pathophysiologic analysis of the symptoms would indicate that the patient is producing excessive urine at night， there is an obstruction to the output of urine so that the bladder cannot be emptied fully on one voiding， or there is an irritative focus in the urinary tract stimulating the patient to urinate more frequently.

【66】1\. Excessive urine production at night： This category includes all the causes of polyuria： diabetes insipidus， diabetes mellitus， hyperthyroidism， diuretic drugs， nephrogenic diabetes insipidus， and chronic nephritis. In addition， the one condition that produces exces-sive urine output almost exclusively at night—conges-tive heart failure—must be considered. In heart failure， edema accumulates in the extremities during the day while the patient is in the upright position and is returned to the circulation and poured out through the kidneys at night while the patient is in the recumbent position.

【67】2.Obstructive uropathy： Bladder neck obstruction by a calculus， enlarged or inflamed prostate， median bar hypertrophy， or urethral stricture is a condition to con-sider here. Neurogenic bladder from poliomyelitis， mul-tiple sclerosis， and other spinal cord diseases must also be considered.

【68】3\. Irritative focus in the urinary tract： Nocturia may result from inflammation of the bladder， prostate， ure-thra， and kidney on this basis. Occasionally a bladder tumor or prostate carcinoma may be the irritative focus. Inflammation of the vagina， fallopian tubes， and rectum are also occasionally responsible.

【69】**Approach to the Diagnosis**

【3】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【6】Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (WM). LPL is morpho-logically heterogeneous and can be indistinguishable from marginal zone lymphoma. It shows white and red pulp involvement by small lymphocytes， lymphoplasmacytic cells， and mature plasma cells. Follicles may be present and are often regressed. Typical SMZL biphasic pattern or monocytoid features are not seen in LPL. The serum mono-clonal protein is higher in LPL/WM than in SMZL (2.0 and0.95 g/dL， respectively) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[51\]</u>. In the BM， SMZL shows either a nodular or more often an intrasinusoidal pattern of involvement， whereas LPL/WM usually shows an intersti-tial and/or a paratrabecular pattern.

【7】T-cell lymphoproliferative disorders， such as T-cell pro-lymphocytic leukemia (T-PLL)， may have dense red pulp infiltration. Rare composite lymphomas of the spleen (e.g.， SMZL and MCL) have been reported. CLL/SLL and FL are distinguished by specific phenotype (CD5/CD23 and CD10/BCL6 expression， respectively).

【8】SDRPL is characterized by predominantly red pulp involvement by _a_ monomorphic population oof small lymphocytes. The phenotype and cytology are similar to those ofSMZL (CD5-/CD10-/BCL2+/CD23-/DBA44+/CDllc+/annexin-A1-/CD43-). Many cases are CD103+，remi-niscent to HCL-V. 【9】Since most of the disease-related deaths in SMZL are associated with transformation to DLBCL， sample has to be carefully analyzed for the number of large lymphoid cells and patients have to be followed to exclude large cell trans-formation. 【11】**HCL VARIANT**

HCL-V (CD103+/CD25-HCL) is a rare B-cell disorder that accounts for ~10% of HCL cases and presents with splenomegaly， lymphocytosis， _and_ cytopeniaswithout monocytopenia. Patients have indolent course with a long survival time. Treatment with Rituxan and anti-CD22 immunotoxin is highly effective. It shares more similarities with SMZL (splenic lymphoma with villous lymphocytes) and SDRPL than with HCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[52\]</u>. HCL-V differs from typical HCL by worse prognosis and poor response to interferon alpha and purine analogs， cladribine or pentostatin. New agents， such as rituximab and BL22 (anti-CD22 immunotoxin)， are actively being evalu-ated and show promising results in both classical HCL and CD25-variant.**

【15】Cytologically， the leukemic cells are characterized by an abundant basophilic cytoplasm with villous projections， regular nuclear borders， and prominent nucleolus (features intermediate between hairy cells or prolymphocytes).

【16】**BM Core Biopsy**

【17】**The pattern of BM involvement is more reminiscent of SMZL with mild infiltrate (predominantly intrasinusoidal) and a good hematopoietic reserve 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12\]</u>. Some cases show a mixture of intrasinusoidal and interstitial patterns and rarely a nodular pattern or a prominent diffuse infiltrate. Paratrabecular marrow involvement is not reported in HCL-V.**

【18】**Spleen**

【19】**In the spleen， the infiltrate involves the red pulp with morphologic features overlapping with SDRPL and HCL.**

【20】**Immunophenotype**

【21】The immunophenotype shows a mature B-cell phenotype with expression of B-cell antigens， CDlle， and CD103， but unlike typical HCL， the cells are negative for CD25 and annexin-1 (some cases may show faint CD25 expression， but never bright as seen in HCL). HCL and HCL-V rarely show abnor-mal karyotype \[e.g.， del(17p)， +12\]， whereas SMZL has abnormal karyotype in 80% \[+3， +18， de(17q)\] and SDRPL in ~30% of cases \[+3， del(7q)\]. It is suggested that SMZL，**

【24】HCL-V， and SDRPL may represent the overlapping enti-ties. HCL shows bright CD20， CD22， CD11c， and CD123expression， and is always positive for CD25. Also an aber-rant expression of CD10 is seen more often in HCL than in HCL-V. In contrast to HCL， HCL-V is negative for BRAF V600E mutations 通用删除6(英):<u>\[53-56\]</u>. SMZL are negative for CD103and CD123 by flow cytometry， although dim CD123 may be occasionally seen on subset of cells.

【25】**SPLENIC DIFFUSE RED PULP SMALL B-CELL LYMPHOMA**

【26】**SDRPL is an uncommon lymphoma with a diffuse pat-tern of involvement of the splenic red pulp， BM sinusoids， and peripheral blood by small monomorphous basophilic B lymphocytes often with villous cytoplasm 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，15，21，57，58\]</u>. All cases are diagnosed at clinical stage IV with spleen， BM， and blood involvement 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Rare cases with skin involvement have been reported. Clinical findings (sple-nomegaly， lymphocytosis without pancytopenia) are remi-niscent of HCL-V 通用删除6(英):<u>\[57\]</u>. Men are affected more often than women and patients are usually in advanced age. The most frequent chromosomal changes include chromosome 7q deletion， complete trisomy 18， and partial trisomy 3q 通用删除6(英):<u>\[57\]</u>. This is an indolent butincurable disease with good response after splenectomy.**

【27】**MORPHOLOGY**

【28】**Blood**

【29】**Peripheral blood smear shows a homogeneous infiltrate of small- to medium-sized cells with round or oval nuclei. sometimes eccentrically placed， and dense and clumped chromatin， basophilicCwith characteristic broad-based， unevenly distributedcytoplasmicexpansions(villous projections) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.**

【30】**Spleen**

【31】**The spleen shows diffuse involvement of the red pulp， with both cord and sinusoid infiltration and characteristic intra-sinusoidal aggregates (pattern similar to HCL and HCL-V). White pulp is most often also replaced or atrophic and shows only occasional follicles. Some lymphoplasmacytoid cells can be observed on blood smear or in the spleen.**

【32】**Bone Marrow**

**BM aspirate shows small lymphocytes with villous pro-cesses (similar to those seen in blood smear). BM core biopsy infiltrate is often subtle on hematoxylin and eosin(H&E) sections. It shows characteristic intrasinusoidal involvement， which occasionally can be accompanied by interstitial or nodular infiltration. In a series of SDRPL reported by Ponzoni et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[32\]</u>， pure intrasinusoidal， pure interstitial， diffuse， mixed1intrasinusoidal-interstitial， and nodular combined with other types were observed in|删除1换行|13%，11%， 11%，37%， and 28% of cases， respectively 通用删除6(英):<u>\[32\]</u>. No paratrabecular has been reported. Reticulin fibrosis is minimal. Presence of a significant percentage of medium-to large-sized cells with a prominent nucleolus suggests progression (transformation).**

【34】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【35】**Flow Cytometry**

【36】**Neoplastic B cells are positive for CD20 (strong expression)， CD22 (strong expression)， and CD1lc (subset of cases； mod-erate expression)， and are negative for CD10， CD25， CD103， and CD123 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，12，15，21，59\]</u>. Occasional cases may show partial and dim expression of CD103 通用删除6(英):<u>\[60\]</u>. Flow cytometric analysis shows an occasional expression of CD5 or CD23(without coexpression)通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.**

【37】**Immunohistochemistrv**

【38】**Lymphoma cells in SDRPL express B-cell markers (CD19， CD20， CD22， CD79a， PAX5)， BCL2， and DBA44， and are negative for CD5， CD10， CD23， CD43， BCL1 (cyclin D1)， BCL6，MUM1，and annexin-A1通用删除6(英):<u>\[15，32，58\]</u>.**

【39】**Differential Diagnosis**

【40】The differential diagnosis includes SMZL， HCL， LPL， and HCL-V. The comparison between SDRPL and SMZL has been previously reported 通用删除6(英):<u>\[57\]</u>. The use of a scoring system based on the expression of CD11c， CD22， CD76， CD38，and CD27 appears to improve the differential diagnosis between SDRPL and SMZL. The statistically significant difference in progression-free survival with SMZL supports the view of SDRPL as a more indolent disease\[571.

**SDRPL shares with HCL some common features， such as the male predominance， the massive congested red pulp pat-tern with sometimes blood lakes， the rarity of clonal chro-mosomal abnormalities， and the expression of classical HCL markers (i.e.， CD11c， CD103， and CD123). 【42】SDRPL and HCL-V have a very similar clinicopathological presentation and the differential diagnosis is not easy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[57，62\]</u>. However， the nucleolus described as small or not visible in SDRPL is prominent in HCL-V. The spleen section shows a monomorphic diffuse infiltrate， predominant in the conges-tive red pulp with atrophic white pulp 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>. Small blood lakes can be observed. The BM infiltrate shows a variable cellularity and mild fibrosis with predominantly intrasinusoidal lymphoid infiltrate， which can be accompanied by interstitial or nodu-lar infiltration. The immunophenotype is distinct from SMZL and HCL with moderate expression of CD11c and CD22， low expression of CD103， but absence of CD25 and annexin-1expression 通用删除6(英):<u>\[15\]</u>.

【43】In the BM， LPL often shows paratrabecular involvement， a pattern not identified in SDRPL.

【44】**CHRONIC LYMPHOCYTIC LEUKEMIA**

【45】CLL/SLL， apart from the BM and blood， frequently involves the lymph nodes， spleen， and other extranodal sites. The white pulp is expanded with a prominent nodular pattern. Red pulp is also often involved with a diffuse and/or nodular pattern. The lymphoid cells are mostly small with a mature chromatic pattern and a scanty cytoplasm， but various proportions of

通用删除16(英):<u>**FIGURE 45.7 Spleen—B-SLL/CLL (inset： higher magnification shows prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblast； arrow).**</u>|删除换行|prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblasts are often identified. In most cases， there are no residual reactive germinal centers. Leukemic cells express CD19， CD20 (dim)， PAX5， CD5， CD23， and BCL2， and are negative for BCL1(cyclin Dl)， annexin-A1， BCL6，and CD10.**

【47】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【48】**The differential diagnosis includes SMZL， MCL， FL， LPL/WM， and SDRPL.**

【49】**LYMPHOPLASMACYTIC LYMPHOMA/WALDENSTROM MACROGLOBULINEMIA**

【50】LPL/WM shows involvement of the white and red pulps by mixture of small lymphocytes， lymphoplasmacytic cells， and plasma cells. Dutcher bodies are present and may be promi-nent. White pulp is expanded and diffusely infiltrate by neo-plastic cells without a biphasic pattern. The residual follicles may be present， but are usually atrophic without germinal centers； they can be visualized by immunostaining with CD21 and CD23. Red pulp is diffusely involved by lympho-plasmacytic infiltrate with a preserved architecture and with-out involvement of the sinuses. Histiocytes and mast cells may be increased， the former with hemosiderin pigment. Lymphomatous cells have nonspecific phenotype (they are negative for CD5， CD10， BCL6， annexin-A1， and CD103).

【51】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

The differential diagnosis includes other low-grade B-cell lymphoproliferations， especially with prominent plasmacytic differentiation. B-CLL/SLL can be distinguished by the presence of proliferation centers (clusters of prolymphocytes and paraimmunoblasts) and specific phenotype (CD5/CD23coexpression). MCLs are positive for CD5 and BCLl (cyclin D1). SMZL shows often a biphasic pattern， follicle coloniza-tion， and a monocytic appearance of B cells-features not seen in LPL/WM. FL is distinguished by cytology (cen-trocytes and centroblasts) and coexpression of CD10 and BCL6. Splenic FLs are positive for BCL2 rearrangement|删除0换行|by fluorescence in situ hybridization \[FISH； or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing.

【53】**MANTLE CELL LYMPHOMA**

【54】MCL  involving the spleen shows usu-ally the involvement of the white pulp， but prominent diffuse involvement with massive splenomegaly and leukemic blood involvement with “prolymphocytoid"morphology have been reported 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1，63\]</u>. Typical MCL shows a prominent mantle zone surrounding a reactive germinal center， which may be well preserved or atrophic due to colonizing mantle cells. Cases with somewhat a biphasic pattern mimicking SMZL， a nodu-lar pattern mimicking FL， and aggressive variants (blastoid or pleomorphic) can also occur. Immunophenotypic analysis shows expression of B-cell markers， CD5， SOX11， and BCL1(cyclin D1). Some cases of MCL may be CD5-or CD10+ .

【55】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

The differential diagnosis includes SMZL， CLL/SLL， LPL/WM，FL，and SDRPL.Cases ofMCL with remnants of follicles imitating the biphasic pattern may be difficult to differentiate from SMZL on H&E sections. SMZLs are only rarely CD5+；1心上they do not express BCL1 (cyclin D1) and are negative for t(11；14). Cases with predominance of intermediate- to large-sized cells (blastoid or pleomorphic variants) need to be|删除0换行|differentiated from DLBCL and T-cell lymphomas. Cases with homogeneous nodules composed of cells with irregular nuclei resembling FL. FL is distinguished by lack of CD5 and positive CD10 expression (FISH studies are positive for BCL2and negative for CCNDI rearrangement).

【57】**FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA**

【58】FL frequently involves the spleen and shows phenotypic and cytogenetic findings similar to nodal FL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[18，19\]</u>. Splenic FL shows two patterns of involvement： pattern with an abnor-mal architecture due to prominent nodular infiltrate with scanty red pulp  and pattern with a mostly preserved architecture and scattered atypical follicles 通用删除6(英):<u>\[18\]</u>. A multimicronodular pattern is most common， especially in a secondary FL. The nodules are often rather homogeneous in size and shape， but some cases show heterogeneous fol-licles. Splenic FL may present with prominent splenomegaly with minimal or no lymphadenopathy 通用删除6(英):<u>\[19\]</u>. Similar to lymph nodes， increased interfollicular B cells expressing CD10are often present. FL in situ can be seen frequently in the spleen 通用删除6(英):<u>\[18\]</u>. Lymphoid cells are mostly small to intermediate in size and have irregular nuclei (germinal center cytologic composition， mostly centrocytes and scattered centroblasts). Marginal zone-like cells may be present at the periphery of the nodules 通用删除6(英):<u>\[19\]</u>. Lymphomatous cells express B-cell mark
