【31】**T-Cell/Histiocyte-Rich Large B-Cell Lymphoma.**

【32】**References.**

【33】NodularlymphocyterpredominantHodgkinlymphoma(NLPHL) is a monoclonal B-cell neoplasm characterized by the presence of scattered large atypical lymphocyte pre-dominant (LP) cells \[“popcorn cells，" formerly known as lymphocytic and histiocytic (L&H) cells\] and a distinct nodular pattern on low magnification 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1-9\]</u>. NLPHL involves most often the cervical， axillary， or inguinal lymph nodes. Mediastinal and bone marrow (BM) involvement are rare.

【34】NLPHL occurs at any age， but most often in the 30-50-year-old age group with median age around 40 years 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. Patients are predominantly males. There is an association between NLPHL and progressively transformed germinal centers(PTGC)， as it may be seen simultaneously with or may pre-cede NLPHL. Therefore， patients with PTGC， but without typ-ical popcorn cells should be closely followed since they have slightly higher risk of developing NLPHL. The prognosis of NLPHL is usually favorable， especially at early stage. The dis-ease develops slowly with frequent relapses. It usually remains responsive to the therapy.

Overall survival rates are similar in patients with NLPHL(86%) and classical Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) (82%) at clini-cal stages IA and IIA treated with anthracycline-based che-motherapy plus high-dose extended irradiation； they share a very good prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[11\]</u>. Treatment of NLPHL patients using standard HL protocols leads to complete remission in >95% of patients (survival and freedom from treatment failure are worse in advanced-stage patients than in early-stage patients) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[6\]</u>. Only a small subset of patients with NLPHL in whom lymph node biopsy shows NLPHL with a typical， purely nodular pat-tern also may have lymphoma in the BM. BM involvement is|删除0换行|associated with laboratory， radiologic， or morphologic evidence of aggressive disease and poor prognosis 通用删除6(英):<u>\[12\]</u>.

【36】**NLPHL and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma(THRLBCL) may occur concurrently or subsequently in the same patient 通用删除6(英):<u>\[13-15\]</u>. At present， an overlap between NLPHL and THRLBCL cannot be excluded 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，16\]</u>. Presence of a diffuse T-cell/histiocyte-rich-like pattern is more common in patients with recurrent disease than those without recur-rence 通用删除6(英):<u>\[17\]</u>. The focally diffuse pattern (THRLBCL-like) in NLPHL is an independent predictor of recurrent disease \[171. Analysis of sequential biopsies from patients with recur-rent disease suggests that the presence of increased number of lymphocyte predominant (LP) cells outside the nodules might represent early evolution to a diffuse (THRLBCL-like) pattern and eventually large B-cell lymphoma 通用删除6(英):<u>\[17\]</u>.**

【37】A subset of patients with NLPHL (2%-7%) may develop more aggressive lymphomas， most often diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)， which were reported to have a better prognosis than de novo DLBCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10，14，18-21\]</u>. In a series reported by Huang et al. 通用删除6(英):<u>\[22\]</u>， however， there were no signifi-cant differences in the survival outcomes between patients with DLBCL arising in NLPHL and age- and sex-matched patients with de novo DLBCL. In that report， the median time to the development of DLBCL in those with prior NLPHL was only 1 year (range： 0.5-24 years)， the median age of the patients at the time of diagnosis of DLBCL was46 years (range： 18-72 years)， and the male-to-female ratio was 17：4. Initial splenic involvement by NLPHL is associ-ated with higher risk of transformation 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>. The 10-year progression-free and overall survival rates in patients with transformed lymphoma are 52% and 62%， respectively 通用删除6(英):<u>\[10\]</u>.

【38】**MORPHOLOGY**

【39】**LYMPH NODE**

The most characteristic morphologic feature of NLPHL is the distinct nodular pattern of the lymph node under low magnification . Nodules are often ill defined and vague and are usually larger than those of follicular lymphoma (FL)， follicular hyperplasia， or nodular mantle cell lymphoma (MCL). The nodules contain histiocytes， which may give the nodules a pseudo-starry-sky appearance on low magnification. The nodular pattern is easily visual-ized by staining with CD21 and/or CD23， which also shows an expanded follicular dendritic cell (FDC) meshwork， or by staining with B-cell markers (e.g.， PAX5 or CD20). There are no fibrous septae separating individual nodules，|删除0换行|as seen in classical nodular sclerosis HL. Although focal diffuse areas may be present， cases with a completely dif-fuse growth pattern most often represent THRLBCL 通用删除6(英):<u>\[23\]</u>.

【41】**LP cells  are large with multilobated or folded nuclei， prominent nucleoli， and pale vesicular chromatin. Because of their cytologic features， they are also called“popcorn cells” or L&H cells. LP cells differ morphologically from Reed-Sternberg (R-S) cells by their smaller size， less pronounced lobation， smaller nucleoli， and scantier cytoplasm. The background cells include mostly small B lymphocytes and scattered follicular helper T cells \[CD3+/CD4+/CD57+/programmed cell death (PD)-1+\]. T cells form characteris-tic rosettes around neoplastic cells. Occasional cases may show histiocytic clusters， with or without epithelioid features. Sclerosis is rare. Neutrophils and eosinophils are seldom seen.**

【46】**EXTRANODAL SITES**

The unique morphologic and immunophenotypic features of NLPHL are preserved in extranodal sites (liver， spleen， tonsil， salivary gland， soft tissue， and BM) 通用删除6(英):<u>\[25\]</u>. Figure 25.4shows NLPHL involving gastrointestinal tract. Advanced stage of NLPHL is rare， and BM involvement is usually seen after many relapses and most likely represent the disease pro-gression into large B-cell lymphoma (such as THRLBCL). The pattern of involvement is usually diffuse， but may be focally nodular or even focally paratrabecular. The morpho-logic and immunophenotypic features of NLPHL in the BM overlap with those of THRLBCL. Figures 25.5 through 25.7show the BM from patient with history of NLPHL. Presence of CD57- (or PD-1-) T cells without small B cells in the background favors the diagnosis of THRLBCL rather than NLPHL， as shown in Figures 25.5 and 25.6. 【48】**IMMUNOPHENOTYPE**

【49】Phenotypically， LP cells are positive for CD45， B-cell markers(CD19，CD20，CD22，CD79a，BOB1，OCT2，andPAX5)，BCL6， and often epithelial membrane antigen 通用删除1(英):<u></u>. BCL2 is usually negative. Most often， the expression of PAX5is dimmer than in the surrounding benign small B cells and the expression of OCT2 is stronger. Subset of cases shows IgD expression (~10%-30%)， especially in young males 通用删除6(英):<u>\[7，26\]</u>. Nearly all cases lack the expression of CD30， CD15， pan-T-cell markers， CD43，MUMl， and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)/EBV-encoded RNA (EBER). In typical cases， LP cells are distributed within aggregates of small (benign) B cells， which create a characteristic nodular pattern on low magnification， appreciated in the H&E section or by the immunostaining with CD20 or PAX5. There is an expanded meshwork of FDC， best visualized by CD21 and/or CD23 staining. LP cells are surrounded by a single layer of small benign CD3+ T cells， which often coexpress CD4， CD57， and PD-1. Dual CD4+/CD8+ T cells are relatively frequent. In contrast to NLPHL that shows in the background predominance of small B cells and CD4+/CD57+ T cells， the absence of small B cells and the presence of CD8+ and T-cell intracytoplasmic antigen(TIA)-1+T cells favor the primary THRLBCL.

【19】**争DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【20】**_A_ Aspiration： This commonly causes bilateral， multilo-bar， poorly defincd consolidation in dependent pul-monary segments.**

【21】**上Pulmonary malignancy： Postobstructive cavitary con-solidation can occur secondary to an endobronchial neoplasm. A further possibility is bronchioalveolar carcinoma.**

【22】**Wegener’s granulomatosis： The most common radiographic findings are nodular opacities with a high propensity for cavitation. Pulmonary consolida tion， which may be scattered and heterogeneous， or homogeneous and lobar， occurs in approximately30% of patients.**

【23】**Pneumonia： Lobar consolidation is usually bacterial in origin. The bacteria that commonly cause cavitation _are Staphylococcus aureus， Klebsiella， Pseudomonas，_ Proteus， and anaerobic organisms. Mycobacteria tuber-culosis (TB) is increasingly a cause of consolidation and cavitation.**

【24】**DIAGNOSIS： Postprimary tuberculosis.**

【25】**KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【26】**__ The highest incidence of postprimary TB is in patients>65 years of age.**

【27】**Postprimary TB usually occurs due to reactivation of dormant bacilli， although some cases may be due to reinfection of a previously sensitized host.**

【28】**专上Reactivation occurs in 55% to 15% of patients， usually in the secondary foci in the apical/posterior segments of the upper lobes and superior segments of the lower lobes.**

【29】**上Because of host hypersensitivity acquired from primary infection， progressive disease with caseous necrosis occurs and can rapidly destroy the lung.**

【30】**__ Most patients have a delayed cutaneous response to the intradermal injection of purified protein derivative.**

【31】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【32】**__ The earliest findings are heterogeneous， poorly mar-ginated opacities in the apical or postcrior segments of the upper lobes or in thc superior segments of the lower lobes.**

【33】**The initial opacities usually evolve into more well-defined reticular and nodular opacities.**

【34】**The infection may occasionally progress to lobar or complete lung consolidation.**

【35】**Cavitation is common (40% to 87%) and typically occurs within areas of consolidation.**

【36】**_A complication of cavitation is endobronchial spread of_ infection，**

【37】**Endobronchial dissemination results in 5- to 10-mm， poorly defined peribronchiolar and centrilobular nodules.**

【38】**Miliary TB occurs less commonly in postprimary than in primary TB， and the classic radiographic findings are diffuse， small (1 to 3 mm)， well-defined nodules.**

【39】**Pleural effusions are uncommon (6% to 18%) and usu-ally small.**

【40】**Hilar and mediastinal adenopathy is rare with postpri-mary TB.**

【41】**Healing may be associated with scarring， cicatricial atelectasis， traction bronchiectasis， residual nodules， and parenchymal calcification.**

【53】**DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS**

【54】**Pneumonia： Lobar consolidation is usually caused by bacterial infection. Organisms include Streptococcus _pneumoniae， Staphylococeus aureus， Legionella pneu-_ mophila， gram-negative bacteria， and Mycobacterium tubereulosis. A bacterial infection is unlikely with a his-tory of chronic weight loss and no fever， although tuberculosis (TB) can have a subacute presentation.**

【55】**Aspiration pneumonia： Aspiration of gram-negative or anacrobic bacteria may causc lobar consolidation. Aspiration commonly causes scattered， poorly defined consolidation in the dependent segments. Involvement of the anterior portions of the lungs in this patient makes this diagnosis unlikely.**

【56】**Wegener's granulomatosis： Although the disease can be indolent， presentation is usually acute， with upper airway involvement (sinusitis， rhinitis， otitis) and func-tional renal impairment. Nodular opacities， which fre-quently cavitate， are the most common presentation. Lobar consolidation and numerous， small nodular opacities occur in 30% of patients.**

【57】**Primary lymphoma of lung： This rare non-Hodgkin's lymphoma is usually low grade， and patients are often asymptomatic. Consolidation with air bronchograms and poorly defined margins is the most common prcsentation. Mass-like and reticulo-nodular opacities are less frequent.**

【58】**Bronchioalveolar cell carcinoma (BAC)： The clinical presentation and homogeneous consolidation with nodules could be due to the diffuse form of BAC.**

【59】**专DIAGNOSIS： Bronchioalveolar cell carcinoma.**

【60】**镂KEY FACTS**

【61】**_CLINICAL_**

【62】**BAC constitutes 1.5% to 10.0% of all lung cancers.**

**IIt is a subtype of adenocarcinoma and can be localized or multifocal. The localized form can， after an indolent period of local growth， progress rapidly to diffuse tho-|删除0换行|racic metastases. The biologic behavior of BAC is， however， controversial， and a further possibility is that the two presentations are distinct， with the localized form rarely evolving into diffuse BAC.**

【64】**Clinical features that distinguish BAC from other lung cancers are (1) younger age at presentation， (2) equal distribution of men and women， (3) copious watery sputum (bronchorrhea)， and (4) higher incidence in nonsmokers.**

【65】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【66】**__ The most common finding is a well-circumscribed， solitary nodule (60%).**

【67】**__ The nodule may remain unchanged in size over many years.**

【68】**The solitary nodule is usually peripheral in location.**

【69】**Pseudocavitation， the presence of small， low-attenua-tion regions within or surrounding the nodule， is more common with this malignancy than other non-small cell carcinomas.**

【70】**The diffuse form may present as (1) multiple pul-monary nodules of varying size； (2) focal， poorly defined opacities resembling pneumonia； (3) reticulo-nodular opacitics resembling interstitial lung disease；(4) other radiographic findings associated with parenchymal disease include hilar and mediastinal adenopathy (18%)， pleural effusions (1% to 10%)， and atelectasis (3%).**

【23】**Pneumonia： Lobar consolidation is usually bacterial in origin. The bacteria that commonly cause cavitation _are Staphylococcus aureus， Klebsiella， Pseudomonas，_ Proteus， and anaerobic organisms. Mycobacteria tuber-culosis (TB) is increasingly a cause of consolidation and cavitation.**

【25】**KEY FACTS _CLINICAL_**

【26】**__ The highest incidence of postprimary TB is in patients>65 years of age.**

【27】**Postprimary TB usually occurs due to reactivation of dormant bacilli， although some cases may be due to reinfection of a previously sensitized host.**

【28】**专上Reactivation occurs in 55% to 15% of patients， usually in the secondary foci in the apical/posterior segments of the upper lobes and superior segments of the lower lobes.**

【29】**上Because of host hypersensitivity acquired from primary infection， progressive disease with caseous necrosis occurs and can rapidly destroy the lung.**

【32】**__ The earliest findings are heterogeneous， poorly mar-ginated opacities in the apical or postcrior segments of the upper lobes or in thc superior segments of the lower lobes.**

【34】**The infection may occasionally progress to lobar or complete lung consolidation.**

【35】**Cavitation is common (40% to 87%) and typically occurs within areas of consolidation.**

【36】**_A complication of cavitation is endobronchial spread of_ infection，**

【37】**Endobronchial dissemination results in 5- to 10-mm， poorly defined peribronchiolar and centrilobular nodules.**

【38】**Miliary TB occurs less commonly in postprimary than in primary TB， and the classic radiographic findings are diffuse， small (1 to 3 mm)， well-defined nodules.**

【39】**Pleural effusions are uncommon (6% to 18%) and usu-ally small.**

【40】**Hilar and mediastinal adenopathy is rare with postpri-mary TB.**

【54】**Pneumonia： Lobar consolidation is usually caused by bacterial infection. Organisms include Streptococcus _pneumoniae， Staphylococeus aureus， Legionella pneu-_ mophila， gram-negative bacteria， and Mycobacterium tubereulosis. A bacterial infection is unlikely with a his-tory of chronic weight loss and no fever， although tuberculosis (TB) can have a subacute presentation.**

【55】**Aspiration pneumonia： Aspiration of gram-negative or anacrobic bacteria may causc lobar consolidation. Aspiration commonly causes scattered， poorly defined consolidation in the dependent segments. Involvement of the anterior portions of the lungs in this patient makes this diagnosis unlikely.**

【56】**Wegener's granulomatosis： Although the disease can be indolent， presentation is usually acute， with upper airway involvement (sinusitis， rhinitis， otitis) and func-tional renal impairment. Nodular opacities， which fre-quently cavitate， are the most common presentation. Lobar consolidation and numerous， small nodular opacities occur in 30% of patients.**

【57】**Primary lymphoma of lung： This rare non-Hodgkin's lymphoma is usually low grade， and patients are often asymptomatic. Consolidation with air bronchograms and poorly defined margins is the most common prcsentation. Mass-like and reticulo-nodular opacities are less frequent.**

【61】**_CLINICAL_**

【62】**BAC constitutes 1.5% to 10.0% of all lung cancers.**

**IIt is a subtype of adenocarcinoma and can be localized or multifocal. The localized form can， after an indolent period of local growth， progress rapidly to diffuse tho-|删除0换行|racic metastases. The biologic behavior of BAC is， however， controversial， and a further possibility is that the two presentations are distinct， with the localized form rarely evolving into diffuse BAC.**

【64】**Clinical features that distinguish BAC from other lung cancers are (1) younger age at presentation， (2) equal distribution of men and women， (3) copious watery sputum (bronchorrhea)， and (4) higher incidence in nonsmokers.**

【65】**_RADIOLOGIC_**

【66】**__ The most common finding is a well-circumscribed， solitary nodule (60%).**

【67】**__ The nodule may remain unchanged in size over many years.**

【68】**The solitary nodule is usually peripheral in location.**

【69】**Pseudocavitation， the presence of small， low-attenua-tion regions within or surrounding the nodule， is more common with this malignancy than other non-small cell carcinomas.**

【70】**The diffuse form may present as (1) multiple pul-monary nodules of varying size； (2) focal， poorly defined opacities resembling pneumonia； (3) reticulo-nodular opacitics resembling interstitial lung disease；(4) other radiographic findings associated with parenchymal disease include hilar and mediastinal adenopathy (18%)， pleural effusions (1% to 10%)， and atelectasis (3%).**

The good news is that approximately 75% of patients improve within a 1-to 3-year period.8 These are not necessarily the pa-tients for whom a diagnosis was made. One study’pro-vided interesting insight into the psychology of the doctor-patient relationship with regard to diagnosis of chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). Seventy-five percent of doctors were reluctant to give their patients a diagno-sis of CFS because of the uncertainty of the scientific un-derstanding of the etiology and treatment. They also feared that the diagnosis might be a self-fulfilling prophecy if patients believed they had the disorder. Patients， how-ever， felt that the negative effects of not having a diagnosis outweighed the negative effects of the diagnosis of CFS.

【1】**History**

【7】What is the patient's typical daily schedule， in-cluding eating habits， work habits， and sleep habits(not enough or interrupted sleep， skipping break-fast， drinking large amounts of coffee in the morn-ing，a large lunch，alcohol consumption during the day， athletic training schedule is excessive， etc.)?

【20】**GENERAL DISCUSSION**

【21】The more common causes of tiredness and fatigue are usually easily recognized by patients. These include stren-uous activity， lack of sleep， flu， pregnancy， and overwork. Often， though， patients do not associate fatigue with stress. Although the first list illustrates situations of in-creased demand or lack of rest (physiologic)， stress bor-ders the categories of physiologic and functional causes. Physiologic stress is often more acute and there fore more easy to associate with a specific cause. Functional or psy-chologic causes are often without an identifiable match.

【22】CFS is a popular label for patients who feel fatigued or who have no other identifiable cause for their complaint. There are， however， specific criteria that may help sep-arate CFS as a cause.10，11 The case definition requires that the patient have a “new"onset of fatigue (not lifelong). This does not result from exertion only nor is it sub-stantially relieved by rest. The sense of fatigue causes a significant reduction in previous levels of occupational， educational， social， and personal activities. To fit the cri-teria， other symptoms such as short-term memory loss， postexertion fatigue lasting more than 24 hours， sore throat， or headache must persist for 6 months or more. These criteria alone will eliminate the majority of pa-tients with a complaint of fatigue in an ambulatory set-ting. It is important to explain to patients that there is no single laboratory or physical examination finding by which to diagnose CFS.

【23】CFS has had many names， including Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) disease， yuppie flu， neuromyasthenia， postvi-ral fatigue syndrome， royal free disease， Iceland disease， and encephalomyelitis； it is often confused with fi-bromyalgia.l? There is little support for most theories for CFS. There is no clear evidence that EBV or chronic yeast infection is the cause. Evidencel does suggest a chronic immunologically mediated inflarrumatory process involving the central nervous system. The immune re-sponse is believed to be secondary to a number ofinfec-tious and psychiatric illnesses. Interest in human herpes

【41】An association between neurally mediated hypotension(NMH) and chronic fatigue is recognized. Initially， NMH was identified as a cause of unexplained syncope in some individuals. In one study the patients had postexertional fatigue， whereas another study tested a sample of patients who met the criteria for CFS. Both groups had an ab-normal response to the upright tilt test and good response to therapy using antihypertensive medication.16，17 The up-right tilt test is designed to detect an abnormal cardio-vascular reflex.

【42】CFS and depression are related. Studies suggest that in many cases， depressioEPIESSTMn precedes CFS； however， depres- sion is found with all CFS patients. For this reason， the original criteria for CFS， which excluded patients with psychiatric disorders， have been modifed to include those with nonpsychotic depression， somatoform disorders，and generalized anxiety or panic disorders.18 In one study， sui-cidal thoughts were found in 55% of CFS patients.

【43】Two other interesting studies should be mentioned. The first study20 illustrates a possible relationship be-tween hypofunctioning of the corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons and CFS. The authors suggest a cen-tral deficiency of a potent arousal-producing neuropep-tide. In the second study，the authors suggest that the immunosupportive role of sleep is key to the under-standing of the sleepiness associated with chronic fatigue. They point out that some viruses cause excessive sleepi-ness and postulate that some infections may cause a dys-function in the sleep/wakefulness cycle.

【44】**EVALUATION**

【45】**History**

【46】The initial focus of the history is to determine exactly what the patient means by a complaint of fatigue. Patients may describe their complaint as being weak， weariness， bore-dom， lack ofenergy， exhaustion， unwillingness or aversion to work， sleepiness， and difficulty breathing with exertion， _Y._ among others. It is important for the chiropractor to lis-ten patiently to this explanation. Although obtaining the history is time consuming， there are often valuable clues that will lead to a more expedient diagnosis with more ju-dicious use of laboratory testing .

【47】The key initial distinction is between organic/physiologic causes and functional/psychologic causes.In general， the history clues that would point toward a func-tional cause include the following：

【48】Fatigue or tiredness is felt more in the morning and improves as the day progresses.

【49】Although the patient may feel like sleeping， sleep-ing does not improve his or her fatigue.

【50】厂The sense of fatigue is associated with work or sit-uations that are perceived as stressful； improve-ment occurs with avoidance.

【51】There is a past or current history of depression， anxiety， or somatization disorder.

【52】Clues that would point toward a physiologic cause in-clude the following：

【53】Complaints of insomnia or disrupted sleep improve with napping.

【54】The patient feels best in the morning and feels worse with activity or as the day progresses； com-plaints improve with sleep.

【58】The patient is taking a medication such as antihy-pertensives， antipsychotics， chemotherapy for cancer，anticonvulsants (for seizure)， tricyclic anti-depressants， benzodiazepines， and antihistamines(antihistamines are the main ingredients in most over-the-counter sleep-inducing medications).

【78】**MANAGEMENT**

【79】Management of fatigue is based on an identifiable cause. When there is an obvious lifestyle factor， such as diet， work， or stress， modification is often all that is needed.The chiropractor can play a clear role in advice regarding proper diet and exercise， stress management， and avoid-ance of excess in alcohol and drugs. When the underly-ing cause is suspected to be a inedication， referral to the prescribing physician with a letter of explanation is nec-essary. All other patients with identifiable or suspected dis-eases should be referred to a primary care or specialist physician for comanagement.

【80】_T.二._ It appears that a moderate exercise plan may be im-portant in preventing worsening of fatigue.25，26 A num-ber of different approaches have been used in the treatment of CFS， but there has been no consistent， re-producible benefit with any. One case study34 used2.5 g of licorice per day. It is important to note that these hypertensive aspects of licorice should be taken quite se-riously prior to recommending licorice as a nutritional aid to CFS. It may mean infrequent stools， hard stools or unsatisfactory defecation (e.g.， defecatory straining， or a sensa-tion of incomplete evacuation). 【69】**Evaluation**

【70】**1\. Is There Structural Gastrointestinal Disease?**

【71】**Obstructive gastrointestinal lesions， including colorectal cancer， may present with constipation. Look for alarm symptoms：**

【72】**·Acute onset of severe constipation.**

【73】**· Obstructive symptoms： Association with abdominal pain， increasing abdominal distension and/or nausea/vomiting. See further workup， for example， abdominal X-ray， discussed in Chapter 12.**

【74】**· Red flags for cancer： Rectal bleeding， decrease in stool calibre， weight loss， anaemia or a strong family history of colorectal cancer. This should prompt further evalua-tion including colonoscopy.**

【75】**Anorectal disorders： A rectal examination should be performed in all patients with constipation. Identify**

【76】**· Painful anal disorders， for example， anal fissure， thrombosed haemorrhoids. These can be the result of constipation or exacerbate it (because defecation becomes painful).**

【77】**·Rectal prolapse-this may be more obvious when the patient bears down.**

【78】**2\. Look for Secondary Causes**

【79】**These diseases rarely first present with constipation， but commonly contribute.**

【80】**1\. Medications： Especially opioid analgesia and anticholinergics (antihistamines， antipsychotics， tricyclic antidepressants). Other culprit drugs include iron supplements and calcium channel blockers.**

【81】**2\. Neurologic disease**

【82】**·Autonomic neuropathy including longstanding diabetes， Parkinson's disease and related syndromes.**

【83】**·Upper motor neuron lesions including spinal cord injury， multiple sclerosis.**

【84】**3\. Metabolic and other disease**

【85】**·Electrolyte disturbance especially hypokalae-mia， hypercalcemia.**

【86】**·Hypothyroidism.**

【87】**·Scleroderma： Examine for clinical features including sclerodactyly， Raynaud's phenom-enon and so forth.**

【88】**Workup**

【89】**\- Go through drug list**

【90】**\- Clinical examination**

【91】**\- Screen for diabetes**

【92】**\- Screen electrolytes and thyroid**

【93】**Psychiatric disease， for example， anorexia： It's hard to have significant bowel output if there is little food intake.**

【94】**3\. Manage As for Functional Disorder**

【95】**Excluding the structural and secondary causes of constipation leaves us with its idio-pathic/functional causes. This may be**

【96】**Irritable bowel syndrome， constipation predominant (IBS-C)： Some patients have a syndrome of constipation with abdominal pain and/or bloating and may fulfil diagnostic criteria for IBS-C-recurrent abdominal pain (at least 1x/week in3 months) with two or more of (1) relationship to defecation， (2) changes in stool frequency or (3) change in stool consistency. There may be alternating periods of diarrhoea (IBS-mixed).**

【97】**Functional constipation： Other patients do not have abdominal pain symptoms， and are simply termed to have functional constipation. Some (but not all) patients have decreased colonic motility or pelvic floor dysfunction (failure to relax pelvic floor muscles during defecation).**

【98】**An approach：**

【99】**__ Begin with a trial of diet modification (increase fibre) and symptomatic therapy(laxatives).**

【100】**Colonoscopy is not necessary for every patient， but offer age-appropriate screening(e.g.， above 50 years old for the general population).**

【101】**4\. If Unacceptable Outcome with Symptomatic Management**

【102】**Consider further specialist evaluation in patients with severe constipation who do not respond to simple measures. Apart from colonoscopy， this may include studies of colonic motility and anorectal physiology**

【114】**Initial Approach**

【115】**The first division is between**

【116】**Oropharyngeal dysphagia： Difficulty initiating a swallow， especially if associated with coughing， choking， regurgitation and drooling. Patients sometimes use their fingers to help position food， and there may also be abnormalities with speech.**

【117】**(Oesophageal dysphagia： A sensation of food getting stuck a few seconds after ini-tiating a swallow. Patients are often able to point to the location in the neck or chest where they feel the food is getting stuck.**

【118】**Acute-onset dysphagia： Suggests foreign body ingestion. Ask for relevant history. Consider neck and chest X-rays to identify radio-opaque foreign bodies (not all foreign bodies are visible on X-ray)， as well as endoscopy (urgent if obstruction is complete， i.e.， unable to swallow even secretions， or the suspected foreign body is dangerous， e.g.， caustic， sharp-pointed or large).**

【119】**Oesophageal Dysphagia**

【120】**The symptomology of oesophageal dysphagia correlates with its mechanism**

【121】**Structural obstruction： Causes greater difficulty swallowing solids than liquids，as the larger the food particle， the more difficult to pass down a narrow oesophagus. Patients may have dysphagia to solids only， or to solids first before liquids are involved later.**

【122】**Motility disorder： Causes equal difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids from the start.**

【123】**Odynophagia (painful swallowing)： Suggests oesophagitis.**

【124】**Patients with severe dysphagia are often unable to maintain adequate food and water intake， becoming cachexic and dehydrated.**

【125】**Dysphagia to Solids > Liquids**

【126】**Aetiologies-progressively worsening dysphagia：**

【127】**Oesophageal cancer： Progressive solid dysphagia in an elderly patient is worri-some， especially if accompanied with severe weight loss， anaemia， hoarseness of voice and cervical lymphadenopathy.**

【128】**Stricture： Patients may have a history of heartburn or reflux symptoms (peptic stricture from gastroesophageal reflux disease)， neck radiation (radiation stricture) or caustic chemical ingestion.**

【129】**Aetiologies-intermittent dysphagia：**

【130】**__ Intra-luminal oesophageal abnormalities including eosinophilic oesophagitis， rings and webs.**

【131】**__ Extra-luminal compression of the aorta by congenital aortic arch abnormalities， enlargement of the left atrium or thoracic aorta， thyroid nodules or mediastinal lymph nodes.**

【132】**Approach： The first consideration is oesophageal cancer， especially in an older patient. Most patients should receive oesophagogastroduodenoscopy (OGD) to visualise the abnormality. Barium swallow is an alternate diagnostic modality in patients who are unfit for OGD， or if severe anatomical distortion is suspected (OGD carries higher risk of perforation).**

【8】**SUMMARY： HERITABLE METABOLIC DISEASES PRESENTING WITH CHOREA**

【9】Children presenting with acute chorea which is not immune-mediated may have a metabolic disease. When chorea is present in a child with developmental delay or regression， metabolic diseases are an important part of the differential diagnosis. Inheritance pattern is important but not always informative， for example， in iso-lated cases which may be autosomal recessive.

【10】Table 13-4 was generated through extracting information from a clinical syn-opsis search of “chorea OR choreoathetosis"from the National Library of Medi-cine’s OMIM， an extremely useful tool for the complex task of diagnosing heritable diseases. This database is of particular utility for disorders in which chorea is a minor or rare feature， which are not addressed in this volume. For others (e.g.， Karak syndrome)， classification and definition are in evolution as causative genes are identified. Nevertheless， this is a valuable resource for the diagnosis of these disorders.

【0】ential Diagnosis

【1】**Adrenal cortical adenoma**

【2】**Typically， adenomas appear golden-yellow on gross examination； pheochromocytomas with lipid degeneration can have a similar gross appearance， but stains for chromogranin and synaptophysin are diagnostic**

【3】**Neuroblastoma**

【4】Typically found in children younger than 4 years； composed of small round blue cells often with pseudorosette formation

【5】**Pearls**

【6】Malignant behavior cannot be determined based on morphologic findings； only presence of distant metastases proves malignancy

【7】Metastatic spread through lymphatic or hematogenous pathways most commonly involves lymph nodes， bones (particularly ribs and spine)， lung， and liver

【8】Benign， surgically treated tumors have a 5-year survival rate of more than 95%； the 5-year survival rate of patients with malignant pheochromocytoma is about 44%

【9】Pheochromocytoma is rare in children and is most often extra-adrenal， multifocal， and associated with hereditary syndromes

【10】Tyrosine hydroxylase immunoreactivity in pheochromocytomas is helpful to rule out neuroendocrine carcinomas

【17】**Ganglioneuroma**

【18】**Clinical Features**

【19】Etiology

【20】\- Ganglioneuromas can present as de novo tumors or may arise from neuroblastomas and GNBs that underwent spontaneous maturation or after treatment with chemotherapy

【21】Epidemiology

【22】\-Rare benign tumors found in older individuals； the median age at diagnosis ranges from 5.5 to 10years； with a slight female predominance (1.5：1)

【23】The most common locations are the posterior mediastinum (41%)， retroperitoneum (37%)， adrenal gland (21%)， and neck (8%)

【24】一 Most common tumor of sympathetic nervous system in adults

【25】**Signs and symptoms**

【26】\- Most often manifests as an asymptomatic mass

【27】\-May present with symptoms of catecholamine excess， rarely with diarrhea

【28】Biochemistry

【29】\- Elevated VMA and homovanillic acid (HVA) levels

【30】\- Increased secretion of vasoactive intestinal peptide

【31】(VIP) or serotonin may cause diarrhea

【32】**Therapy**

【33】\- Tumor removal is the preferred treatment

【34】Gross Pathology

【35】Large， well circumscribed，although a true capsule is uncommon

Measure from 1 cm to more than 15 cm； average|删除换行|about 8 cm**

【37】Firm consistency with homogeneous， solid， tan-yellow to gray-white cut surface

【38】Occasionally multifocal

【39】通用删除16(英):<u>Figure 9-8. A. Ganglioneuroma. High-power view showing characteristic proliferation of spindle cells with wavy nuclei. Several classic ganglion cells are present in the center of the field. B， Composite pheochromocytoma and ganglioneuroma. The lesion consists of two components： a typical pheochromocytoma (eft) and spindle cell ganglioneuroma (right).</u>

【40】Histopathology

【41】**Composed entirely of ganglion cells and stromal elements represented by Schwann cells and mature fibrous tissue**

【42】Ganglion cells have compact eosinophilic cytoplasm with distinct cell borders and a single eccentric nucleus with a prominent nucleolus； may contain granular golden-brown pigment(neuromelanin)

【43】Variable numbers of ganglion cells may be present； few may be seen， making distinction from neurofibroma difficult

【44】上Mitotic activity and necrosis are absent

【45】Mast cells may be present， although tumor does not contain neuroblasts or intermediate cells

【46】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【47】S-100 protein positive

【48】Synaptophysin： ganglion cells positive

【49】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【50】Electron microscopy： ganglion cells have an eccentric nucleus with a prominent nucleolus； cytoplasm shows peripheral rough endoplasmic reticulum， and neurosecretory granules

【51】Differential Diagnosis

【52】**Neurofibroma**

【53】__ Lacks ganglion cell differentiation

【54】**Pearls**

【55】Ganglioneuroma is believed to be the fully differentiated counterpart of peripheral neuroblastic tumors

【56】Considered a benign tumor； however， malignant transformation to malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) has been reported

【57】Thorough sampling needed to rule out less well-differentiated areas； all friable or hemorrhagic areas must be submitted for microscopic examination

【64】**Ganglioneuroblastoma**

【65】**Clinical Features**

【66】**Epidemiology**

【67】_—_ Most often seen in patients 2 to 4 years old， and exceedingly rare after the age of 10 years； occur with equal frequency in boys and girls

【68】Signs and symptoms

【69】**_—_ Patients often present with an abdominal mass or with abdominal tenderness**

【70】**一 Most common tumor site is the abdomen， followed by the mediastinum， neck， and lower extremity**

【71】**TTherapy**

【72】**\- Prognosis and response to therapy is significantly more favorable than those of neuroblastoma**

【73】Gross Pathology

【74】VWell-circumscribed mass with a variegated cut surface

【75】Tumor appearance varies depending on the amount of mature to immature elements， ranging from predominantly solid to cystic

【76】Firm tan-white areas (better differentiated component) and hemorrhagic areas (poorly differentiated component) may be seen

【77】**Granular calcifications are often present**

【78】Histopathology

【79】Shows histologic features similar to those of neuroblastoma， except that ganglion cell differentiation is present

【80】**Variable amounts of neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma are seen in the same tumor； typically the ganglioneuromatous component is in excess of 50% of the tumor**

【81】Subtypes (International Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee)

【82】GNB： nodular classic (abrupt transition between the neuroblastomatous nodule and the surrounding ganglioneuromatous component)

【83】_—_ GNB： nodular atypical (no nodules are seen on gross or microscopic examination； ganglioneuromatous component is present as a thin rim； metastasis shows neuroblastomatous features)

【84】_—I_ GNB： intermixed (tumor is composed predominantly of gangliomatous component with well-delineated microscopic foci of neuroblastomatous component)

【85】__ TThese categories have prognostic significance：nodular has an unfavorable prognosis； intermixed has favorable prognosis

【86】Special Stains and Immunohistochemistry

【87】Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) positive

【88】Neurofilament positive Chromogranin positive SSynaptophysin positive

【89】S-100 protein positive in spindle cell population

【90】Other Techniques for Diagnosis

【91】Electron microscopy： cells with abundant filiform cell processes； cytoplasm showing distinct neurosecretory granules and neurotubules

【92】**Neuroblastoma**

【93】Has single population of small to medium-sized blue cells with no ganglion cells or evidence of differentiation

【94】**Ganglioneuroma**

【95】Has a spindle cell population in a loose， myxoid background with distinct ganglion cells and no component of neuroblastoma

【96】**Pearls**

【97】GNBs are transitional tumors of sympathetic cell origin that contain elements of both neuroblastoma and ganglioneuroma

【98】It has been suggested that nodular GNB evolves as a result of clonal proliferation of more aggressive malignant tumor cells in a neuroblastomatous component of what originally was a GNB of intermixed type maturing ganglioneuroma

【99】Nodules of nodular GNB may be identified by imaging studies and present with higher levels of urinary excretion of catecholamines compared with intermixed GNB and ganglioneuroma

【105】**Neuroblastoma**

【106】**Clinical Features**

【107】Etiology

【108】\- Malignant tumor of sympaticoadrenal lineage of the neural crest that can develop anywhere in the sympathetic nervous system

【109】Genomic amplification of MYCN is common and consistently associated with poor outcome

【110】_—_ Other biologic variables include deletions of 1p(25% to 35%)， allelic l125oss of 11q(35% to 45%)，and gain of 17q

【111】**Epidemiology**

【112】**—Incidence of about 8 per1×10° population； most common extracranial solid tumor of childhood**

【114】\- Accounts for more than 7% of malignancies in patients younger than 15 years； more than 85%occur in children younger than 4 years

【115】_—_ Can occur in a variety of locations， with adrenal gland being most common site (50%to 80%)

【116】_—_ Other common sites include posterior mediastinum (about 15%)

【117】Signs and symptoms

【118】About 40% of patients present with localized disease ranging from an incidental adrenal mass discovered on prenatal ultrasound to large and invasive tumors

【119】\- Classic signs of disseminated neuroblastoma include periorbital ecchymoses (raccoon eyes)， proptosis， or both， due to metastasis to the bony orbit

【120】_—_ Paraneoplastic syndromes include (1) intractable diarrhea and failure to thrive secondary to secretion of VIP and (2) opsoclonus-myoclonus syndrome (2% to 4%)

【121】**FBiochemistry**

【122】\- May produce catecholamines with increased levels of urinary VMA

【123】**Therapy**

【124】_一_ Surgery， chemotherapy， radiotherapy， and biotherapy， as well as observation alone in selected cases， are used according to risk group based on the presence or absence of unfavorable biologic features

【125】Gross Pathology

【126】Typically circumscribed，round to oval mass， often with a variegated， lobular cut surface； usually tan to gray-white

【127】**May be variable in size ranging from less thanl cm to greater than 10 cm**

【128】Usually solitary and unicentric， but bilateral cases have been reported

【129】Typically solid but occasionally shows cystic degeneration

【130】Often shows marked hemorrhage， necrosis， or calcification

【131】Invasion into adjacent organs and soft tissue may be seen

【132】Histopathology

【133】Cellular， small round blue cell tumor with vague lobular architecture

【134】Nodular aggregates of tumor cells separated by delicate fibrovascular septa

【135】Prominent Homer-Wright pseudorosettes (round spaces surrounded by palisading peripheral nuclei and filled with a faintly eosinophilic fibrillary matrix) may be seen

【136】Fibrillar matrix representing neuritic cell processes； resembles neuropil of the central nervous system

【137】Cells are medium sized and round to oval with high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and scant cytoplasm； hyperchromatic nuclei have stippled chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli

【138】Hemorrhage and microcalcifications are common findings

【139】**Variable mitotic activity**

【141】Neuroblastoma Pathology Committee \[INPC\])： the criteria divide tumors into subtypes

【142】_Neuroblastoma， undifferentiated： small， medium， or_ large round neuroblasts showing lack of differentiation or neuropil by routine light microscopy

_—Neuroblastoma， undifferentiated， pleomorphic_ subtype： neuroblasts are large， with pleomorphic|删除0换行|nuclei， prominent nucleoli， and moderate to abundant cytoplasm (some cells may have rhabdoid features)； no neuropil

【144】_—Neuroblastoma， poorly differentiated： less than 5%_ neuroblasts show synchronous differentiation toward ganglion cells

【145】_—Neuroblastoma， differentiating： more than 5%_ neuroblasts show synchronous differentiation toward ganglion cells

【146】Mitosis karyorrhexis index (MKI) is based on percentage seen in 10 high-power fields (total of5000 cells)： less than 2% (low)， 2% to 4%(intermediate)， and more than 4%(high)

【147】Assessment of the MKI is crucial because it is used to determine prognostic categories (unfavorable versus favorable histology) in combination with the tumor differentiation and age of the patient

【93】**HISTOLOGY OF THE OVARY**

【94】**SURFACE EPITHELIUM AND EPITHELIALINCLUSION**

【95】CYSTSS The ovaries are covered by a single layer of modified peritoneal cells that vary from flat to columnar. The surface epithelium is separated from the underlying stroma by a dis-tinct basement membrane 通用删除6(英):<u>\[1\]</u>.

【96】Epithelial inclusion cysts are considered invaginations of the surface epithelium that have lost any connection with the surface. With advancing age， the frequency of inclusion cysts increases. The epithelium of the cysts may become hyperplas-tic or undergo metaplasia into different miillerian cell types(ciliated， mucinous， endometrioid， or even transitional). Epi-thelial inclusion cysts are thought to result from scarring fol-lowing ovulation. It is widely accepted that they are responsible for the development of benign， borderline， or malignant epi-thelial-stromal ovarian tumors 通用删除6(英):<u>\[2\]</u>.

【97】STROMA The ovarian cortical stromais composed of spin-dle-shaped cells arranged in whorls with a storiform pattern. In womenin the reproductive age group， the stroma contains folli-cles，corpora lutea， and corpora albicantia. Some of the stromal cells may exhibit microscopic features associated with steroid hormone production， such as condensation or luteinization. The ovarian cortical stroma may occasionally contain other ele-ments such as bundles of smooth muscle， decidual cells， fat cells， cortical poorly defined granulomas， and sears.

【98】**FOLLICLES AND DERIVATIVESSTThe ovarian stroma con-tains follicles in different stages of maturation (primordial，pri-mary， secondary， graafian). The number of primordial follicles is estimated to be approx 400，000 at birth.**

【99】Primordial follicles are composed of a primary oocyte sur-rounded by a single layer of inconspicuous granulosa cells. After gonadotropin stimulation， the oocyte enlarges and the granulosa cells become polygonal (primary follicle).

【100】Follicular maturation produces changes in the morphology of the follicles (secondary follicles). Granulosa cells prolifer-ate and become stratified (preantral follicle)， and the surround-ing cortical stroma differentiate into both theca interna and externa. 【9】### 71 Stroke in adults, etiologies

【12】#### Introduction

【13】Strokes are defined as a sudden, non-convulsive, focal neurologic deficit that continues for more than 24 hours. Strokes are the third most common cause of death and one of the leading causes of serious, long-term disability in the USA. Over a year, about 795,000 people suffer from strokes, and more than 140,000 people die in the USA.

【14】Risk factors for stroke include hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, intracranial disease, atrial fibrillation, and tobacco usage. This chapter focuses upon ischemic stroke.

【15】The following are the objectives of this chapter:

【16】*   Systematically approach acute focal neurologic deficits.
*   Approach common etiologies of stroke, particularly ischemic etiology.
*   Emphasize basic stroke work-up.
*   Discuss evaluation of acute stroke management.
*   Discuss overall secondary prevention options for ischemic strokes.

【17】#### Types of stroke

【18】Strokes are classified as cardioembolic, artery to artery, and lacunar. A basic stroke work-up includes brain imaging, transthoracic echocardiogram, investigation of intra- and extracranial arteries, and risk stratifications (hgA1C, lipid panel). Other work-up to consider ordering depending on clinical circumstances includes investigation of prothrombic state – protein C, protein S, antithrombin III, factor V Leiden, and homocysteine.

【19】#### Anatomy

【20】A solid understanding of cerebral arterial architecture is needed for localizing lesions. There are two categories of findings when investigating the location of a stroke lesion – cortical deficits and brainstem deficits. Cortically based deficits involve functions such as language, attention, visual field deficits, and apraxia. Brainstem-based deficits involve oculomotor dysfunction, swallowing, and forehead-involved facial paresis and may be associated with ataxia, discoordinated speech, nystagmus, and vertigo. Cerebellar lesions may be associated with ataxia, discoordinated speech, nystagmus, and vertigo.

【3】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【4】 Paget’s disease of bone: The pattern seen on the radionuclide bone scan is that of regions of markedly increased bone tracer accumulation with an expanded appearance to the entire bone. These features are typical of Paget’s disease, the most likely diagnosis.

【5】 Metastases: Metastases can simulate lesions of Paget’s bone disease. The advanced degree of tracer accumulation and expanded bone appearance seen in this case, however, are atypical even for advanced prostate, breast, or lung carcinoma. This diagnosis is an unlikely consideration.

【6】 Fractures: The expanded bone and diffuse tracer accumulation make fractures unlikely considerations.

【7】 Osteomyelitis: Regions of intense tracer accumulation can be seen in osteomyelitis, but the clinical setting, the diffuse nature of the abnormalities, and the expansile changes seen on the radiograph make this diagnosis highly unlikely.

【8】 Fibrous dysplasia: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia can produce increased tracer accumulation in multiple bones, as is seen in this case. However, the history of progressive bony expansion late in life and the radio-graphic findings make this diagnosis unlikely.

【9】DIAGNOSIS

【10】Paget’s disease of bone

【11】KEY FACTS

【12】Clinical

【13】 Paget’s disease is most commonly encountered in Eastern and Western Europe (with the exception of Scandinavia), with a prevalence of 3.5% to 4.5% and with a 3 to 2 male-to-female predominance.

【14】 The etiology of Paget’s disease is not known definitively. Slow virus inoculation early in life is one hypothesis that has been strongly considered.

【15】 Progression of Paget’s disease can be classified into three stages: (1) bone resorption, (2) mixed bone resorp-tion and deformation, and (3) decline in resorption accompanied by a decrease in irregularity and fibrosis.

【16】 The prevalence of fractures in Paget’s disease is reported to be 8% to 18%, based on retrospective series.

【55】Radiologic

【56】 The majority of metastatic bone tumors appear as focal regions of increased radiotracer accumulation on radionuclide bone scan. However, photopenic foci can be seen in malignancies such as breast, lung, renal, and anaplastic carcinomas; neuroblastoma; and multiple myeloma.

【57】 Soft tissue neoplasms can invade bone and produce increased radiotracer uptake or a photopenic focus, which usually has a rim of increased radiotracer accumulation.

【58】 Benign bone conditions that can appear photopenic include bone infarction, bone resection, very early osteomyelitis, radiation-induced bone changes, and histiocytosis X.

【59】 Skeletal involvement from multiple myeloma, plasma-cytoma, neuroblastoma, and eosinophilic granuloma can produce normal, increased, or decreased radio-tracer accumulation.

【86】KEY FACTS

【87】Clinical

【88】 Hypercalcemia can occur secondary to a number of entities, including hyperparathyroidism, metastatic skeletal disease, hyperthyroidism, and sarcoidosis.

The biphos-phonates interact with the hydroxyapatite crystal, inhibiting bone resorption, and may impair osteoclast function. These agents are also used to treat Paget’s disease and heterotopic ossification and may have a role in treating osteoporosis.

The biphosphonate used and the method of administration (oral or intravenous) may make a difference in the effect on the bone scan. 【86】KEY FACTS

【87】Clinical

【88】 Hypercalcemia can occur secondary to a number of entities, including hyperparathyroidism, metastatic skeletal disease, hyperthyroidism, and sarcoidosis.

【89】 Biphosphonates such as etidronate and pamidronate are used to treat the hypercalcemia of malignancy because of their effect on bone turnover. The biphos-phonates interact with the hydroxyapatite crystal, inhibiting bone resorption, and may impair osteoclast function. These agents are also used to treat Paget’s disease and heterotopic ossification and may have a role in treating osteoporosis.

【90】 Radionuclide bone scans in patients with hypercalcemia and elevated calcium phosphorus products frequently show abnormal localization of the radiopharmaceutical in the lungs, stomach, and kidneys, reflecting the acid-base changes that occur in these tissues. Furthermore, these are the sites of metastatic calcification that can occur in these patients.

The biphosphonate used and the method of administration (oral or intravenous) may make a difference in the effect on the bone scan. Some studies report difficulty in interpretation of radionu-clide bone scans in patients undergoing biphosphonate therapy, whereas other studies have shown no effect on the sensitivity of the bone scan.

【93】 A Tc-99m MDP bone scan that shows poor bone uptake and prominent soft tissue accumulation usually results from a radiopharmaceutical preparation problem, with excess Tc-99m pertechnetate in the preparation. The excess pertechnetate is manifested by radiotracer accumulation in the thyroid and stomach.

【94】 The clue to the diagnosis in the patient shown above is accumulation of the Tc-99m MDP in the lungs, which occurs with hypercalcemia. In a patient with accumulation of Tc-99m MDP in the lungs, associated bone scan findings should be considered as possibly related to hypercalcemia or its treatment.

【95】 Radionuclide bone scans usually provide diagnostic information in patients receiving biphosphonates, but as noted above, this agent can affect the scan. The effect of this therapy needs to be taken into account when interpreting the images.

【18】 Elevated cardiac output is seen in some patients with Paget’s disease due to the increased vascularity of acute pagetoid bone.

【20】 On radiographs, vertebrae appear enlarged and deformed; the scapulae and pelvic bones appear expanded and thickened; the skull enlarges with basi-lar flattening and cortical thickening; and the long bones bow and develop cortical thickening.

【21】 The degree of radiotracer accumulation in pagetoid bone is variable.

【22】 The radionuclide study is reported to be more sensitive than radiographs: 5% to 20% of patients have abnormal bone scans and normal radiographs, compared to 1% with abnormal radiographs and normal radionuclide bone scan.

【23】 Bone scan findings do not correlate well with the severity of bone pain in Paget’s disease.

【24】 Reduced accumulation of In-111-labeled leukocytes and of Tc-99m sulfur colloid has been reported to occur in Paget’s disease.

【25】 Photopenic regions can be seen in pagetoid bone in instances of sarcomatous degeneration, most likely due to proliferation of nonosteoblastic tissue.

【26】 A photopenic area in a bone scan that occurs in a radio-graphically evident region of Paget’s disease can represent either early disease or sarcomatous degeneration.

【27】 Ga-67 may be useful for sarcoma detection. 【43】 Metastases: Bone metastases can appear on bone scans as any or all of the following: multiple foci of increased radiotracer accumulation , increased or decreased radiotracer accumulation , and normal bone radiotracer accumulation. The pattern and location of the abnormalities in Figures 10-7A and 10-7C make bone metastases the most likely consideration.

【44】 Pathologic fractures: Pathologic fractures can be solitary or multiple and usually occur in metastatic bone lesions that are subject to stress or trauma. Bone metastases in weight-bearing regions are particularly susceptible to fracture.

【45】 Multiple benign fractures: The pattern, location, and clinical history are important in distinguishing benign fractures from metastatic disease. Some patterns of fractures 通用删除1(英):<u></u> are typical of benign fractures. This is the diagnosis in patient B.

【47】DIAGNOSIS

【48】Patients A and C: multiple bone metastases; Patient B: benign rib fractures

【49】KEY FACTS

【50】Clinical

【51】 The likelihood of bone metastases depends on the primary tumor (e.g. most primary bone tumors rarely metastasize) and the stage of disease.

【52】 The lifetime risk of developing breast cancer in American women is reported to be approximately 11%, and over one-half of breast cancers occur in women after the age of 65 years. In autopsy series of women with metastatic breast carcinoma, the frequency of bone metastases has been reported to be between 44% and 71%.

【53】 The digital rectal examination and serum PSA test are currently the recommended screening procedures for prostate carcinoma. Approximately one-third of men over the age of 50 years harbor foci of prostatic carcinoma without clinical evidence of disease.

【54】 Approximately 80% of patients with detectable prostate carcinoma and distant metastases are found to have bone metastases.

【55】Radiologic

【56】 The majority of metastatic bone tumors appear as focal regions of increased radiotracer accumulation on radionuclide bone scan. However, photopenic foci can be seen in malignancies such as breast, lung, renal, and anaplastic carcinomas; neuroblastoma; and multiple myeloma.

【57】 Soft tissue neoplasms can invade bone and produce increased radiotracer uptake or a photopenic focus, which usually has a rim of increased radiotracer accumulation.

【58】 Benign bone conditions that can appear photopenic include bone infarction, bone resection, very early osteomyelitis, radiation-induced bone changes, and histiocytosis X.

【59】 Skeletal involvement from multiple myeloma, plasma-cytoma, neuroblastoma, and eosinophilic granuloma can produce normal, increased, or decreased radio-tracer accumulation.

【60】 Particular care must be taken in evaluating the radio-nuclide bone imaging study of a patient with bone metastases during the first 4 to 6 months after starting chemotherapy, because a disparity between the clini-cal/radiologic status and findings on radionuclide bone scan can be seen. These patients can improve clinically and have a decrease in the number and size of bone lesions on radiographs but no change or apparent worsening of lesions (the so-called flare phenomenon) on the radionuclide bone imaging study. This pattern change presumably reflects healing of lesions and is most commonly reported in bone metastases from a primary breast or prostate tumor. Following further healing of bone lesions after this initial period, the radionuclide bone study reflects the clinical and radiologic status more accurately.

【61】 Patients with a PSA value of <10 ng/mL during their initial evaluation for prostate carcinoma have a very low likelihood of having a positive radionuclide bone imaging study for metastases.

【62】 The likelihood of a solitary bone scan lesion being a metastasis is reported to range from 10% (in adults) to 60% (in children).

【63】 In the presence of a known primary malignancy, approximately 10% to 20% of solitary rib lesions on bone scans are metastases. On the other hand, focal rib lesions having a string-of-pearls pattern are highly likely to be benign rib fractures.

【64】 Correlation with radiographs or other imaging studies is often useful to confirm the presence of bone metas-tases in patients with bone scan abnormalities. In the presence of an abnormal radionuclide bone scan, a normal radiograph actually makes a bone metastasis a likely consideration by excluding other possible causes.

【3】DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS

【4】 Paget’s disease of bone: The pattern seen on the radionuclide bone scan is that of regions of markedly increased bone tracer accumulation with an expanded appearance to the entire bone. These features are typical of Paget’s disease, the most likely diagnosis.

【5】 Metastases: Metastases can simulate lesions of Paget’s bone disease. The advanced degree of tracer accumulation and expanded bone appearance seen in this case, however, are atypical even for advanced prostate, breast, or lung carcinoma. This diagnosis is an unlikely consideration.

【6】 Fractures: The expanded bone and diffuse tracer accumulation make fractures unlikely considerations.

【7】 Osteomyelitis: Regions of intense tracer accumulation can be seen in osteomyelitis, but the clinical setting, the diffuse nature of the abnormalities, and the expansile changes seen on the radiograph make this diagnosis highly unlikely.

【8】 Fibrous dysplasia: Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia can produce increased tracer accumulation in multiple bones, as is seen in this case. However, the history of progressive bony expansion late in life and the radio-graphic findings make this diagnosis unlikely.

【10】Paget’s disease of bone

【11】KEY FACTS

【12】Clinical

【13】 Paget’s disease is most commonly encountered in Eastern and Western Europe (with the exception of Scandinavia), with a prevalence of 3.5% to 4.5% and with a 3 to 2 male-to-female predominance.

【14】 The etiology of Paget’s disease is not known definitively. Slow virus inoculation early in life is one hypothesis that has been strongly considered.

【15】 Progression of Paget’s disease can be classified into three stages: (1) bone resorption, (2) mixed bone resorp-tion and deformation, and (3) decline in resorption accompanied by a decrease in irregularity and fibrosis.

【16】 The prevalence of fractures in Paget’s disease is reported to be 8% to 18%, based on retrospective series.

【17】 Sarcomatous degeneration of pagetoid bone can occur and can be solitary or multicentric.

【18】 Elevated cardiac output is seen in some patients with Paget’s disease due to the increased vascularity of acute pagetoid bone.

【19】Radiologic

【20】 On radiographs, vertebrae appear enlarged and deformed; the scapulae and pelvic bones appear expanded and thickened; the skull enlarges with basi-lar flattening and cortical thickening; and the long bones bow and develop cortical thickening.

【21】 The degree of radiotracer accumulation in pagetoid bone is variable.

【22】 The radionuclide study is reported to be more sensitive than radiographs: 5% to 20% of patients have abnormal bone scans and normal radiographs, compared to 1% with abnormal radiographs and normal radionuclide bone scan.

【23】 Bone scan findings do not correlate well with the severity of bone pain in Paget’s disease.

【24】 Reduced accumulation of In-111-labeled leukocytes and of Tc-99m sulfur colloid has been reported to occur in Paget’s disease.

【25】 Photopenic regions can be seen in pagetoid bone in instances of sarcomatous degeneration, most likely due to proliferation of nonosteoblastic tissue.

【26】 A photopenic area in a bone scan that occurs in a radio-graphically evident region of Paget’s disease can represent either early disease or sarcomatous degeneration.

【27】 Ga-67 may be useful for sarcoma detection. In one small study, slightly more than half of Paget’s disease patients with sarcomas and a focal photopenic area on bone scan were found to have increased Ga-67 accumulation at the site of the sarcoma. Another small series found the Ga-67 scan to be less sensitive.

The pattern and location of the abnormalities in Figures 10-7A and 10-7C make bone metastases the most likely consideration.

【44】 Pathologic fractures: Pathologic fractures can be solitary or multiple and usually occur in metastatic bone lesions that are subject to stress or trauma. Bone metastases in weight-bearing regions are particularly susceptible to fracture.

【47】DIAGNOSIS

【48】Patients A and C: multiple bone metastases; Patient B: benign rib fractures

【49】KEY FACTS

【50】Clinical

【51】 The likelihood of bone metastases depends on the primary tumor (e.g. most primary bone tumors rarely metastasize) and the stage of disease.

【52】 The lifetime risk of developing breast cancer in American women is reported to be approximately 11%, and over one-half of breast cancers occur in women after the age of 65 years. In autopsy series of women with metastatic breast carcinoma, the frequency of bone metastases has been reported to be between 44% and 71%.

【53】 The digital rectal examination and serum PSA test are currently the recommended screening procedures for prostate carcinoma. Approximately one-third of men over the age of 50 years harbor foci of prostatic carcinoma without clinical evidence of disease.

【54】 Approximately 80% of patients with detectable prostate carcinoma and distant metastases are found to have bone metastases.

【55】Radiologic

【56】 The majority of metastatic bone tumors appear as focal regions of increased radiotracer accumulation on radionuclide bone scan. However, photopenic foci can be seen in malignancies such as breast, lung, renal, and anaplastic carcinomas; neuroblastoma; and multiple myeloma.

【57】 Soft tissue neoplasms can invade bone and produce increased radiotracer uptake or a photopenic focus, which usually has a rim of increased radiotracer accumulation.

【58】 Benign bone conditions that can appear photopenic include bone infarction, bone resection, very early osteomyelitis, radiation-induced bone changes, and histiocytosis X.

【59】 Skeletal involvement from multiple myeloma, plasma-cytoma, neuroblastoma, and eosinophilic granuloma can produce normal, increased, or decreased radio-tracer accumulation.

【60】 Particular care must be taken in evaluating the radio-nuclide bone imaging study of a patient with bone metastases during the first 4 to 6 months after starting chemotherapy, because a disparity between the clini-cal/radiologic status and findings on radionuclide bone scan can be seen. These patients can improve clinically and have a decrease in the number and size of bone lesions on radiographs but no change or apparent worsening of lesions (the so-called flare phenomenon) on the radionuclide bone imaging study. This pattern change presumably reflects healing of lesions and is most commonly reported in bone metastases from a primary breast or prostate tumor. Following further healing of bone lesions after this initial period, the radionuclide bone study reflects the clinical and radiologic status more accurately.

【61】 Patients with a PSA value of <10 ng/mL during their initial evaluation for prostate carcinoma have a very low likelihood of having a positive radionuclide bone imaging study for metastases.

【62】 The likelihood of a solitary bone scan lesion being a metastasis is reported to range from 10% (in adults) to 60% (in children).

【63】 In the presence of a known primary malignancy, approximately 10% to 20% of solitary rib lesions on bone scans are metastases. On the other hand, focal rib lesions having a string-of-pearls pattern are highly likely to be benign rib fractures.

【64】 Correlation with radiographs or other imaging studies is often useful to confirm the presence of bone metas-tases in patients with bone scan abnormalities. In the presence of an abnormal radionuclide bone scan, a normal radiograph actually makes a bone metastasis a likely consideration by excluding other possible causes.

【79】 Administration of incorrect radiopharmaceutical: This diagnosis is unlikely because no radiopharmaceu-tical has the pattern of distribution seen in this patient.

【80】 Presence of excess aluminum ion: Contamination of Tc-99m methylene diphosphonate (MDP) with aluminum ion from the eluate or the presence of high plasma aluminum levels in patients taking aluminum hydroxide antacids can alter biodistribution of the radiophar-maceutical agent. 【81】 Effect of therapy for hypercalcemia: The patient shown above was receiving intravenously administered etidronate for treatment of hypercalcemia. Etidronate (hydroxyethylidene diphosphonic acid \[HEDP\]) inhibits the formation, growth, and dissolution of hydroxyap-atite crystals. This agent can cause the lack of radio-pharmaceutical accumulation within bones, as shown above.

【82】 Premature imaging: Images obtained immediately after administration of Tc-99m MDP will typically show blood pool activity, prominent soft tissue activity, and some bone accumulation. However, accumulation in the lungs would not be expected, making this diagnosis unlikely.

【83】 Iron overload: This diagnosis might be considered because in iron overload, such as in hemochromatosis or following multiple blood transfusions, the accumulation of Tc-99m MDP into bone is diminished and renal excretion is increased. However, pulmonary deposition of the radiotracer would not be expected.

【85】Hypercalcemia with etidronate therapy

【86】KEY FACTS

【87】Clinical

【88】 Hypercalcemia can occur secondary to a number of entities, including hyperparathyroidism, metastatic skeletal disease, hyperthyroidism, and sarcoidosis.

【89】 Biphosphonates such as etidronate and pamidronate are used to treat the hypercalcemia of malignancy because of their effect on bone turnover. The biphos-phonates interact with the hydroxyapatite crystal, inhibiting bone resorption, and may impair osteoclast function. These agents are also used to treat Paget’s disease and heterotopic ossification and may have a role in treating osteoporosis.

【90】 Radionuclide bone scans in patients with hypercalcemia and elevated calcium phosphorus products frequently show abnormal localization of the radiopharmaceutical in the lungs, stomach, and kidneys, reflecting the acid-base changes that occur in these tissues. Furthermore, these are the sites of metastatic calcification that can occur in these patients.

【91】 The effect of biphosphonates on Tc-99m MDP bone scans is variable. The biphosphonate used and the method of administration (oral or intravenous) may make a difference in the effect on the bone scan. Some studies report difficulty in interpretation of radionu-clide bone scans in patients undergoing biphosphonate therapy, whereas other studies have shown no effect on the sensitivity of the bone scan.

【92】Radiologic

【93】 A Tc-99m MDP bone scan that shows poor bone uptake and prominent soft tissue accumulation usually results from a radiopharmaceutical preparation problem, with excess Tc-99m pertechnetate in the preparation. The excess pertechnetate is manifested by radiotracer accumulation in the thyroid and stomach.

【94】 The clue to the diagnosis in the patient shown above is accumulation of the Tc-99m MDP in the lungs, which occurs with hypercalcemia. In a patient with accumulation of Tc-99m MDP in the lungs, associated bone scan findings should be considered as possibly related to hypercalcemia or its treatment.

【95】 Radionuclide bone scans usually provide diagnostic information in patients receiving biphosphonates, but as noted above, this agent can affect the scan. The effect of this therapy needs to be taken into account when interpreting the images.
