【1】**CASE SCENARIO**

【2】**Emergency medical services \[EMS\] arrive at the emergency department with a 52-year-old White male who awoke from sleep with chest pain. His initial blood pressure was 136/70 mmHg， pulse was 109 beats per minute， respira-tory rate was 14 breaths per minute， oxygen saturation was 100% on room air， and he was afebrile. The emergency physician asks the patient the following questions to obtain a historu：**

【3】**Q： Can you tell me what happened tonight to bring you to the emergency department?**

【4】A： I had chest pain that woke me up.

【5】**Q： What time did this occur?**

【6】A： About midnight.

【7】Q： Can you tell me where the pain is located? A： Right here under my breastbone \[patient points to his sternum\].

【8】**Q： What did you do when you first felt the pain?**

【9】A： I got up， it seemed better， but not much， and then I took some TUMS thinking it was indigestion-but it didn’t help.

【10】**Q： Did the pain get better or worse with any movement or activity? A： No， I don't think so.**

【11】**Q： Did you have any other symptoms associated with the pain? A： No.**

【12】**Q： What level was your pain initially on a scale of 0 to 10 (0 being no pain， 10 being severe)， and what is it now?**

【13】A： It was a 10 but got better once the paramedics gave me aspirin. Now it's a 7 out of 10.

【14】**Q： Do you have any history of heart disease? A： No.**

【15】**Q： Do you have any history of high blood pressure， high cholesterol， diabetes， or smoking?**

【16】零碎段删除-1:<u>**A： No.**</u>

【17】The emergency physician obtains an ECG， which does not show any ischemia. Sublingual nitroglycerin is administered but does not improve the patient's symptoms. Initial vital signs are within normal limits except for mild tachycardia (heart rate of 110 beats per minute). Labs are drawn， which are notable only for a troponin T level of 0.09 ng/mL and a white blood cell (WBC) count of 11，000. The chest radiograph is also unremark-able. An exam is performed and is negative for any findings.

【18】The emergency physician calls the on-call cardiovascular clinician at0300 to evaluate this patient， who is believed to be havinganon-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). The emergency physician summarizes the information (history A) to the cardiovascular clinician.

【19】**HISTORY A**

【20】_A52-year-old White man with no prior cardiac history and no cardiac risk factors_ _comes into the emergency department via EMS with complaints of substernal_ _chest pain that awoke him from sleep around midnight. He thought the pain was_ _indigestion and took TUMS， but it did not improve， so he called 911. He denies_ _the pain being associated with movement. Initially， the pain was 10 out of 10 on_ _a pain scale. Paramedics gave him 4 chewable baby aspirin， which gave him some_ _relief， bringing the pain to 7 out of 10. He’s received 1 sublingual nitroglycerin_ _tablet in the emergency department with no further relief of pain. His exam was_ _unremarkable. The initial ECG appears normal； however， his initial troponin T_ _is 0.09 ng/mL. Basic chemistry panel and complete blood count (CBC) are other-wise normal except for a mildly elevated WBC count of 11，000. Chest radiograph_ _is unremarkable for any acute process._

【21】Based on the preceding information， the cardiovascular clinician is already formulating a differential diagnosis. It sounds as though this patient could be having a NSTEMI， but in order to confirm this diagno-sis， more information needs to be gathered， and quickly， to ensure timely treatment.

【22】Before we examine how the next history is taken， are there any key features missing from the initial history taken by the emergency physi-cian? Was that history detailed enough to lead you to the right diagnosis? Let us see what other questions the cardiovascular clinician asks to fur-ther evaluate the chief complaint.

【23】Upon evaluating the patient， the following vital signs are obtained：Blood pressure， 138/72； pulse， 105 beats per minute； respiratory rate，16 breaths per minute； oxygen saturation， 99% on room air； and the patient is afebrile. The cardiovascular clinician asks the patient the fol-lowing questions：

【24】**Q： What brings you to the emergency department?**

【25】A： I had chest pain that woke me from sleep.

【26】**Q： What time was that?**

【27】A： Around midnight.

【28】**Q： Can you describe the pain for me? Is it sharp， burning， dull， or does it feel like a pressure or squeezing sensation? Have you had this pain before?**

【29】A： It was sharp at first， now it’s dull. I've never felt anything like this.

【30】**Q： Where is it located?**

【31】A： Right here in the center of my chest. \[The patient points to his sternum.

【32】**Q： What is your level of pain now on a scale of 0 to10? A： Around a7.**

【33】**Q： Do you notice the pain radiating to your back， jaw， neck， or arms? A： No-it’s staying right there.**

【34】**Q： Are you short of breath， dizzy， nauseous， or sweaty with this pain or were you when it first occurred or did you feel an acid taste in your mouth or burning with it?**

【35】A： No， none of that.

【36】**Q： Have you been lightheaded with this pain or have you passed out from it?**

【37】零碎段删除-1:<u>**A： No.**</u>

【38】**Q： I heard that you took TUMS to alleviate the pain. Did this help at all? How long did you wait before you took it?**

【39】A： I got out of bed and the pain was a little less sharp， but it didn’t go away so after 10 minutes or so I took some TUMS. It didn't help at all.

【40】**Q： The aspirin they gave you helped some，right， but not the nitroglycerin?**

【41】A： Yes， the aspirin did seem to take the edge off， but I didn’t notice any change with the nitroglycerin.

【42】**Q： Does any movement make it better or worse； for example， moving your arms or sitting up versus lying down?**

【43】A： No. \[He moves around in the bed.\]I don't think so. I haven't tried lying down again since I woke up.

【44】**Q： I noticed you said the pain became less sharp when you got out of bed. Let me try something. (Currently the patient is lying at a 45-degree angle in the bed； the bed is adjusted to a supine position for a few minutes and then is lifted to a 90-degree angle.) Did you notice your pain changing at all as I repositioned you in the bed?**

【45】A： Yes-in fact I feel much better sitting up like this. The pain is less sharp.

【46】**Q： What is your pain level when you sit upright versus when you were lying flat?**

【47】A： It went back up to a 10 out of 10 lying down， but now it’s about a 5 out of 10 sitting up.

【48】**Q： Do you feel the pain gets worse as you take a deep breath?**

【49】A： \[Patient proceeds to take a deep breath and winces at end of inspiration.\] Yes.

【50】**Q： Have you been sick recently， traveled recently， or been exposed to anyone who has been sick?**

【51】A： I haven't traveled anywhere， but I had the flu about a week ago.

【52】**Q： What were your symptoms at that time? Did you have cough， chest pain， or fever?**

【53】A： I had a cough， congestion， and fever， although I never checked it. But I had chills. I still feel really run down. No energy.

【54】**Q： Were you on any medication for your symptoms and do you take any medications on a daily basis?**

【55】A： I took some decongestant and Tylenol， but nothing else. I only take a daily multivitamin and fish oil capsules at night.

【56】**Q： Have you ever had a heart attack or stroke? Or do you have a history of high blood pressure， diabetes， or clots to your lungs or legs?**

【57】零碎段删除-1:<u>**A： No.**</u>

【58】**Q： Do you exercise?**

【59】A： I cycle three times a week and lift weights twice a week.

【60】**Q： Have you done anything more strenuous than usual or feel that you have pulled any muscles?**

【61】A： No， I haven't worked out in 2 weeks because I was sick.

【62】**Q： Prior to tonight and even before your illness， have you felt more tired， had decreased endurance， or experienced any shortness of breath or chest pain?**

【63】零碎段删除-1:<u>**A： No.**</u>

【64】**Q： Have you noticed any weight loss， weight gain， or changes in your bowel or bladder patterns? A： No.**

【65】**Q： Tell me about your day yesterday before going to bed last night. Did you do anything out of the ordinary or eat anything spicy or unusual for your diet?**

【66】A： No. I haven’t had much of an appetite so I had some soup for dinner. I spent the whole day at home.

【67】The patient's chief complaint has been thoroughly evaluated at this point. The cardiovascular clinician summarizes this information in history B.

【68】**HISTORY B**

【69】_A 52-year-old White male with a recent history ofpresumed flu presents to the_ _emergency department via EMS with complaints of substernal chest pain that_ _awoke him from sleep around midnight. He has no past cardiac history or car-diac risk factors. His only symptom leading up to this episode was fatigue. He_ _describes the pain as sharp， nonradiating， worse with deep breathing and lying_ _down， and better with sitting upright and forward. He has not pulled any mus-cles recently or done any unusual activity or eaten anything out of the ordinary_ _for his diet. The pain is not associated with shortness of breath， nausea or 丫om-iting， syncope， near syncope， or diaphoresis. He attempted to alleviate the pain_ _with TUMS； however， that was unsuccessful._

【70】_While in route to the emergency department he was treated with aspirin， which_ _was somewhat effective in lessening the pain. Nitroglycerin did not give any fur-ther improvement and he currently states his pain is 5 out of 10 sitting upright._

【71】Utilizing only the history and no objective data， is a diagnosis of NSTEMI still at the top of your differential?

【72】**KEY FEATURES OF THE HISTORY**

【73】The first history obtained (history A) seemed to be thorough， initially. It provided relevant and key information that was organized in a way that would likely lead any provider to a diagnosis of NSTEMI. Upon closer examination， however， the objective data， in conjunction with the history are what essentially narrowed your thinking to this conclusior， right? Does that still hold true with history B? Did you need the objective data to change your differential diagnosis? Let us go back to the earlier question. What， if any， key features were missing from the initial history?

【74】**Character**

【75】The character of the chest pain was identified in history A by asking the patient where the pain was located and the severity of pain. In history B， no questions were asked about what type of pain it was， or whether the pain radiated anywhere else.

【76】In history B， the cardiovascular clinician asked detailed questions about whether the pain was a pressure， more of a dull ache， or was sharp. In addi-tion， the patient was asked if the pain radiated to his neck， jaw， arms， or back. Every patient's perception of pain is different. It is important to iden-tify the type of pain (sharp versus pressure) being experienced， particularly when talking about the chest as this symptom can drastically change the differential diagnosis.

【77】**Timing and Duration**

In both history A and history B， the patient was asked at what time of the day the pain occurred. The patient also disclosed what he was doing when it occurred. Pain that either awakens someone from sleep or occurs at rest can be a classic sign of an acute coronary syndrome or unstable angina， which makes this statement a key point of the patient’s history. Duration was not directly asked， but it was clear that the patient was having ongoing pain without|删除0换行|complete relief. In history B. the patient was asked if he had experienced this type of pain before. Addressing the frequency is an important point to establish for pain that might be consistent with a pattern of unstable angina.

【79】**Associated Symptoms**

【80】Both providers asked the patient whether any other symptoms were asso-ciated with his pain. Although the answer was the same， how they asked the question was very different.

【81】In history A， the patient was asked if he was having any other symp-toms with his pain. In history B， the patient was asked whether he was feeling short of breath， nauseous， dizzy， sweaty， or had an acid taste in his mouth. These symptoms often occur in tandem with chest pain in situations of acute coronary syndromes and with other causes of chest pain， such as aortic dissection， gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)， and pulmonary embolism， to name a few. The patient may not be able to identify that he had other symptoms if not prompted directly about those symptoms， which may have led to a false response when the pro-vider in history A asked the question.

【82】In addition， the provider in history B was thorough in asking the patient how he was feeling leading up to the event， including recent ill-nesses and exercise. In this line of questioning， the cardiovascular clini-cian was trying to determine whether the pain was associated with illness or caused by a pulled muscle. The fact that the patient had a recent history of viral illness is crucial in determining the right diagnosis， as you will soon see.

【83】**Mitigating or Alleviating Factors**

【84】The provider in history A asked the patient what he did when he first felt the pain. He was asked a vague question about whether movement changed the pain， but was not asked specifically about what type of movement. This question yielded a false negative response from the patient. He gave away a key detail， though， that went unnoticed by the first provider， but was astutely caught by the second provider. The patient noted that when he stood， the pain was slightly better.
He relayed this observation in passing， though， and clearly did not recognize its importance. He took TUMS， which did not help to allevi-ate the pain， but the aspirin that the paramedics gave him did improve his pain to some degree.

【85】When the second provider asked the patient if any movement made the pain better or worse， it was noted that the patient felt some differ-ence upon standing and the provider questioned the patient about it. This information prompted the change in bed position to demonstrate this finding further. The patient was unaware of the connection until he was asked. In fact， putting the patient in an upright position was the only thing that improved his pain at all other than the aspirin. This was a critical piece of information that demonstrates the importance of paying close attention to everything the patient says. The patient was also asked whether deep breathing changed the pain， which it did. He again was unable to make this connection on his own without prompt-ing from the provider. The positional nature of the pain as well as the relief with an anti-inflammatory should have definitely steered your thinking away from a diagnosis of NSTEMI.

【86】**KEY FEATURES OF THE DATA**

【87】The key features of the data relevant to this patient's chief complaint are the vital signs， ECG， chest radiograph， and biomarkers and lab results. In addition， other data such as the medication list and relevant medical history need to be taken into consideration.

【88】**Vital Signs**

【89】The following findings are reported at the time the cardiovascular clini-cian evaluates the patient：

【90】_Blood pressure： 138/70mmHg_

【91】**Pulse： 95 beats per minute**

【92】Respirations： 16 breaths per minute

【93】**_Oxygen saturation： 99% on room air_**

【94】_Temperature： 37.0°℃_

【95】A subsequent blood pressure reading is taken in each arm with the following results： right， 136/65 mmHg， left， 132/70 mmHg. This patient is slightly tachycardic， which can be a normal response in someone who is in pain. This finding is noteworthy as it can be indicative of pulmonary embolus as well as pericarditis.

【96】**Electrocardiogram \[ECG\]**

【97】The ECG is read as sinus tachycardia without any acute abnormalities. The cardiovascular clinician carefully reviews the ECG and notes sinus tachycardia without any signs of ischemia such as ST-segment or T-wave abnormalities. There is depression of the PR segment in all leads. There is no prior ECG for comparison. The ECG is otherwise unremarkable.

【98】**Chest Radiograph**

【99】The chest film does not demonstrate any findings of heart failure， pneu-monia， or lung disease. The mediastinum is within normal limits and there is no cardiomegaly.

【100】**Biomarkers and Lab Results**

【101】The initial troponin T level is abnormal at 0.09 ng/mL. As we learned with the case scenario in Chapter 1， modern troponin assays can rise as early as 3 to 4 hours after myocardial damage . This patient's pain awoke him from sleep around midnight and he is being evaluated in the emergency department around 3 a.m. His D-dimer level was checked and came back normal. His chemistry panel is within normal limits and shows no signs of kidney disease.

【102】An abnormal troponin level in this setting should certainly narrow your focus to a cardiac cause for his symptoms. The CBC shows no signs of anemia and platelets are normal， but the patient’s WBC is elevated at11，000. Leukocytosis is frequently a sign of inflammation. It can also be due to a coronary event such as a NSTEMI  or other cardiac conditions such as pericarditis or myopericarditis . We know that this patient had a recent viral illness， which may also contribute to the mildly abnormal WBC result.

【103】**Other Data**

【104】The patient's medications are carefully reviewed with him and are nota-ble only for a daily multivitamin and fish oil (1，000 mg) at night. He was taking over-the-counter cold and flu medicine during his viral illness. He is asked whether he had any history of cardiac disease， stroke， high blood pressure， diabetes， high cholesterol， or blood clots to his lungs or legs. Any risk factors associated with heart disease are relevant as is the absence of such. He has no past medical or surgical history other than left knee meniscus tear and repair about 10 years ago. He is an accountant and has no family history of coronary artery disease or any other cardiac problems. He does not smoke and drinks only on occasion. He denies any use of illicit drugs. He is seen by his primary care provider on a regular basis for routine physical examinations， but has never had a stress test or cardiac evaluation of any kind.

【105】Assessing whether cardiac evaluation has occurred in the past can be helpful in deciding treatment and comparing data. Whenever patients state that they have no medical history， it is imperative that providers question them about the frequency of their primary care visits. If a patient has not been seen on a regular basis， he or she may harbor many under-lying conditions that have yet to be detected. In this case， we can be reas-sured that the patient's medical history is up to date since he admits to seeing his primary care provider routinely.

【106】**DIFFERENTIALS AND DIFFERENCES IN EXAM**

【107】At this point， the top differentials should be formulated based on the key findings of the data. The physical examination can often be the deciding factor when choosing the right diagnosis and a thorough examination of the chest， lungs， abdomen， and extremities is necessary. It should also focus on any physical findings that might confirm your diagnosis.

【108】The cardiovascular clinician examines the patient. The findings are as follows：

【109】_General appearance： Well-nourished， well-developed White male. Physically fit._

【110】_Head and neck： Head is normocephalic and atraumatic， without evidence of_ _lesions or masses. Sclera are anicteric. Neck is soft and supple， without thyromeg-aly or lymphadenopathy._

【111】_Cardiac exam： No elevation of jugular venous pressure. No carotid bruits. No_ _abdominal or femoral bruits. Carotid upstroke is brisk. Peripheral pulses are pal-pable and symmetric. Auscultation of the heart reveals a regular rate and rhythm._ _S1 and S2 present. No S3 or S4. There is a pericardial friction rub best heard with_ _the patient leaning forward. This is barely audible in the supine position. Chest_ _wall is nontender to palpation._

【112】_Lungs： Clear breath sounds bilaterally with symmetric expansion. Pain noted on_ _inspiration._

【113】_Abdomen： Soft， nontender.

【4】**Sample peritoneal fluid： Peritoneal fluid may be obtained via a diagnostic para-centesis (in SBP)， or through the Tenckhoff catheter (for PD peritonitis-drain existing PD fluid or dwell dialysate for 2 hr). Fluid should be sent for cell count and differential， biochemistry (albumin， protein， glucose)， gram stain and culture.**

【5】**\- SBP is diagnosed in a patient with ascites and a cloudy ascitic tap， ascitic fluid neutrophils > 250 cells/mm or positive gram stain.**

【6】**\- PD peritonitis is diagnosed in a patient on PD who has a cloudy effluent， PD cell count>100 cells/mm(0.1 cells/mL)， neutrophils> 50% (even if cell count<100 cells/mm3) or positive gram stain. (Observe that these criteria are stricter than for SBP.)**

【7】**·Consider secondary bacterial peritonitis： Patients on PD or with ascites may still develop ‘surgical' peritonitis (e.g.， perforated viscus， diverticulitis， etc.) with spillage of gut flora. Features worrisome for secondary bacterial peritonitis include (i) focal abdominal symptoms suggestive of surgical causes， (ii) sudden onset of symptoms，(iii) polymicrobial gram stain or culture result， (iv) very low glucose (<2.8 mmol/L) or very high protein (>1 g/dL in ascitic fluid). If there is concern for secondary bac-terial peritonitis， consider performing CT abdomen to look for a perforated viscus.**

On the other hand， they are easy to exclude on bedside examination or point-of-care tests. It is advantageous to look for these diagnoses early and deliberately. 【122】**This symptomology is worrisome for a relentlessly worsening disease process.**

【123】**Malignant causes： Should these present as chronic abdominal pain， disease is usually advanced.**

【124】**__ Gastric cancer： Asymptomatic early， then vague constant epigastric pain， with no relationship to meals. Friable malignant tissue may bleed， causing anaemia， hae-matemesis and melena. Late symptoms include early satiety， vomiting of undigested food (in gastric outlet obstruction or linitis plastica)，dysphagia (in tumours near the cardia)， loss of appetite and weight or symptoms from metastatic disease.**

【125】**__ Pancreatic cancer： A cancer in the body or tail of pancreas presents late， with severe weight loss and constitutional symptoms， as well as chronic progressive epi-gastric pain radiating to the back (vs. head of pancreas tumour， which more likely presents with obstructive jaundice).**

【0】ecrosis involve nuclear changes only， and collagen is an anuclear fiber. Fibrocytes may undergo necrosis， but collagen cannot.

【1】diferentiation is any change whereby things become unlike and， in blology， refers to the process by which， in the course of development， cells be-come modified into a specific form. Differentiation occurs in an em-bryo as germinative cells evolve into tissues and organs， such as the follicular germ into a hair follicle， and in neoplasms that attempt to recapitulate events in an embryo by forming parts of tissues or organs， as is the case， for example， in trichoblastoma. Theoretically， differenti-ation of a neoplasm refers to the relative capability of neoplastic cells to form structures that resemble those in embryonic or mature tissues or organs. In practice， however， it often is difficult to identify， with cer-tainty， embryonal structures， e.g.， subtle follicular germs and papillae， whereas it is much easier to recognize more mature structures， e.g.， follicular bulbs and papillae. When no evidence of normal structures is apparent， a neoplasm is designated undifferentiated； when seemingly normal structures are apparent， a neoplasm is considered well differ-entiated， and when there are only vague hints of normal structures， a neoplasm is termed poorly differentiated.

Maturation is a kind of differentiation， namely， the specific differ-entiation of cells as they age， e.g.， a basal keratinocyte into a cor-neocvte.'|删除换行|duskeratosis refers to prerature cornification of individual cells within the viable layers of the epidermis and of epithelial structures of adnexa. Dyskeratotic cells have pyknotic nuclei and eosinophilic cytoplasm that， by electron microscopy， is seen to be packed with filaments of keratin in perinuclear aggregates. These prematurely cornified cells may be encountered in inflammatory discases like the verrucous stage of in-continentia pigmenti； in neoplastic diseases like subungual keratoacan-thomas， solar keratoses， and Bowen’s disease； in genodermatoses like Darier’s disease； and in cystic conditions like warty dyskeratoma. In all instances， dyskeratosis is an expression of premature， but slow， cell death. Rapidly dying keratinocytes do not have time to cornify and this is reflected by a normal basket-weave stratum corneum， as in erythema multiforme， fixed drug eruption， or pityriasis lichenoides acuta. Slowly dying keratinocytes cornify and therefore the stratum corneum is either parakeratotic or compactly orthokeratotic.

【3】dysplasia， in classical pathology， had a specific meaning， namely， an aber-ration that occurred in the embryologic anlage. Unfortunately， that definition has been perverted in recent years， beginning in gynecologic pathology in regard to morphologic changes in the cervix， “invading”to cutaneous pathology in the realm of reputed morphologic findings in a type of melanocytic nevus， and then “metastasizing”to pathology of all organs. In regard to melanocytic neoplasia， the term "dysplasia” has not been defined in a repeatable， reliable， and comprehensible fashion. Some pathologists use it synonymously with “melanocytic nuclear atypia，" others with "disordered hyperplasia，” and still others with “ar-chitectural and cytological atypia.” Many reflective pathologists do not use the term “dysplasia"at all because they understand that to employ it means to obfuscate rather than clarify an issue under discussion.

Because the bastardization of the word “dysplasia” has had a re-tarding influence on the study of neoplasia in the cervix， the skin， and other organs， we advise that it be eschewed. In short， there is no place in the realm of melanocytic neoplasia for the terms “dysplasia，"“dys-plastic cells，"“dysplastic nevus，" and the “dysplastic nevus syndrome.”|删除换行|elastotic material is synonymous with solar elastosis， i.e.， the basophilic spaghetti-like connective tissue produced by fibrocytes that have been exposed chronically to damaging effects of sunlight.

【5】**epidermotropism describes the movement of neoplastic cells toward and into the epidermis. Epithelial neoplasms metastatic to skin sometimes involve the epidermis， in addition to the dermis. The most common of these is melanoma. Epidermotropically metastatic melanoma may be difficult to differentiate from primary cutaneous melanoma. The stim-ulus for movemnent of cells of a melanoma into the epidermis is un-known， but it might be related to that which attracts melanoblasts to.. the epidermis in an embryo.**

【6】epithelium denotes a layer of cells that covers the surfaces of body mem-branes that line it， in which glands also may form. Epithelia are de-rived from all three germ layers， although most of them arise from ectoderm and endoderm.

Epithelia are classified on the basis of their number of layers into simple and stratified， and on the basis of cellular characteristics into squamous， cuboidal， and columnar. Simple squamous epithelium con-sists of a single laver of flat cells as are found in the air spaces of the lungs. Epithelia that line the lumina of blood vessels and body cavities are similar morphologically to simple squamous type but are classified separately as endothelium and mesothelium， respectively. Simple cu-boidal epithelium may be observed in the lining of the ovary. Simple columnar epithelium appears in portions of many ducts and glands such as apocrine glands. Specialized columnar epithelium with capa-bility to secrete mucus is characteristic for the lining of the stomach， the cervical canal of the uterus， and the conjunctiva. Pseudostratified columnar epithelium is found in the male urethra and in large excre-tory ducts of a parotid gland and consists ofa single layer of tall cells whose nuclei are situated at different levels and thus create the impres-|删除0换行|sion of being arranged in several layers. Stratified columnar epithelium may be seen in large ducts of exocrine glands. Stratified epithelium that does not cornify is typical of mucous membranes of the mouth， upper esophagus， and vagina. Stratified epithelium that cornifies， also known as epidermis， covers the surface of the skin. Transitional epithelium， seen only in the urinary bladder， is comprised of one or two layers of cells when the bladder is stretched， but numerous lavers when the bladder is ernpty and relaxed.

【8】erosion significs loss of part or all of the epidermis without loss of any dermis， in contrast to ulcer， which denotes loss of the entire epidermis and at least part of the dermis.

【9】erythroderma means red skin and refers to nearly universal redness of the skin as occurs mostly in a variety of inflammatory diseases， e.g.，psoria-sis， pityriasis rubra pilaris， atopic dermatitis， and allergic contact der-matitis， but also in a neoplastic discase， i.e.， mycosis fungoides， espe-cially in the form of Sézary's syndrome. Allergic reactions to certain drugs may be expressed as erythroderma. Seborrheic dermatitis is re-puted to eventuate in an erythroderma， but that assumption probably isuntrue. Aperson affected by an erythroderma is designated“Thomme rouge，" and an erythroderma typified by striking desquama-tion is termed an "exfoliative erythroderma."Study of histopathologic sections from a biopsy specimen of an erythroderma often enables spe-cific diagnosis to be accomplished.

【10】fibrin is a filamentous protein derived from fibrinogen by the action of thrombin during coagulation of the blood and is seen in histologic sections stained by hematoxylin and eosin as fibrillary eosinophilic material.

【11】fibrosis is formation of fibrous tissue characterized by an increase in the amount of collagen at a particular site. Fibrocytes are increased in number in the early stages of fibrosis， but they are reduced at a much later stage known as sclerosis. Fibrosis is a consequence of any patho-logical process associated with loss of parenchyma and its framework， such as occurs in long-standing inflammatory processes like caseous tuberculosis and gummatous syphilis. In general， the quantity of fibro-sis is related to the extent of damage to tissue caused by an acute inflammatory process or by a chronic one. Fibroplasia is a synonym for fibrosis. When fibroplasia occurs in response to a benign or malignant neoplasm， it is called “desmoplasia，”e.g.， desmoplastic Spitz’s nevus and desmoplastic melanoma.

【12】fibrotic tracts are linear bands of fibrosis that form at sites of permanently extinct hair follicles as a consequence of dense inflammatory-cell infil-trates.

【13】**fibrous septa are struts of bundles of collagen and fibrocytes that separate compartments， such as lobules of adipose tissue， from one another. In sections of normal subcutaneous tissue， fibrous septa are thin and out-line rectangles of fat lobules and are oriented both perpendicular and parallel to the skin surface. Fibrous septa also are known as fibrous trabeculae.**

【14】fibrous tracts are linear bands of fibrous tissue that form normally behind hair follicles that have retracted in catagen and telogen and are inde-pendent of any inflammatory cell infiltrates.

【15】foam cells are lipid-laden macrophages in which the cytoplasm contains numerous pale and clear vacuoles from which lipids had been ex-tracted during fixation in formalin and subsequent processing in alco-hols of different grades. The lipid nature of the droplets can be demon-strated in frozen sections by fat stains such as scarlet red， oil red O，or Sudan black. Foam cells are not specific for a single pathological pro-cess but predominate in lipidoses and xanthomatoses， a broad category of diseases characterized by deposits of excessive amounts of lipids in various organs of the body， including the skin. Any resolving inflamma-tory process with intense degradation of red blood cells as a conse-quence of extravasation of numerous erythrocytes， as well as inflam-matory processes that involve adipose tissue， e.g.，lupus erythematosus profundus， may be accompanied by foam cells.

【16】follicular germ， imprecisely termed “hair germ，”is a primordium of the folliculo-sebaceous-apocrine unit. It is a crescentic collection of closely crowded germinative cells at the base of an embryonic epidermis， below which are closely crowded mesenchymal cells of an embryonic follicular papilla. The basal cells of a follicular germ are columnar and are aligned in a palisade. Follicular germinative cells consist mostly of nuclei devoid of a detectable nucleolus； cytoplasm is scant.

【17】germinal centers are characteristic structures of lymph nodes which some-times occur in the skin， especially in pseudolymphomas. Germinal cen-ters consist of macrophages， immunoblasts， and small and large lym-phocytes.

【18】**grunuloma refers to a collection of histiocytes. Epithelioid histiocytes may be predominant in tuberculoid leprosy， for example， foamy histiocytes in lepromatous leprosy， and both epithelioid histiocytes and foamy his-tiocytes in dimorphous leprosy. Multinucleated histiocytes may be pres-ent， in addition to mononuclear histiocyles， in a granuloma. A granu-loma may be devoid of inflammatory cells other than histiocytes， e.g.， a naked tubercle of sarcoidosis， or it may be surrounded by a dense man-tle of\`lymphocytes as in some expressions of tuberculosis. When histio-cytes are aligned like stakes in a stockade， the arrangement is desig-nated palisaded granuloma. When an abscess is present within a collection of histiocytes， as is common in infections by atypical myco-bacteria and deep fungi， the structure is known as a suppurative granu-loma.**

【19】guttate means drop-sized and -shaped. The description usually is applied to eruptive lesions of psoriasis and to a distinctive condition termed“gut-tate parapsoriasis”that is unrelated to psoriasis but related to digitate dermatosis， another expression of so-called small plaque parapsoriasis， which seems to be one of the many morphologic expressions of mycosis fungoides.

【20】**hamartoma refers to a circumscribed lesion that has resulted from an crror in development and is characterized by an abnormal arrangement of tissues indigenous to an organ. Hamartomas are not neoplasms， be-cause the rate of their growth parallels the growth of the persons who bear them. The term “hamartoma”should not be applied to cellular proliferations that begin after tissues have reached maturity structur-ally. Congenital melanocytic nevi of the deep type should be classified as hamartomas， whereas acquired melanocytic nevi are more appro-priately classified as benigin neoplasms. This distinction is supported by clinical， histopathologic， and biologic differences between melanocytic nevi that are present at birth and those that truly arise after birth.**

【21】horn pseudocysts are whorls of delicate， laminated orthokeratotic cells that form within tunnels of infundibula， particularly as within some sebor-rheic keratoses. They are not true cysts because each connects to the skin surface through a prominent ostium and only appear to be encir-cled by epithelium because sections of them are off center.

【22】hpaline designates a substance that， when stained with hematoxylin and eosin and viewed by conventional light microscopy， has a “glassy，”homogeneous， eosinophilic appearance. For almost a century， histopa-thologists used the term“hyaline”as synonymous with a specified sub-stance considered to be diagnostic of certain diseases， c.g.， “toxic hya-line”for erythema elevatum diutinum. It now is appreciated that“toxic hyaline” is fibrin. “Hyaline globules” is a name given to degenerating erythrocytes in lysosomes of neoplastic endothelial cells of Kaposi’s sar-coma. In short， the term hyaline is not specific and is best avoided in favor of substances that are specific and definable.

【23】hyperplasia is an increase in number of normal cells in normal arrangement in a tissue. Inherent in this term in classical pathology is the concept that hyperplasia ceases when the stimulus that initiated it is removed and reverts toward its normal state. Melanocytic hyperplasia means an increase in the absolute number of normal-appearing melanocytes within the epidermis per unit area of the skin. An example would be the temporary increase in epidermal melanocytes after sunburn. Malig-nant melanoma in situ， however， is neoplasia rather than hyperplasia because the process does not ordinarily cease and reverse but continues to evolve progressively. In morphology， it is preferable to speak and write of “proliferation” of cells rather than of hyperplasia or neoplasia， because the meaning of those two terms is predicated upon identifica-tion of the stimulus responsible for them. In fact， the stimuli responsi-ble for nearly all “hyperplasias” and "neoplasias"are not known. For that reason， the term“proliferation，"which is devoid of implications of cause， is more accurate.

in situ is a term used to denote neoplasms tha For eyart are confined to their site of origin. For example， markedly atypical squamous neoplasia of the sur-face epithelium of the cervix is referred to as carcinoma in situ of the cervix. This usage presumes that， untreated， the process could even-tuate in metastatic melanoma. This prediction of biological behavior by a histopathologist is based on retrospective analysis of similar le-sions. Cells of a malignant neoplasm that are confined to epithelium|删除0换行|need not eventuate in metastases； they may remain in situ for the life of the patient and even regress. Unfortunately， a histopathologist cannot predict the behavior of those cells and， for that reason， malignancy in situ must be removed completely to ensure that it never will progress to the point that it may prove fatal. The concept of intra-cpithelial carci-noma of the skin is accepted for neoplasms with squamous differentia-tion， e.g.， Bowen’s disease， and for glandular differentiation， e.g.， ex-tramammary Paget's disease. Superficial basal-cell carcinoma is seated beneath the epidermis and therefore is not considered to be truly in situ， i.e.， intraepidermal.**

【25】**Melanoma in situ is a proliferation of atypical melanocytes， con-fined to the epidermis and epithelial structures of adnexa， that fulfills all of the intra-epithelial criteria for melanoma. Virtually all primary cutaneous melanomas begin within the epidermis， i.e.， in situ.**

【26】infundibulum refers to the upper funnel-shaped portion of a follicle that is bounded by an ostium above and the duct of a sebaceous gland below. For practical purposes， the basal， spinous， granular， and cornified lay-ers of an infundibulum are indistinguishable from those of epidermis. The infundibulum and isthmus， together， form the upper segment of a follicle.

【27】**isthmus of a follicle designates that part which is a bridge between the more prominent portions above and below it， namely， the infundibulum and the lower segment. The isthmus is bounded above by the entry into a follicle of the duct of a sebaceous gland and below by disappearance of the inner sheath at about the level of the bulge， the structure that is the site for attachment of a muscle of hair erection. The epithelium of the outer sheath at the isthmus is indistinguishable from that of the outer sheath early in catagen， both being typified by a basal layer， pale stain-ing spinous zone in which intercellular bridges are detected with diffi-culty by conventional microscopy， no granular zone， and a compactly arranged cornified layer whose surface is crenulated. The outer sheath at the isthmus and early in catagen is free to cornify unrestrained be-cause it no longer is compressed by a firm cornified inner sheath， which has disappeared at both those sites.**

【28】**lichenoid means flat-topped papules clinically and a band-like infiltrate， usually of lymphocytes， in a thickened papillary dermis histopathologi-cally. The infiltrate tends to obscure the dermo-epidermal junction， along which there generally is vacuolar alteration and episodically ne-crotic keratinocytes. It is the band-like cellular infiltrate throughout a thickened papillary dermis that conveys the appearance of papules with flat tops.**

**lobule designates a discrete unit of cells bounded by fibrous struts. Lobules in the subcutaneous fat consist of rectangles composed mostly of adi-pocytes bounded by fibrous septa (trabeculae). Lobules of eccrine and apocrine units， like lobules in mammary glands， consist of units formed by glandular and proximal ductal segments (epithelial compo-nent) and surrounding stroma rich in mucin (non-epithelial compo-nent). These epithelial and non-epithelial components form a recoginiz-able morphologic and functional unit that contrasts strikingly with|删除0换行|enveloping normal connective tissue， which is constituted mostly of bundles of collagen， but also of scant mucin. The term “lobule”is applied also to each of many similar-appearing units that comprise entire neoplasms considered to be multilobular， such as angiolipoma.**

【30】**lymphoid follicles refer to collections of mononuclear cells like those in lymph nodes and that appear in some cutaneous pseudolymphomas(iymphocytoma cutis) as well as an incidental finding in other inflam-matory processes， e.g.， responses to tick bites， and neoplastic ones.e.g. at the base of some basal-cell carcinomas. The finding of lymphoid follicles in skin is an evidence of a hypersensitivy reaction at that site.**

【31】**macule refers to a small， flat， non-palpable spot on the skin， up to 1 cm in size， of different color than that of the surrounding normal skin. A flat lesion larger than a macule is known as a patch.**

【32】**malformation denotes a structural abnormality present at birth that re-sulted from an aberration in the embryologic anlage，e.g.， an arteriove-nous shunt or a cleft lip. 【19】**QUETIAPINE**

【20】Summary of the Clinical Experience with Quetiapine

There is limited research support for the use of quetiapine in children. Que-tiapine， except for clozapine， displays the most benign EPS profile among the second-generation antipsychotics； it also has moderate weight and metabolic side effects profiles and does not increase prolactin secretion. Quetiapine is a very safe medication， although it is very sedative； due to its short half-life， it is recommended for twice a day dosing. Single night dosing is on the rise； single dosing schedule will greatly increase tolerability since BID dose titration is frequently problematic. For BID dosing， increasing experience demonstrates that assertive rapid titration creates rapid tolerance to sedative side effects. In|删除0换行|the author’s experience， if the child or adolescent reaches tolerance to 100 mg of quetiapine in the morning， without sedation， the patient will be able to tolerate any further dose increases without experiencing drowsiness. Quetiapine carries a moderate risk for obesity， diabetes， and dyslipidemias. Quetiapine appears to have favorable neurocognitive effects. Since the ratio of dose initiation to therapeutic dose is large， and there is a small available oral dosing， quetiapine can be safely prescribed to very small children in appropriate amounts. Because of its strong sedative properties at lower doses， quetiapine is commonly used as a sleeping medication.

Quetiapine was superior to haloperidol in reducing depressive symptoms. This result was a direct effect of quetiapine on depressive symptoms and was not related to quetiapine impact on positive or negative symptoms or on EPS . A report on quetiapine in bipolar depression appears below.

Cognitive deficits (in executive function， attention， and verbal memory) improved to greater extent in doses of 300 to 600 mg/day compared to haloperi-dol at 12 mg/day dose after 24 weeks of treatment . Furthermore， Velligan et al. (2002) reported cognitive improvement in patients on quetiapine 600 mg/day (p<0.02) in comparison to patients on haloperidol≤ 30 mg/day. There were specific differences in executive function (Verbal Fluency Test， p<0.04)， attention (Stroop Color Word T， p<0.03)， and verbal memory (Paragraph Recall Test， p <0.02). (However， the doses ofhaloperidol are excessive and put haloperidol in disadvantage to quetiapine). The authors stated that the group differences were not solely due to the benztropine use， medication side effects， or changes in symptomatology. The improvement in cognitive performance (attention， memory and executive function) is predictive|删除0换行|of role functioning and community outcome (including global functioning occupational functioning and social skills) in patients with schizophrenia (pp.239-240). (2005) concluded that quetiapine monotherapy has significant antidepressant efficacy in a group of patients with bipolar I and II depressive disorders. The effect size is considered low if it is less than 0.4， moderate if the effect size is 0.40 to 0.79， and large if the effect size is larger than 0.80. 【47】**ZIPRASIDONE**

【48】Summary of Clinical Experience with Ziprasidone

A pharmaceutical competitor of ziprasidone created an aura of apprehension about this medications cardiological side effects long before this medication had obtained FDA approval. The orchestrated campaign against this product was very successful in creating physicians'apprehension about ziprasidone. These fears are unjustified； the alarming purported side effects of ziprasidone never materialized， and were dispelled by the Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness (CATIE I) trial . Ziprasidone is an eminently safe and effective second-generation antipsychotic in adults. There is limited literature to substantiate safety and effectiveness in childhood. So far， ziprasidone has not been associated with|删除0换行|torsades des pointes (TdP)， and has demonstrated no lethality in overdose .

【50】Its weight neutrality， its favorable metabolic side effects and prolactin profiles， render ziprasidone an attractive therapeutic option. Ziprasidone is an optimal antipsychotic medication for overweight and obese children and adolescents. Ziprasidone also appears to have significant antidepressive effects and a favorable neurocognitive effect. A minor disadvantage is that it is a twice a day medication， and that it requires food in the stomach for optimal absorption. There is an ongoing empirical experimentation with single nightly dosing.

【47】**ZIPRASIDONE**

【48】Summary of Clinical Experience with Ziprasidone

A pharmaceutical competitor of ziprasidone created an aura of apprehension about this medications cardiological side effects long before this medication had obtained FDA approval. The orchestrated campaign against this product was very successful in creating physicians'apprehension about ziprasidone. These fears are unjustified； the alarming purported side effects of ziprasidone never materialized， and were dispelled by the Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness (CATIE I) trial . Ziprasidone is an eminently safe and effective second-generation antipsychotic in adults. There is limited literature to substantiate safety and effectiveness in childhood. So far， ziprasidone has not been associated with|删除0换行|torsades des pointes (TdP)， and has demonstrated no lethality in overdose .

【50】Its weight neutrality， its favorable metabolic side effects and prolactin profiles， render ziprasidone an attractive therapeutic option. Ziprasidone is an optimal antipsychotic medication for overweight and obese children and adolescents. Ziprasidone also appears to have significant antidepressive effects and a favorable neurocognitive effect. A minor disadvantage is that it is a twice a day medication， and that it requires food in the stomach for optimal absorption. There is an ongoing empirical experimentation with single nightly dosing.

【38】**·Brainstem auditory-evoked potentials test acoustic conduction through the ear， the eighth cranial nerve， into the lower pons， and continuing rostrally in the lateral lemniscus up the brainstem.**

【55】**Visual-evoked potentials (VEPs)**

【56】**·The visual-evoked potential (VEP) is the potential recorded from the occipital region in response to visual stimuli. It differs from other evoked responses in that the response is long-latency，while it is short-latency in others. VEP is also the only evoked response that is visible without averaging.**

【61】**· Inspection of normal VEP reveals three identifiable waveforms： N75， P100， and N145. P100 is a positive potential at about 100 ms (the normal limit is up to 117 ms)， and is the only one used for VEP interpretation.**

【62】**· An intact VEP usually suggests continuity of the visual pathways， but it does not fully exclude cortical blindness.**

【20】**Most of the standard neuropsychological tests used in assessing dementia were developed many years ago and not specifically designed for the investi-gation of patients with AD， but often for younger patients suffering from traumatic brain injury or temporal lobe epilepsy. For example， the CERAD-NAB was developed more than 25 years ago and the construction of the CERAD-NAB reflects the knowledge about hippocampal memory dysfunc-tions dominating the scientific discussion during that time. In the following， three additional aspects of memory impairment will be discussed that are not part of routine CERAD-NAB testing： the serial position effect of wordlist learning， the difference between recollection and familiarity and their role in recognition memory， and the meaning of relational learning for differential diagnosis.**

【21】**The word list serial position effect means that the first and the last words of a word list have a much higher chance of being reproduced during learn-ing than words stemming from the middle part of the list. One explanation of this effect is that the first words of the list are transferred into to long-term memory， whereas the last words are remembered by working memory. This explanation has been criticized， however， because a specific strategy might play a role for the phenomenon： participants might be inclined to rehearse the first words during word list learning and rehearsing might be the reason why these words are remembered better. Although this distinction is important from a cognitive neuropsychological view， if the measurement of long-term consolidation is the relevant task， it is irrelevant how long-term consolidation is achieved.**

Several studies have shown that AD and amnestic MCI patients suffer from a reduced primacy effect (remembering less words from the beginning of a word list) and an increased recency effect (remembering more words from the end of the word list). For a short review， consult the introduction|删除0换行|section of Cunha， Guerreiro， de Mendonca， Oliveira， and Santana (2012). Moreover， AD patients are less able to remember words especially from the last part of a word list during free delayed recall， arguing that in AD patients these words are less likely to be transferred in long-term memory (as pre-dicted for an amnestic syndrome of the hippocampal type).**

【23】**Some studies also show that the primacy and the recency effect might be helpful for the differential diagnosis. In an early study Capitani， Della Sala， Logie， and Spinnler (1992) documented differences between AD patients and patients with frontal lesions based on an evaluation of the recency part of the word list. Orru et al. (2009) compared clinical diagnosed AD patients with patients with mixed dementia and those with vascular dementia. Although the three groups did not differ in learning and delayed recall， AD patients and those with mixed dementia exhibited a relatively increased recency to primacy proportion， whereas patients with only vascular dementia showed an increased primacy to recency proportion. This result suggests that patients with AD pathology suffer from long-term consolidation and use their work-ing memory capacities to replicate wordlists， whereas vascular patients suffer from working memory impairments and use their remaining long-term mem-ory process for the reproduction of the list.**

【24】**Bayley et al. (2000) compared AD patients with different degrees of disease progression with patients suffering from an electroconvulsive amnesia. AD patients showed a reduced primacy portion compared with their recency portion， whereas thepatients with electroconvulsive therapy displayed a balanced recency and primacy ratio. Foldi， Brickman， Schaefer， and Knutelska (2003) also showed that AD patients， compared with those with late life depres-sion， are characterized by a larger recency effect. In a recent study， Busse et al.(2017)compared AD patients with patients suffering from Lewy body disease with neuropsychological tests and wordlist learning. Patients with Lewy body disease were impaired in visuoperception and visuocon-struction (compare Section 3.5 on visual impairments in this patient group)， whereas AD patients exhibited fast forgetting of words after dis-traction. Concerning the recency and primacy proportion， both patients groups showed a low primacy proportion， however， patients with Lewy body dementia also showed a decrease in the recency part of the wordlist. Busse et al. (2017) argue that the reduction of the recency proportion may be caused by a working memory deficit in the Lewy body disease patients. They base this argument on the correlation of recency proportion and performance in the digit span task.**

The patient is evaluated with a urinalysis. Urinalysis includes a microscopic evaluation of clean-catch urine for bacteria and pyuria (pus in the urine). Pyuria and colony counts greater than 100，000 bacteria/mL of urine are found in most infected patients. In symptomatic patients pyuria and colony counts of100 to 100，000 bacteria/mL establish infection， most often lower UTI. The urine is cultured ifbacte-ria are found. Generally， the isolation of two or more bacterial species on culture indicates a contarninated|删除0换行|specimen. Patients with pyuria without bacteriuria may have chlamydial urethritis， gonococcal ure-thritis， or gram-positive cocci infection. Gross hematuria strongly suggests cystitis. Men with urethritis and purulent discharge often have Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection； men with a whitish mucoid dis-charge have a nonspecific infection. Yeast infections are most common in diabetics and patients who have had a course of antibiotic treatment. For urethritis in females， see Chapter 56.

【2】Management

【3】For a conventional UTI， antibiotic treatment with amoxicillin/clavulanate， a cephalosporin， a fluo-roquinotone， nitrofurantoin， or trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is prescribed. For pylonephritis， more aggressive therapy including hospitalization with intravenous antibiotics is often recommended. Asymptomatic infections should be treated if there is underlying vesicoureteral reflux， stone， dia-betes， or pregnancy or if the patient is an immunosuppressed individual. Prevention may be possible with changes in pH through the use of cranberry juice.

【4】**Benign Prostate Hypertrophy**

【5】Classic Presentation

【6】A male patient presents with complaints of decreased force of urine stream， hesitancy， dribbling， and a sense of incomplete bladder emptying.

【7】Cause/Occurrence

【8】There is a direct relationship between age and benign prostate hypertrophy (BPH). There is histo-logic evidence of BPH in 50% of men at age 60， which increases to 90% by age 80.12 The relation-ship between glandular enlargement and symptoms is not always present. Symptonis of BPH are usually due to a combination of causes including： (1) enlargement of glandular nodules causing ure-thral blockage (androgens are prinary cause)， (2) smooth muscle tone of the posterior capsule and blad-der neck (o-1-adrenergicstimulation)， and (3) impaired bladder contractility and destrusor instability(involuntary“spasms"of the bladder). Although BPH increases with age， the symptoms do not nec-essarily follow this pattern.

【9】Evaluation

【10】A. digital prostate examination is required. In an effort to rule out other causes of symptoms or com-plications of BPH， a urinalysis for bladder cancer and UTI involvement (hematuria requires an im-mediate urologic referral). Yearly serum creatinine measurement is recommended to screen for possible involvement of the upper urinary tract.

【11】Management

【12】Patients with mild symptoms may be managed with watchful waiting with recommendations of de-creasing sympathetic stimulation (i.e.， decreasing stress， decreased caffeine， etc.) and phytotherapy. Men who smoke more than 35 cigarettes/day and have high alcohol intake are at higher risk. 13 Men who are more physically active have a lower frequency of symptoms.+ Those with more disruptive symptoms or risk ofupper urinary tract involvement may need medical or surgical treatment.

【13】Prostate growth is governed by hormonal influences. Testosterone is converted to 5-alpha-dihydrotestosterone (DHT) in the prostate. This is accomplished through an enzyme 5-a-reductase. The medical approach to reducing DHT is to block the conversion of testosterone to DHTthrough the use of 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors (e.g.， finasteride \[Proscar\]). In this way the levels of testosterone are not affected. o-1-adrenergic blocking agents such as terazosin (Hytrin) and doxazosin (Cardura) _16\._ are often prescribed to reduce smooth muscle tone.

【14】These medical options are being used more frequently in place of transurethral resection of the prostate(TURP)， Other surgical options include open prostatectomy， balloon dilation， stents， and newer tech-niques including laser ablation and microwave hyperthermia. Surgery should be reserved for those who do not respond to conservative or medical management or those with serious complications.

【15】Phytotherapeutic agents such as saw palretto are suggested as alternative treatment options. It is postulated that saw palmetto reduces ievels of DHT. A recommended dose is 320 mg of standardized extract per day. Symptons may improve within 1 month.

【16】**Prostate Cancer**

【17】Classic Presentation

【18】A male patient is usually asymptomatic in the early stages. Later local growth may cause the patient to present with complaints of decreased force of urine stream， hesitancy， dribbling， and a sense ofin-complete bladder emptying. Later presentations with metastasis may include back or pelvic pain.

【19】Cause/Occurrence

【20】There is a higher incidence of prostate cancer in black males in the United States and lower rates for Asian males while in Asia. Rates increase for Asian males when they immigrate to the United States， indicating an environmental influence. The development of prostate cancer is related to an interac-tion of genetic predisposition， dietary factors， and lifestyle. Two genes，RNASEL and MSRl， may in-creasc the risk of prostate cancer in relation to infection.It is now believed that prostatic inflammation， either septic (as in sexually transmitted infection) or aseptic， may progress to pro iferative inflamma-tory atrophy. Loss of n-class glutathione-S-transferace (GSTP1) enzyme caretaker function then al-lows the developtnent of cells of prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia and prostate cancer cells. The findings from one large study indicate that approximnately 42 % of cases of prostate cancer are related to inheritance， with the remainder most likely due to environmental factors.7 Possible dietary rela-tionships inc.ude：

【21】A diet high in animal fats and meats may increase the risk of prostate cancer (especially meats cooked at high temperature or grilled/broiled， which form heterocyclic aromnatic amine and poly-cyclic atomatic hydrocarbon carcinogens).I8

【22】品Low vegetable intake： High intake of the antioxidant carotenoid Iveopene， found in tomatoes， may be assnciated with a reduced risk of nrostate cancer.19 Also， high intake of cruciferous ver-etables containing isothiocynate sulforaphane may reduce risk of prostate cancer.删除14:<u>0</u>

【25】Adenocarcinoma of the prostate is only second to lung cancer as a cause of cancer-related death ini men. Incidence increases with age so that by age 65 and older， 75% have some prostate cancer.2Most prostate cancers do not progress to metastasis and death. However， those with local disease and high tumor grade tend to progress. 【26】Evaluation

【27】For those at high risk (familial predisposition or African Americans)， an annual DRE and PSA screen should begin at age 40.26 For men not at high risk， annual screening with DRE and PSA should be-gin at age 50.26 PSA values in the 4 to 10 ng/mL range have a 25% positive predictive value. PSA val-ues higher than 10 ng/mL. have a 67% positive predictive value. Also， the measurement of free and tota. PSA may help. The proportion of free-to-total PSA is higher for men with BPH and lower in men with prostate cancer. Other available testing includes PSA density， PSA velocity， and PSAage-specific ranges， aithough their value has not been established. An elevated PSA and an abnormal DRE will usually result in transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy. Four to six samples are of-ten recommended to increase the yield. The grading systei for prostate cancer is the Gleason sys-ten. This is divided into five grades based on degree of differentiation.

【29】Patients who are aver 70 years oid or have less than 10 years’ life expectancy are usually not treated. Options for those in need of treatment include radical prostatectomy， radiation therapy， or hormonal therapy. As noted above， patients who smoke and have a high calcium intake are at higher risk for fa-tal cancer. 【63】**CONTEXT**

【64】Nocturnal enuresis is a distressing disorder for parents and children. Approximately 5 to 7 million children in the United States are affected. It is more common in boys than in girls. Girls are more likely to have daytime inconti-nence， mnore often associated with bacteriuria. In a large study in Sweden， 2.9% of girls and 3.8% of boy school en-trants reported bed-wetting once per week.删除14:<u>1</u>

【65】Parents are often unaware of the natural history of continence development and expect their child to be con-tinent at a relatively early age. One study indicated that between 30% and 70% of parents punish their children for bed-wetting. Ironically， there is a strong genetic com-ponent. Children whose parents both have a history of enuresis as a child have a 77% chance of bed-wetting，44% chance if only one parent has a positive history， and only 15% chance if neither did.

【66】Parents seeking a nondrug， nonparent-intensive ap-proach to bed-wetting seek a chiropractor's advice. The chiropractor may perform the initial evaluation to deter-mine known causes such as urinary tract infection or di-abetes. The nonpathologic， neurodevelopmen tal type of enuresis may be managed with conservative approaches. When these fail， referral for medication may be warranted.

【67】Enuresis has been defined by the American Psychiatric Association as bed-wetting occurring in a child at age5 years or above (and mental age of 4 years). The fre-quency is defined as two or more incontinent occurrences in a month between the ages of 5 and 6 or one or more occurrences after age 6 in children who do not have an as-sociated physical disorder such as urinary tract infection(UTI)， diabetes， or seizures. At age 5 approximately 20%of children have enuresis， which decreases to 10% atage10 and 1% at age 15.5.6

Enuresis is often categorized into primary and sec-ondary causes. Primary causes include both functional and structural causes. Secondary enuresis is defined as|删除0换行|the presence of a prior history of continence for more than a 6-month period. These patients often have a re-gression due to a stressful emotional event in the early years of life. Approximately 80% to 90% of childhood enuresis is the primary type.删除14:<u>78</u>

【69】When not due to a structural cause， enuresis seems to follow a natural spontaneous remission. This natural his-tory must be taken into account when it appears that a child is responding to a specific therapy. Wichout any Oas specific therapy the natural history indicates that 50% _SF_ of patients will become continent within 4 years. The prevalence of enuresis decreases with age at a rate of 10%to 20% per year after age 6.9

【78】Evaluate the neurologic status of the child with em-phasis on peripheral sensation and reflexes， genital sensation and perianal reflexes， and a search for any indications of congerital abnormalities such as club-toot，spina bifida， or other.

The patient is evaluated with a urinalysis. Urinalysis includes a microscopic evaluation of clean-catch urine for bacteria and pyuria (pus in the urine). Pyuria and colony counts greater than 100，000 bacteria/mL of urine are found in most infected patients. In symptomatic patients pyuria and colony counts of100 to 100，000 bacteria/mL establish infection， most often lower UTI. The urine is cultured ifbacte-ria are found. Generally， the isolation of two or more bacterial species on culture indicates a contarninated|删除0换行|specimen. Patients with pyuria without bacteriuria may have chlamydial urethritis， gonococcal ure-thritis， or gram-positive cocci infection. Gross hematuria strongly suggests cystitis. Men with urethritis and purulent discharge often have Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection； men with a whitish mucoid dis-charge have a nonspecific infection. Yeast infections are most common in diabetics and patients who have had a course of antibiotic treatment. For urethritis in females， see Chapter 56.

【2】Management

【3】For a conventional UTI， antibiotic treatment with amoxicillin/clavulanate， a cephalosporin， a fluo-roquinotone， nitrofurantoin， or trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is prescribed. For pylonephritis， more aggressive therapy including hospitalization with intravenous antibiotics is often recommended. Asymptomatic infections should be treated if there is underlying vesicoureteral reflux， stone， dia-betes， or pregnancy or if the patient is an immunosuppressed individual. Prevention may be possible with changes in pH through the use of cranberry juice.

【4】**Benign Prostate Hypertrophy**

【5】Classic Presentation

【6】A male patient presents with complaints of decreased force of urine stream， hesitancy， dribbling， and a sense of incomplete bladder emptying.

【7】Cause/Occurrence

【8】There is a direct relationship between age and benign prostate hypertrophy (BPH). There is histo-logic evidence of BPH in 50% of men at age 60， which increases to 90% by age 80.12 The relation-ship between glandular enlargement and symptoms is not always present. Symptonis of BPH are usually due to a combination of causes including： (1) enlargement of glandular nodules causing ure-thral blockage (androgens are prinary cause)， (2) smooth muscle tone of the posterior capsule and blad-der neck (o-1-adrenergicstimulation)， and (3) impaired bladder contractility and destrusor instability(involuntary“spasms"of the bladder). Although BPH increases with age， the symptoms do not nec-essarily follow this pattern.

【9】Evaluation

【10】A. digital prostate examination is required. In an effort to rule out other causes of symptoms or com-plications of BPH， a urinalysis for bladder cancer and UTI involvement (hematuria requires an im-mediate urologic referral). Yearly serum creatinine measurement is recommended to screen for possible involvement of the upper urinary tract.

【11】Management

【12】Patients with mild symptoms may be managed with watchful waiting with recommendations of de-creasing sympathetic stimulation (i.e.， decreasing stress， decreased caffeine， etc.) and phytotherapy. Men who smoke more than 35 cigarettes/day and have high alcohol intake are at higher risk. 13 Men who are more physically active have a lower frequency of symptoms.+ Those with more disruptive symptoms or risk ofupper urinary tract involvement may need medical or surgical treatment.

【13】Prostate growth is governed by hormonal influences. Testosterone is converted to 5-alpha-dihydrotestosterone (DHT) in the prostate. This is accomplished through an enzyme 5-a-reductase. The medical approach to reducing DHT is to block the conversion of testosterone to DHTthrough the use of 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors (e.g.， finasteride \[Proscar\]). In this way the levels of testosterone are not affected. o-1-adrenergic blocking agents such as terazosin (Hytrin) and doxazosin (Cardura) _16\._ are often prescribed to reduce smooth muscle tone.

【14】These medical options are being used more frequently in place of transurethral resection of the prostate(TURP)， Other surgical options include open prostatectomy， balloon dilation， stents， and newer tech-niques including laser ablation and microwave hyperthermia. Surgery should be reserved for those who do not respond to conservative or medical management or those with serious complications.

【15】Phytotherapeutic agents such as saw palretto are suggested as alternative treatment options. It is postulated that saw palmetto reduces ievels of DHT. A recommended dose is 320 mg of standardized extract per day. Symptons may improve within 1 month.

【17】Classic Presentation

【18】A male patient is usually asymptomatic in the early stages. Later local growth may cause the patient to present with complaints of decreased force of urine stream， hesitancy， dribbling， and a sense ofin-complete bladder emptying. Later presentations with metastasis may include back or pelvic pain.

【19】Cause/Occurrence

【20】There is a higher incidence of prostate cancer in black males in the United States and lower rates for Asian males while in Asia. Rates increase for Asian males when they immigrate to the United States， indicating an environmental influence. The development of prostate cancer is related to an interac-tion of genetic predisposition， dietary factors， and lifestyle. Two genes，RNASEL and MSRl， may in-creasc the risk of prostate cancer in relation to infection.It is now believed that prostatic inflammation， either septic (as in sexually transmitted infection) or aseptic， may progress to pro iferative inflamma-tory atrophy. Loss of n-class glutathione-S-transferace (GSTP1) enzyme caretaker function then al-lows the developtnent of cells of prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia and prostate cancer cells. 【25】Adenocarcinoma of the prostate is only second to lung cancer as a cause of cancer-related death ini men. Incidence increases with age so that by age 65 and older， 75% have some prostate cancer.2Most prostate cancers do not progress to metastasis and death. However， those with local disease and high tumor grade tend to progress. Although the incidence does not increase， the risk of fatal prostatc cancer inereases with smoking， tallness， high calcium intake， and is inversely related to physical activity.删除14:<u>23--25</u>

【26】Evaluation

【27】For those at high risk (familial predisposition or African Americans)， an annual DRE and PSA screen should begin at age 40.26 For men not at high risk， annual screening with DRE and PSA should be-gin at age 50.26 PSA values in the 4 to 10 ng/mL range have a 25% positive predictive value. PSA val-ues higher than 10 ng/mL. have a 67% positive predictive value. Also， the measurement of free and tota. PSA may help. The proportion of free-to-total PSA is higher for men with BPH and lower in men with prostate cancer. Other available testing includes PSA density， PSA velocity， and PSAage-specific ranges， aithough their value has not been established. An elevated PSA and an abnormal DRE will usually result in transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy. Four to six samples are of-ten recommended to increase the yield. The grading systei for prostate cancer is the Gleason sys-ten. This is divided into five grades based on degree of differentiation.

【29】Patients who are aver 70 years oid or have less than 10 years’ life expectancy are usually not treated. Options for those in need of treatment include radical prostatectomy， radiation therapy， or hormonal therapy. As noted above， patients who smoke and have a high calcium intake are at higher risk for fa-tal cancer. Those who are more physically active， have a high fruit intake， and supplement their diet with zine and vitamins C and E may have a ower risk for fatal prostate cancer.删除14:<u>27.28</u>

【64】Nocturnal enuresis is a distressing disorder for parents and children. Approximately 5 to 7 million children in the United States are affected. It is more common in boys than in girls. Girls are more likely to have daytime inconti-nence， mnore often associated with bacteriuria. 【65】Parents are often unaware of the natural history of continence development and expect their child to be con-tinent at a relatively early age. One study indicated that between 30% and 70% of parents punish their children for bed-wetting. Ironically， there is a strong genetic com-ponent. Children whose parents both have a history of enuresis as a child have a 77% chance of bed-wetting，44% chance if only one parent has a positive history， and only 15% chance if neither did.

【66】Parents seeking a nondrug， nonparent-intensive ap-proach to bed-wetting seek a chiropractor's advice. The chiropractor may perform the initial evaluation to deter-mine known causes such as urinary tract infection or di-abetes. The nonpathologic， neurodevelopmen tal type of enuresis may be managed with conservative approaches. When these fail， referral for medication may be warranted.

【67】Enuresis has been defined by the American Psychiatric Association as bed-wetting occurring in a child at age5 years or above (and mental age of 4 years). The fre-quency is defined as two or more incontinent occurrences in a month between the ages of 5 and 6 or one or more occurrences after age 6 in children who do not have an as-sociated physical disorder such as urinary tract infection(UTI)， diabetes， or seizures. At age 5 approximately 20%of children have enuresis， which decreases to 10% atage10 and 1% at age 15.5.6

Secondary enuresis is defined as|删除0换行|the presence of a prior history of continence for more than a 6-month period. These patients often have a re-gression due to a stressful emotional event in the early years of life. Approximately 80% to 90% of childhood enuresis is the primary type.删除14:<u>78</u>

This natural his-tory must be taken into account when it appears that a child is responding to a specific therapy. Wichout any Oas specific therapy the natural history indicates that 50% _SF_ of patients will become continent within 4 years. The prevalence of enuresis decreases with age at a rate of 10%to 20% per year after age 6.9

【72】Determine whether the patient fits the criteria for nocturnal enuresis.

【74】Determine the family history of enuresis.

【75】Determine the environmental and social history of the child with regard to changes in living environ-ment， stresses， any psychologic problems， and parental punishment for enuresis.

【78】Evaluate the neurologic status of the child with em-phasis on peripheral sensation and reflexes， genital sensation and perianal reflexes， and a search for any indications of congerital abnormalities such as club-toot，spina bifida， or other.

Unless a clinician is a neurologist， he or she is not going to perform a thorough neurologic examination during the routine physical examination unless the patient's complaints are definitely neurological. Here is an abbre-viated examination that may be useful if there is simply no time to do a thorough examination：

· Check coordination by having the patient pat the physician's hand with each of his or her hands and feet|删除0换行|in rapid succession. Have the patient stand with his or her feet together and close his or her eyes. Check the patient's gait.
